definition_zh: 修正；修订；修正案；（法律文件的）更改；（土壤）改良剂；改过自新
definition_en: a change made to correct or improve something, especially a formal change to a law or document, or the act of removing faults from something
core_image: 把条文里那处缺陷挖掉、补正，让文本重新站直
scene: 议事厅里，一名议员把一张纸推到桌子中央，提议把「十八岁投票」写进宪法。 In the chamber, a member pushes a sheet of paper to the centre of the table and proposes an amendment that would let eighteen-year-olds vote.
sceneCN: 这里 amendment 是「宪法修正案」（第 2 个义项：对宪法或法律的正式修改）；句意：议事厅里，一名议员把纸推到桌子中央，提出一项允许十八岁者投票的宪法修正案。场景要点：议事厅的长桌、推到中央的纸页、纸上的编号、议员举起的手。

pos.zh: 修正；修订；修正案；（土壤）改良剂；改过自新

senses.title: Making something better by removing faults
senses.definition: the act of correcting or improving something that is faulty or imperfect
senses.definitionCN: 纠正或改进有缺陷、不完美之事的行为
senses.example: The amendment of the manuscript took longer than writing it.
senses.exampleCN: 修订这份手稿花的时间比写它还长。
senses.why: The earliest sense, recorded in the early 13th century, is simply 'betterment, improvement'. Latin emendare is ex- 'out' plus menda 'fault', so making better begins with taking a fault out, not with putting something in.
senses.whyCN: 最早义项记录于 13 世纪早期，就是“改善、变好”。拉丁语 emendare 是 ex-“出”加 menda“缺陷”，所以“变好”的起点是把缺陷拿出去，而不是把东西放进去。

senses.title: A formal change to a constitution or law
senses.titleCN: 对宪法或法律的正式修改
senses.definition: an official change to a constitution, statute, or legal instrument, made according to established procedure
senses.definitionCN: 依照既定程序对宪法、成文法或法律文书作出的正式更改
senses.example: The First Amendment protects freedom of speech and of the press.
senses.exampleCN: 第一修正案保护言论与出版自由。
senses.why: A constitution is treated as a text with possible faults or gaps. Once the correction must pass a fixed procedure, the act of removing the fault becomes a numbered public document called an amendment.
senses.whyCN: 宪法被当作一份可能有缺陷或空白的文本。当纠正必须经过固定程序时，“去掉缺陷”的行为就变成一份编号的公开文件，称为 amendment。

senses.title: A proposed change to a bill
senses.definition: a change proposed to a bill during debate, by a member or a committee, before it becomes law
senses.definitionCN: 法案在辩论期间由议员或委员会提出、在其成为法律之前的更改
senses.example: The committee tabled an amendment to cut the proposed budget.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会提出一项修正案，要求削减拟议预算。
senses.why: Here the fault is not yet in a finished law but in a draft. The amendment is the correction offered while the text is still open, which is why it is often a proposal rather than a settled change.
senses.whyCN: 这里的缺陷还不在已生效的法律里，而在草案里。修正案是在文本仍然敞开时提出的纠正，因此它往往是一项提案，而不是已经落定的更改。

senses.title: Correction of an error in legal process
senses.titleCN: 对法律程序错误的更正
senses.definition: in law, the correction of an error in a writ, pleading, or court process
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上，对令状、诉状或法院程序中的错误进行更正
senses.example: The court allowed an amendment of the writ to correct the defendant's name.
senses.exampleCN: 法院允许修改令状，以更正被告的姓名。
senses.why: The sense 'correction of error in a legal process' is recorded about 1600, and 'alteration of a writ or bill to remove its faults' in the 1690s. The fault is now procedural, and the amendment is the official act that removes it.
senses.whyCN: “更正法律程序中的错误”这一义项约记录于 1600 年，而“更改令状或法案以去掉其缺陷”记录于 17 世纪 90 年代。这里的缺陷是程序性的，修正就是去掉它的正式行为。

senses.title: A change to a contract or agreement
senses.definition: a formal change to the terms of a contract, lease, or agreement, usually signed by all parties
senses.definitionCN: 对合同、租约或协议条款的正式更改，通常由各方签署
senses.example: Both parties signed an amendment extending the lease by two years.
senses.exampleCN: 双方签署了一份修正协议，把租期延长两年。
senses.why: A contract is a text whose terms must fit reality. When reality changes, the mismatch is treated as a fault in the document, and the amendment restores the fit.
senses.whyCN: 合同是一份条款必须贴合现实的文本。现实一变，不匹配就被当作文件里的缺陷，而 amendment 恢复这种贴合。

senses.title: A textual revision before publication
senses.definition: a correction or revision made to a scholarly, technical, or literary text
senses.definitionCN: 对学术、技术或文学文本所作的更正或修订
senses.example: The journal asked for several amendments before accepting the paper.
senses.exampleCN: 期刊在接受论文之前要求作几处修订。
senses.why: This is the domain where the old 'remove the fault' sense survives most purely. The sibling verb emend and the noun emendation are reserved for exactly this textual work, while amendment has spread to law and institutions.
senses.whyCN: 这是“去掉缺陷”这一古老义项保留得最纯粹的领域。同源的动词 emend 与名词 emendation 专门用于这种文本工作，而 amendment 则扩展到了法律与制度。

senses.title: Material added to improve soil
senses.definition: a substance such as compost, lime, or gypsum added to soil to improve its condition for growing plants
senses.definitionCN: 为改善土壤种植条件而加入土壤的物质，如堆肥、石灰或石膏
senses.example: Compost is a common soil amendment in organic farming.
senses.exampleCN: 堆肥是有机农业中常见的土壤改良剂。
senses.why: This looks like the 'adding' sense, but the name comes from the purpose, not the motion: the material is called an amendment because it amends the soil, that is, removes its defects. The addition is only the means.
senses.whyCN: 这看起来像“添加”义，但名称来自目的而非动作：这种材料被称为 amendment，是因为它改良土壤，也就是去掉土壤的缺陷。添加只是手段。

senses.title: Reformation of a person's conduct
senses.definition: the correction or improvement of a person's behaviour or character, an older sense recorded around 1300
senses.definitionCN: 对一个人的行为或品性的纠正与改善，这一较古老的义项约记录于 1300 年
senses.example: The programme was designed for the amendment of young offenders.
senses.exampleCN: 该项目是为改造年轻罪犯而设计的。
senses.why: Around 1300 the word was applied to persons as well as things: a person could be 'corrected, reformed'. The fault is now a habit or a character trait, and removing it is moral improvement.
senses.whyCN: 约 1300 年时，这个词也用于人而不只是物：人可以“被纠正、被改造”。这里的缺陷是习惯或品性，去掉它就是道德上的改善。

senses.title: An addition wearing the name of correction
senses.titleCN: 顶着“修正”之名的追加条款
senses.definition: in modern legislative usage, a provision attached to a law or bill that is formally an amendment even when it adds new material rather than repairing a fault
senses.definitionCN: 在现代立法用法中，附加到法律或法案上的条款；即使它增加新内容而非修复缺陷，形式上仍叫 amendment
senses.example: The bill was loaded with amendments that had little to do with correcting anything.
senses.exampleCN: 这项法案被塞进了许多与纠正错误几乎无关的修正条款。
senses.why: The meaning 'to add to legislation, ostensibly to correct or improve it' is recorded from 1777. The word's form still says 'remove the fault', but practice can turn it into an addition, which is exactly where learners misread amendment as 'extra clause'.
senses.whyCN: “为立法增加内容、名义上是纠正或改进它”这一用法记录于 1777 年。词形仍在说“去掉缺陷”，但实践可以把它变成追加，这正是学习者把 amendment 误读为“额外条款”的地方。

intro.en: Amendment is amend plus -ment, and amend comes from Old French amender, from Latin emendare 'to correct, free from fault'. The Latin verb is ex- 'out' + menda 'fault, blemish', so the core is removal of a defect, not addition. The same Latin source gives emend and emendation, but those stay in the domain of textual correction, while amendment spread to law, contracts and even soil.
intro.cn: amendment 是 amend 加 -ment；amend 来自古法语 amender，再上溯拉丁语 emendare“纠正、去掉缺陷”。这个拉丁动词是 ex-“出”加 menda“缺陷、瑕疵”，所以核心是“去掉缺陷”，不是“添加”。同一拉丁来源还给出 emend 与 emendation，但这两个词留在文本校勘领域，而 amendment 扩展到了法律、合同甚至土壤。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'betterment, improvement'. By c.1300 it is also used of persons, meaning 'correction, reformation'. The starting point is not an added clause but a thing made better.
items.cn: 英语最早记录为“改善、变好”。到 1300 年左右也用于人，意为“纠正、改造”。起点不是追加条款，而是使某物变好。

items.en: From Old French amendement 'rectification, correction; advancement, improvement', from amender 'to amend' (12c.), which could mean 'correct, set right, make better, improve'.
items.cn: 来自古法语 amendement“纠正、改正；促进、改善”，出自 amender“修正”（12 世纪），意为“纠正、摆正、使更好、改进”。

items.en: Amender goes back to Latin emendare 'to correct, free from fault', built from ex 'out' + menda, mendum 'fault, physical blemish; error'. The prepositional image is pulling the fault out of the thing.
items.cn: amender 上溯拉丁语 emendare“纠正、去掉缺陷”，由 ex“出”加 menda、mendum“缺陷、身体瑕疵；错误”构成。其介词意象是把缺陷从东西里拉出来。

items.en: Standard references trace menda to PIE *mend- 'physical defect, fault', said to be the source also of Sanskrit minda 'physical blemish', Old Irish mennar 'stain', Welsh mann 'sign, mark', and Hittite mant- 'something harming'. The set is well attested, though the exact reconstruction is not beyond dispute.
items.cn: 通行词源资料把 menda 追溯到原始印欧语 *mend-“身体缺陷、过错”，并称它也是梵语 minda“身体瑕疵”、古爱尔兰语 mennar“污点”、威尔士语 mann“记号”与赫梯语 mant-“有害之物”的来源。这组对应有充分记录，但具体构拟并非毫无争议。

items.en: The spelling with a- is unusual but early, and also appears in Provençal and Italian. In English, the senses 'repair; cure' were largely taken over by the shortened offspring mend, formed by dropping the initial a-. That is why amendment now sounds institutional while mend sounds manual.
items.cn: 带 a- 的拼写不寻常但出现很早，也见于普罗旺斯语和意大利语。在英语里，“修理；治愈”这些义项大多被缩短形式 mend 接管——它去掉了开头的 a-。因此 amendment 现在听起来偏制度，而 mend 听起来偏手工。

items.en: The legal sense 'correction of error in a legal process' is c.1600, and 'alteration of a writ or bill to remove its faults' is the 1690s. The meaning 'to add to legislation, ostensibly to correct or improve it' is recorded from 1777, which marks the drift toward 'added clause'. Modern soil amendment is named for the improvement it brings, not for the act of adding.
items.cn: 法律义“更正法律程序中的错误”约在 1600 年，“更改令状或法案以去掉缺陷”在 17 世纪 90 年代。“为立法增加内容、名义上纠正或改进它”的用法记录于 1777 年，这标志着向“追加条款”的漂移。现代 soil amendment 是因它带来的改良而得名，而不是因“添加”这个动作。

note.en: The first group separates amendment from the verb it comes from, the plural noun amends, and the scholarly sibling emend; the second compares words that also name changes but do not share the 'remove a fault' core.
note.cn: 第一组把 amendment 与它的源动词、复数名词 amends、以及学术领域的同源词 emend 分开；第二组比较同样表示“改动”、却不含“去掉缺陷”核心的词。

entries.definition: to correct or improve a text, law, or situation. It is the verb behind amendment; the noun names the act or the resulting document.
entries.definitionCN: 纠正或改进文本、法律或状况。它是 amendment 背后的动词；名词指行为或由此产生的文件。

entries.definition: in the phrase make amends, compensation for a wrong done. It looks like the plural of amend but functions as a fixed noun meaning reparation.
entries.definitionCN: 用于 make amends，意为对造成的过错作出补偿。它看起来像 amend 的复数，但实际是表示“补偿”的固定名词。

entries.definition: to correct errors in a text, especially by scholarly editing. It shares Latin emendare with amend but is restricted to textual criticism.
entries.definitionCN: 校订文本中的错误，尤指学术编辑。它与 amend 共享拉丁语 emendare，但只限用于文本校勘。

entries.definition: a scholarly correction to a text, or the act of making one. It is the technical counterpart of amendment in textual criticism.
entries.definitionCN: 对文本的学术性校正，或作出这种校正的行为。它是 amendment 在文本校勘领域的技术对应词。

entries.definition: a general re-examination and change of a text or plan. Revision can rework the whole, while an amendment usually targets a specific fault or clause.
entries.definitionCN: 对文本或计划的整体重新审视与改动。revision 可以重做整体，而 amendment 通常针对某一缺陷或条款。

entries.definition: the act of making something wrong right. Correction is narrower and more factual; a legal amendment can be formal even when nothing is strictly wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 把错误改对的行为。correction 更窄、更偏事实；法律上的 amendment 即使没有严格意义上的错误也可以是正式程序。

entries.definition: a change of any kind, with no implication that the result is better. Alteration is neutral, while amendment carries the purpose of removing a fault.
entries.definitionCN: 任何形式的改动，不暗示结果更好。alteration 是中性的，而 amendment 带有“去掉缺陷”的目的。

entries.definition: material added at the end of a document to supplement it. An addendum adds without rewriting; an amendment alters existing wording.
entries.definitionCN: 附加在文件末尾以补充内容的材料。addendum 只追加、不改写；amendment 则改动现有措辞。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: ex- 'out' plus menda 'fault', the amend/emend family, and the shortened mend. No invented 'add' meaning.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：ex-“出”加 menda“缺陷”、amend/emend 词族，以及缩短形式 mend。不编造“添加”的意思。

normal.en: Latin emendare is ex- 'out' + menda 'fault'. Amendment is literally 'fault-out', the removal of a defect.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 emendare 是 ex-“出”加 menda“缺陷”。amendment 字面上就是“把缺陷拿出去”。

normal.en: Mend is the shortened child of amend: the same word lost its first a-. That is why you mend a sock but amend a law.
normal.cn: mend 是 amend 缩短后的子嗣：同一个词丢掉了开头的 a-。所以你补袜子用 mend，改法律用 amend。

normal.en: Emend and emendation stay with manuscripts; amendment moved into law, contracts and soil.
normal.cn: emend 与 emendation 留在手稿校勘里；amendment 则走进了法律、合同和土壤。

normal.en: Soil amendment is named for the improvement it brings to the soil, even though you physically add it.
normal.cn: soil amendment 是因它给土壤带来的改良而得名，尽管你实际上是把东西加进去。

normal.en: The modern political 'amendment' can be an added clause, but the word still pretends to be a correction: that gap is the trap.
normal.cn: 现代政治中的 amendment 可能是追加条款，但这个词仍假装自己是在纠错：这个落差正是陷阱。

abstract.en: Picture a crack in a stone step. Amendment is not a new slab laid on top; it is the work of digging out the bad piece and making the step level again.
abstract.cn: 想象石阶上有一道裂缝。amendment 不是在上面铺一块新石板，而是把坏掉的一块挖出来、让台阶重新平整。

abstract.en: The same repair can be done to a sentence, a law, a contract or a person's conduct. What changes is the material, not the gesture.
abstract.cn: 同一种修补可以施于句子、法律、合同或一个人的行为。改变的是材料，不是动作。

abstract.en: When the repair is written down and voted on, it becomes a numbered document. When it merely adds, the name survives but the gesture has changed.
abstract.cn: 当修补被写下来并付诸表决，它就变成一份编号文件；当它只是追加时，名字留了下来，动作却已经变了。

examples.en: The senate passed an amendment to the housing law.
examples.cn: 参议院通过了一项住房法修正案。

examples.en: We signed a short amendment to the contract last Friday.
examples.cn: 上周五我们签署了一份简短的合同修订协议。

examples.en: The editor suggested three amendments to the second chapter.
examples.cn: 编辑建议对第二章作三处修订。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿门得门」——阿门牧师把写错的条文改得端正，再推门进去宣读 → amendment 修正、修正案

root: 来自古法语 amendement，上溯 amender 与拉丁语 emendare“去掉缺陷”，字面是 ex-“出”加 menda“缺陷”，核心是“把缺陷拿掉”，而非“添加”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of amendment, all one gesture: a fault is found and taken out. The material can be a manuscript, a constitution, a bill, a writ, a contract, soil or a person's conduct; only in the modern legislative drift does the gesture turn into addition.
sensesIntro.cn: amendment 的九个义项都来自同一个动作：发现缺陷并把它拿出去。材料可以是手稿、宪法、法案、令状、合同、土壤或一个人的行为；只有现代立法的漂移让这个动作变成了追加。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a faulty piece is dug out so the whole can stand correct.
core.cn: 核心意象：把坏掉的一块挖出来，让整体重新站正。

branches.en: THINGS AND PERSONS: a manuscript or a character can both be made better by removing what is wrong.
branches.cn: 物与人：手稿和品性都可以通过去掉错误之处而变好。

branches.en: LAW AND LEGISLATURE: a constitution is amended by procedure, and a bill is amended while it is still a draft.
branches.cn: 法律与立法：宪法依程序被修正，法案在仍是草案时被修正。

branches.en: DOCUMENTS: a writ, a contract and a scholarly text each have faults that must be officially removed.
branches.cn: 文件：令状、合同与学术文本各有必须正式去掉的缺陷。

branches.en: SOIL: the material is named for the improvement it brings, not for the act of adding it.
branches.cn: 土壤：这种材料因带来的改良而得名，而不是因添加的动作而得名。

branches.en: DRIFT: a clause may be attached purely to add, yet it still travels under the name of correction.
branches.cn: 漂移：条款可能纯粹为追加而附加，却仍顶着“纠正”的名字行走。

intro.en: Amendment is a transparent English derivative: amend + -ment. The base verb came into English from Old French, and its Latin core is ex- 'out' + menda 'fault'. English then adds -ment, -able, -atory and the negative un- to the finished stem, while the same Latin source also enters through emend and emendation.
intro.cn: amendment 是一个透明的英语派生词：amend + -ment。基础动词经古法语进入英语，其拉丁内核是 ex-“出”加 menda“缺陷”。英语随后在成品词干上加 -ment、-able、-atory 和否定前缀 un-，而同一拉丁来源还通过 emend 与 emendation 进入英语。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is emendare 'to correct, free from fault', menda/mendum 'fault, blemish', and the preposition ex 'out'. Menda is not related to English mend as a separate root; mend is simply amend with its first syllable lost.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族包括 emendare“纠正、去掉缺陷”、menda/mendum“缺陷、瑕疵”，以及介词 ex“出”。menda 与英语 mend 并非两个独立词根；mend 只是丢掉了第一个音节的 amend。

items.meaning: the act of correcting, or the corrected clause itself
items.meaningCN: 修正行为，或修正后的条款本身（-ment 构成行为或结果名词）
items.example: The amendment was accepted without debate.
items.exampleCN: 该修正案未经辩论就被接受了。

items.structure: Old French amender < Latin emendare (ex- out + menda fault)
items.meaning: to remove faults from something, to correct
items.example: They agreed to amend the treaty.
items.exampleCN: 他们同意修订这项条约。

items.meaning: compensation for a wrong, in make amends
items.meaningCN: （make amends）补偿；赔罪（-s 构成的固定名词）
items.example: He tried to make amends for the damage.
items.exampleCN: 他试图为造成的损害作出补偿。

items.meaning: able to be corrected or changed
items.meaningCN: 可修正的；可修订的（-able 表示能够）
items.example: The draft is still amendable at this stage.
items.exampleCN: 草案在这个阶段仍可修订。

items.meaningCN: 修正性的；起修改作用的（-atory 构成形容词）
items.example: The amendatory clause changed the payment date.
items.exampleCN: 这条修正性条款改变了付款日期。

items.meaningCN: 未修正的；未经修改的（un- 否定 + -ed 形容词）
items.example: The unamended text still contains the error.
items.exampleCN: 未修订的文本仍含有那个错误。

items.structure: e- (ex-, out) + mend(um) (fault) — same Latin source
items.meaning: to correct a text by scholarly editing
items.meaningCN: 校订文本；勘正（同源，限于文本校勘）
items.example: The editor emended the disputed line.
items.exampleCN: 编辑勘正了那行有争议的文字。

items.meaning: a scholarly correction to a text
items.meaningCN: 校勘；勘正（-ation 构成行为名词）
items.example: The new edition lists every emendation.
items.exampleCN: 新版列出了每一处校勘。

items.structure: shortened from amend by loss of the initial a- (aphetic form)
items.meaningCN: 修补；缝补（amendment 的缩短亲族，多用于具体物件）
items.example: She mended the torn sleeve herself.
items.exampleCN: 她自己缝好了破了的袖子。

items.example: The emendatory notes fill thirty pages.
items.exampleCN: 校订注释占了三页篇幅。

definition_zh: 样本量；样本容量；研究中受试者或观测的数量
definition_en: the number of individuals or observations included in a sample
core_image: 一张摊开的表格上写着各组应收的份数，负责人用手指点着其中一行核对数目
scene: 项目组围着一张大桌子开会，桌上摊着一张列着各组份数的表格，负责人用手指点住其中一行，确认数目后才开始招募。 The sample size was fixed at two hundred before the first participant was enrolled.
sceneCN: 这里指样本所包含的个体或观测数量（第 1 个义项：一个样本中包含的个体或观测的数目）；句意为在第一名参与者入组之前，样本量就已定为两百。图中可辨识物件：大桌、份数表格、笔、招募名单。

pos.zh: 样本量；样本容量

senses.title: The number in a sample
senses.definition: the number of individuals or observations that a sample contains
senses.definitionCN: 一个样本所包含的个体或观测的数目
senses.example: The sample size was fixed at two hundred before the first participant was enrolled.
senses.exampleCN: 在第一名参与者入组之前，样本量就已定为两百。
senses.why: Size came to mean extent or bulk, and the phrase simply asks how much of a sample there is.
senses.whyCN: 后一词指规模或份量，这个短语问的就是一份样本有多大。

senses.title: The number a study plans for
senses.titleCN: 研究计划中的受试人数
senses.definition: the number of participants a study design requires or promises to recruit
senses.definitionCN: 研究设计所需要或承诺招募的参与者人数
senses.example: The protocol states the sample size and the reason for it.
senses.exampleCN: 研究方案写明了样本量以及这样定的理由。
senses.why: A plan must name a number in advance, so the phrase moved from description to design.
senses.whyCN: 计划必须事先说出一个数目，短语于是从描述转为设计。

senses.title: The capacity in probability
senses.definition: the number of units in a sample treated as a quantity in mathematical statistics
senses.definitionCN: 在数理统计中被当作一个量来处理的样本单位数
senses.example: In probability, the sample size enters every estimate of error.
senses.exampleCN: 在概率论里，样本量进入每一个误差估计。
senses.why: Mathematics treats the count as a variable, so the phrase can name a symbol as well as a fact.
senses.whyCN: 数学把这个数目当作变量，短语因此也能命名一个符号，而不只是事实。

senses.title: The count left after losses
senses.titleCN: 剔除损耗后的有效数目
senses.definition: the number of usable cases that remain after missing or invalid data are removed
senses.definitionCN: 在剔除缺失或无效数据之后剩下的可用案例数
senses.example: After missing forms were removed, the effective sample size fell by a third.
senses.exampleCN: 剔除缺失表格后，有效样本量减少了三分之一。
senses.why: Real studies lose cases, so the phrase splits into the planned number and the number actually usable.
senses.whyCN: 真实研究总会损失案例，短语于是分成计划数目与实际可用数目。

senses.title: A small study
senses.definition: a study whose small number of cases makes strong conclusions unsafe
senses.definitionCN: 案例数目很少、因而难以支撑强结论的研究
senses.example: A small sample size makes the graph look certain when it is not.
senses.exampleCN: 样本量小会让图表显得确定，其实并不确定。
senses.why: The phrase can stand for the study itself when smallness is the point being criticised.
senses.whyCN: 当被批评的重点是规模太小时，这个短语可以代指研究本身。

senses.title: The calculation behind the number
senses.definition: the statistical work of deciding how many cases a study needs
senses.definitionCN: 决定一项研究需要多少案例的统计工作
senses.example: The team used a pilot study to plan the sample size.
senses.exampleCN: 团队用一项预试验来规划样本量。
senses.why: Once a number must be justified, the calculation that produces it takes the same name.
senses.whyCN: 一旦数目需要理由，产生它的计算也就用了同一个名字。

senses.title: The number too low to answer
senses.titleCN: 低到回答不了问题的数目
senses.definition: a number of cases too low for the effect being studied to show itself
senses.definitionCN: 案例数目过低，使所研究的效应无法显现
senses.example: A sample size of ten cannot support such a strong claim.
senses.exampleCN: 十例的样本量支撑不起这么强的结论。
senses.why: Smallness has a threshold, and below it the phrase turns into a criticism rather than a description.
senses.whyCN: 「小」有一个门槛，低于门槛时，这个短语就变成批评而不是描述。

senses.title: The count tied to statistical power
senses.titleCN: 与统计功效挂钩的数目
senses.definition: the number of cases needed for a study to detect an effect of a stated size
senses.definitionCN: 为使研究能检出某一既定大小的效应所需的案例数
senses.example: Power analysis links the sample size to the smallest effect worth detecting.
senses.exampleCN: 功效分析把样本量与值得检出的最小效应联系起来。
senses.why: Power is a function of numbers, so the phrase became the practical lever for planning a study.
senses.whyCN: 功效是数目的函数，短语因此成了规划研究的实际杠杆。

intro.en: Sample size joins the clipped Latin loanword sample and the French loanword size. The source of both halves is clear; the compound itself is a modern statistical term whose first record date is uncertain.
intro.cn: 这个短语把缩略的拉丁借词「样本」与法语借词「规模」合在一起。两部分的来源都清楚；复合词本身是近现代统计术语，最早记录的年代不确定。

items.en: Sample descends from exemplum, a sample or pattern, and from eximere, to take out.
items.cn: 前一词源自 exemplum「样本、范型」，更早来自 eximere「取出」。

items.en: Size came from Old French sise, a shortened form of assise, a session or assessment of dimensions.
items.cn: 后一词来自古法语 sise，是 assise 的缩略，后者指一次评定或对尺寸的核定。

items.en: Assise goes back to asseoir, to sit, and to Latin sedere, because a court or an assessment sits to settle a matter.
items.cn: assise 可追到 asseoir「坐」与拉丁语 sedere，因为法庭或评定要坐下来定夺事情。

items.en: English size is recorded from the fourteenth century with the sense of extent or bulk; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语里表示规模或份量的这个词自十四世纪起有记录；确切的首见年代不确定。

items.en: Sample size became a fixed term with the growth of statistical design in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.
items.cn: 随着十九至二十世纪统计设计的发展，这个短语成为固定术语。

items.en: Twentieth-century power analysis made the phrase a planning tool rather than a mere description.
items.cn: 二十世纪的功效分析使它成为规划工具，而不只是描述。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like sample size; the second group names neighbouring quantities in a study.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与「样本量」相近；第二组是研究里相邻的数量说法。

entries.definition: The portion itself, whose count the phrase measures.
entries.definitionCN: 指样本本身，短语量的正是它的数目。

entries.definition: The method by which the counted portion is chosen.
entries.definitionCN: 选出这份被计数样本的方法。

entries.definition: Extent or bulk; the second half of the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 规模或份量；短语的后一半。

entries.definition: Fairly large in extent, a word often used of samples.
entries.definitionCN: 规模相当大的，常用于形容样本。

entries.definition: Having a stated size, as in a well sized sample.
entries.definitionCN: 具有所述规模的，如规模合适的样本。

entries.definition: The count of participants in a study, stated more plainly.
entries.definitionCN: 研究参与者的数目，说法更直白。

entries.definition: The chosen set itself, which has a size.
entries.definitionCN: 被选出的那批本身，它有大小。

entries.definition: The chance of detecting a real effect, which depends on the count.
entries.definitionCN: 检出真实效应的机会，取决于案例数。

entries.definition: The whole group from which a sample and its size are drawn.
entries.definitionCN: 样本及其数目所由取出的整个群体。

entries.definition: The usable count after losses and weighting.
entries.definitionCN: 经损耗与加权后仍可用的数目。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real halves of the compound, the real statistical term and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用复合词两个真实的半、真实的统计术语与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Sample size is literally the size of the sample: how many units it holds.
normal.cn: sample size 字面就是样本的规模：它装着多少个单位。

normal.en: Size came from a word for an assessment that sits down to settle a matter.
normal.cn: size 来自「坐下来评定一件事」的说法。

normal.en: Fixed phrases include adequate sample size, effective sample size and sample size calculation.
normal.cn: 固定说法有足够样本量、有效样本量与样本量计算。

normal.en: A pilot study can suggest the sample size before the main study begins.
normal.cn: 预试验可以在主研究开始前提示样本量。

normal.en: Power analysis ties the number to the smallest effect worth detecting.
normal.cn: 功效分析把数目与值得检出的最小效应绑在一起。

abstract.en: Sample size is a promise about how much evidence the study is willing to buy.
abstract.cn: 样本量是研究愿意买多少证据的承诺。

abstract.en: Too few cases make a clear answer impossible, however neat the table looks.
abstract.cn: 案例太少，无论表格多整齐，都给不出清楚答案。

abstract.en: Every extra case costs time, so the number is always a bargain with reality.
abstract.cn: 每多一个案例都要花时间，所以这个数目永远是与现实的讨价还价。

examples.en: The sample size was doubled after the first analysis looked weak.
examples.cn: 第一次分析显得薄弱后，样本量被加倍。

examples.en: A sample size stated in advance protects the study from wishful thinking.
examples.cn: 事先写明样本量，可以保护研究不受一厢情愿之害。

examples.en: The paper reports the sample size in the first line of its methods.
examples.cn: 论文在方法部分第一行报告了样本量。

root: 前一词源自拉丁 exemplum「样本」，更早为 eximere「取出」；后一词源自法语 sise，为 assise 的缩略，更早来自 asseoir「坐」与拉丁 sedere「坐」。短语 sample size 是十九至二十世纪统计设计的固定术语，词源清楚，最早记录的年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one count: the number in a sample, the number a study plans, the mathematical capacity, the usable count, a small study, the calculation, the number too low to answer, and the count tied to power.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一个数目：样本里的数目、研究计划的数目、数学容量、可用数目、规模很小的研究、得出数目的计算、低到回答不了问题的数目，以及与功效挂钩的数目。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a table of quotas on a table, and a finger pressing one row until the number is agreed.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上一张份数表，一根手指按住其中一行，直到数目被确认。

branches.en: THE NUMBER AS FACT AND AS PLAN: what a sample holds, and what a study promises to recruit.
branches.cn: 数目作为事实与计划：样本里装了多少，以及研究承诺招募多少。

branches.en: THE SYMBOL IN PROBABILITY: the count becomes a variable in every error estimate.
branches.cn: 概率里的符号：这个数目在每一个误差估计里成为变量。

branches.en: THE COUNT THAT SURVIVES: missing cases are removed and the usable number remains.
branches.cn: 留下来的数目：缺失案例被剔除，可用数目留下。

branches.en: THE TOO SMALL STUDY: smallness turns the phrase from description into criticism.
branches.cn: 太小的研究：规模小使这个短语从描述变成批评。

branches.en: THE PLANNING LEVER: calculation and power analysis decide the number before data arrive.
branches.cn: 规划的杠杆：计算与功效分析在数据到来之前定下数目。

intro.en: The compound joins an English clipping of a Latin loanword to a French loanword; both halves are free words, and the Latin list covers the sample half only.
intro.cn: 这个复合词把拉丁借词的英语缩略形式与一个法语借词合在一起；两半都是自由词，拉丁词条只覆盖 sample 一半。

latinIntro.en: Latin exemplum, eximere and emere stand behind sample; size has no Latin ancestor in its immediate chain beyond sedere.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 exemplum、eximere 与 emere 在 sample 背后；size 的直接词链里除 sedere 外没有别的拉丁祖先。

items.example: The first half descends from this noun.
items.exampleCN: 前半部分由这个名词传下。

items.example: The verb supplies the picture behind sample.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「样本」一词背后的画面。

items.example: The first half names the portion counted.
items.exampleCN: 前半部分指被计数的那一份。

items.example: The second half came through French.
items.exampleCN: 后半部分经法语而来。

items.example: The longer French form settled dimensions.
items.exampleCN: 较长的法语形式用来核定尺寸。

items.example: A court sits to settle a matter.
items.exampleCN: 法庭坐下来定夺事情。

items.example: The second half is an ordinary English word.
items.exampleCN: 后半部分是一个普通英语词。

items.example: It builds sizeable from size.
items.exampleCN: 它由「规模」一词构成表示「可观的」形容词。

items.example: The compound fixes the two halves into one term.
items.exampleCN: 复合词把两半固定成一个术语。

definition_zh: 抵消；补偿；弥补；对冲；偏移；胶印
definition_en: to balance one cost, effect or influence against another so that the net result is reduced
core_image: 天平一端压着涨价账单，另一端放上节省下来的硬币，横梁慢慢回到水平
scene: 运费涨了不少，但仓库搬到近郊后省下的租金正好填上这块。 The savings offset the higher freight cost.
sceneCN: 这里指用省下的钱抵掉多出来的开支（第 1 个义项：抵消成本或开支）；句意为节省的费用抵消了上涨的运费。图中可辨识物件：天平、涨价的账单、一叠硬币。

pos.zh: 抵消；补偿；弥补；对冲
抵消；偏移；胶印

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示进行或性质的后缀构成，义为「抵消；起抵消作用的」
名词复数，义为「各项抵消额；偏移量」
由「碳」与「抵消额」合成的复合词，义为「碳抵消额度」

senses.title: To cancel a cost
senses.definition: to balance an extra cost with a saving elsewhere so that the net charge falls
senses.definitionCN: 用在别处省下的钱抵掉额外开支，使净支出下降
senses.example: The lower rent offset the rise in transport fees.
senses.exampleCN: 更低的租金抵消了运费的上涨。
senses.why: The word pictures one item set against another on a scale, and money is the easiest thing to weigh that way.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的画面是把一项放在天平上与另一项对着，而钱最容易被这样称量。

senses.title: To compensate for a loss
senses.definition: to make up for a loss or disadvantage with a gain in another area
senses.definitionCN: 用另一方面的收益补上损失或劣势
senses.example: Higher output offset the loss of two machines.
senses.exampleCN: 更高的产量补偿了两台机器的损失。
senses.why: Compensation is the accounting face of the same balance: what was lost is entered against what was gained.
senses.whyCN: 补偿是同一平衡的会计面孔：失去的与得到的对着记账。

senses.title: To make up for a shortfall
senses.definition: to supply what is missing so that the total reaches the required level
senses.definitionCN: 补上缺少的部分，使总量达到应有水平
senses.example: Extra tutoring offset the gap in her early schooling.
senses.exampleCN: 额外的辅导弥补了她早期教育的缺口。
senses.why: A shortfall is an imbalance on one side, and the verb puts weight on the other side.
senses.whyCN: 缺口是一侧的不平衡，这个动词往另一侧放上重量。

senses.title: To hedge a risk
senses.definition: to arrange a position that moves opposite to a risk so that losses are limited
senses.definitionCN: 安排一个与风险反向的头寸，以限制损失
senses.example: The airline offset its fuel exposure with forward contracts.
senses.exampleCN: 这家航空公司用远期合约对冲燃油敞口。
senses.why: Finance takes the scale literally: two positions are set against each other on purpose.
senses.whyCN: 金融把这个天平照字面使用：两个头寸被有意对着摆。

senses.title: To shift a position
senses.definition: to move an object or a line away from its original centre or alignment
senses.definitionCN: 使物体或线条离开原来的中心或对齐位置
senses.example: The surveyor offset the foundation line by ten centimetres.
senses.exampleCN: 测量员把基础线偏移了十厘米。
senses.why: Printing and engineering use offset for a displacement, the same side-by-side picture moved into space.
senses.whyCN: 印刷与工程用这个词表示位移，即同一「错开摆放」的画面移入空间。

senses.title: To balance the books
senses.definition: to enter one amount against another so that the accounts agree
senses.definitionCN: 把一笔金额对着另一笔记账，使账目相符
senses.example: The auditor offset the advance against the final invoice.
senses.exampleCN: 审计员把预付款与最终发票相抵。
senses.why: Accounting formalised the scale into two columns that must come to the same total.
senses.whyCN: 会计把这个天平固定成两栏，两栏最后要合成同一个数。

senses.title: To print by offset
senses.definition: to print from a plate onto a rubber blanket and then onto paper
senses.definitionCN: 先把印版上的图文转到橡皮布，再转到纸上
senses.example: The booklet was offset on coated stock.
senses.exampleCN: 这本小册子用胶印印在铜版纸上。
senses.why: The printing sense grew from the idea of an indirect transfer, ink being set off onto another surface.
senses.whyCN: 印刷义从「间接转移」长出，油墨被「转印」到另一表面。

senses.title: To neutralise emissions
senses.definition: to remove or balance an amount of carbon or pollution by an equivalent saving elsewhere
senses.definitionCN: 用在别处等量的减排来抵消一定量的碳排放或污染
senses.example: The firm offset its flights by funding a forest project.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司通过资助一个森林项目来抵消其航班的排放。
senses.why: Climate policy borrowed the accounting verb and made the two pans visible as emissions and removals.
senses.whyCN: 气候政策借用了这个会计动词，把天平两端的排放与移除摆到明面上。

intro.en: Offset is an English compound of off and set, first meaning to set out or start, later to place one thing against another. The printing sense arrived in the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: 这是英语中由 off 与 set 构成的复合词，最初意为「出发、开始」，后来指「把一物对着另一物摆放」；印刷义在十九世纪出现。

items.en: Set goes back to Old English settan, to place or cause to sit, and it supplies the placing half of the compound.
items.cn: set 可追溯到古英语 settan「放置、使坐」，提供这个复合词「摆放」的那一半。

items.en: Off marks separation or away, so offset began as a placing away from the main line.
items.cn: off 标出分离或离开，所以这个词最初指「放在主线之外」。

items.en: The early verb meant to set out on a journey, a sense now carried by set off rather than offset.
items.cn: 早期动词义为「出发上路」，这一义今天由「出发」那一短语承担，而不是本词。

items.en: The accounting and balancing sense developed later; the exact date of that shift is uncertain and is usually given only as the early modern period.
items.cn: 会计与抵消义后来才发展出来；这一转变的确切年代不确定，通常只给近代早期这一约数。

items.en: Offset printing named the transfer of ink from plate to blanket to paper, an indirect set-off.
items.cn: 胶印得名于油墨从印版转到橡皮布再到纸上的间接转印。

items.en: Carbon offset extended the accounting image to emissions, with one pan holding what is released and the other what is removed.
items.cn: 碳抵消把会计画面扩展到排放，一端放释放的量，另一端放移除的量。

note.en: The first group looks close or shares the set root; the second group names neighbouring ideas of compensation.
note.cn: 第一组与「offset」形近或共享 set 词根；第二组是与「补偿」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The present participle and noun for the act of balancing one item against another.
entries.definitionCN: 现在分词与名词，指把一项对着另一项抵消。

entries.definition: A phrasal verb meaning to start a journey or to trigger something.
entries.definitionCN: 短语动词，指出发或触发。

entries.definition: The beginning of something, from the same set with a different prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 指开端，由同一个表示「放置」的词根配不同前缀。

entries.definition: The machine used in offset printing.
entries.definitionCN: 胶印所用的机器。

entries.definition: A reversal or delay, from set and back rather than set and off.
entries.definitionCN: 指挫折或延误，由表示「放置」的词与表示「向后」的词构成。

entries.definition: To weigh against something with equal force.
entries.definitionCN: 指以相等的力量与之抗衡。

entries.definition: To make up for a loss or a disadvantage.
entries.definitionCN: 指弥补损失或劣势。

entries.definition: To bring two sides into equal weight.
entries.definitionCN: 指使两边重量相等。

entries.definition: To cancel the effect of something completely.
entries.definitionCN: 指彻底取消某物的作用。

entries.definition: To supply what is missing, in everyday wording.
entries.definitionCN: 指补上缺少的部分，日常说法。

entries.definition: To protect against a financial risk by an opposite position.
entries.definitionCN: 指用反向头寸防范金融风险。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the two halves off and set, the accounting image and the printing trade term.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用 off 与 set 两个部分、会计的天平画面，以及印刷行业术语。

normal.en: Off means away and set means place, so offset is to place one thing against another.
normal.cn: off 是「离开」，set 是「放置」，所以这个词就是把一物对着另一物放。

normal.en: The past tense does not change: offset, offset, offsetting.
normal.cn: 过去式不变：offset、offset、offsetting。

normal.en: Accounting says to offset an advance against an invoice.
normal.cn: 会计说把预付款与发票相抵。

normal.en: Printers speak of offset printing, where ink is transferred twice.
normal.cn: 印刷行话说胶印，油墨要转印两次。

normal.en: Carbon offset is the modern phrase for balancing emissions with removals.
normal.cn: 碳抵消是用移除量平衡排放量的现代说法。

abstract.en: To offset is to admit that a gain and a loss can sit on the same scale.
abstract.cn: 抵消，就是承认一份得与一份失可以放在同一架天平上。

abstract.en: Nothing is undone by offsetting; the scale simply returns to level.
abstract.cn: 抵消并没有撤销什么，只是让天平回到水平。

abstract.en: Every saving you find is a weight you may later place against a cost you cannot avoid.
abstract.cn: 你找到的每一笔节省，都是日后可以放到无法避免的开支对面的重量。

examples.en: Fuel savings offset the higher purchase price within three years.
examples.cn: 燃油节省在三年内抵消了更高的购价。

examples.en: The charity offsets its office emissions by planting trees.
examples.cn: 这家慈善机构通过植树抵消办公排放。

examples.en: The pipe was offset slightly to clear the beam.
examples.cn: 为了避开梁，这根管子被略微偏移。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「奥夫塞特」——天平一端压账单，一端放硬币：抵消、补偿

root: 英语复合词，由表示「离开」的前缀与表示「放置」的古英语动词构成；先指出发，后指抵消与错开摆放；印刷义为十九世纪。抵消义的确切转变年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses put two things on opposite pans: cost, loss, shortfall, risk, position, accounts, print and emissions.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把两样东西放到天平两端：成本、损失、缺口、风险、位置、账目、印刷与排放。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bill sits on one pan and a stack of coins on the other until the beam levels.
core.cn: 核心意象：一端压着账单，另一端放上硬币，横梁慢慢回到水平。

branches.en: THE TWO COLUMNS: an extra cost meets a saving, and the books are made to agree.
branches.cn: 两栏相对：额外开支遇上节省，账目被做成相符。

branches.en: THE GAP IS FILLED: a loss or a shortfall is covered from the other side.
branches.cn: 缺口被填：损失或不足由另一端补上。

branches.en: THE RISK IS HEDGED: a position is deliberately placed opposite to a threat.
branches.cn: 风险被对冲：有意把一笔头寸摆在威胁的对面。

branches.en: THE LINE IS SHIFTED: an object leaves its original alignment.
branches.cn: 线条被挪开：物体离开原来的对齐位置。

branches.en: THE INDIRECT TRANSFER: ink or emissions are set off onto another surface or account.
branches.cn: 间接转印：油墨或排放被转到另一表面或另一本账上。

intro.en: Offset is a native English compound, so its parts are ordinary English words and its endings are English endings.
intro.cn: 这是一个英语本族复合词，其组成部分是普通英语词，词尾也是英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source for this compound; the Latin column stays empty rather than importing unrelated forms.
latinIntro.cn: 这个复合词没有拉丁语来源，拉丁部分留空，不引入无关形式。

items.example: It marks the displacement in the compound.
items.exampleCN: 它标出这个复合词中的位移。

items.meaning: to place, to cause to sit
items.example: It supplies the placing half of the word.
items.exampleCN: 它提供这个词「摆放」的那一半。

items.example: The Old English form behind modern set.
items.exampleCN: 现代 set 背后的古英语形式。

items.example: The same form serves as verb and noun.
items.exampleCN: 同一形式兼作动词与名词。

items.example: It forms offsetting.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 offsetting。

items.example: The trade name preserves the transfer image.
items.exampleCN: 行业名称保留了转印画面。

items.example: It extends the accounting image to climate.
items.exampleCN: 它把会计画面扩展到气候。

items.example: It shows set with a different prefix.
items.exampleCN: 它展示 set 配另一个前缀。

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示进行或性质的后缀构成，义为「抵消；起抵消作用的」
名词复数，义为「各项抵消额；偏移量」
由「碳」与「抵消额」合成的复合词，义为「碳抵消额度」

definition_zh: 中位数；中线；中间值；中央分隔带；正中的
definition_en: the middle value of a set of numbers arranged in order, or a line or strip running through the middle
core_image: 一排高低不齐的柱子按高度站好，正中间那一根被圈出来
scene: 研究者在把七份薪水从低到高排好后，圈出了正中间的那一份。 The median of the seven salaries is lower than the average.
sceneCN: 这里指「按大小排好后位于正中间的那个数」（第 1 个义项：统计中的中位数）；句意为七份薪水的中位数低于平均值。可辨识物件：薪水单、排序标尺、红圈、直尺。

pos.zh: 中位数；中线；中间值；中央分隔带
中间的；中位的

senses.title: The middle value in statistics
senses.definition: the value that divides an ordered set into two equal halves
senses.definitionCN: 把一个按序排列的集合分成相等两半的那个值
senses.example: The median of the seven salaries is lower than the average.
senses.exampleCN: 七份薪水的中位数低于平均值。
senses.why: Medianus means 'of the middle', and statistics simply names the item that stands at the middle of an ordered row.
senses.whyCN: medianus 意为「中间的」，统计学只是把按序排好后站在中间的那一项命名为中位数。

senses.title: A line from a vertex to the midpoint
senses.definition: a line drawn from a vertex of a triangle to the midpoint of the opposite side
senses.definitionCN: 从三角形一个顶点画到对边中点的线段
senses.example: The three medians of a triangle meet at a single point.
senses.exampleCN: 三角形的三条中线交于一点。
senses.why: The geometric line runs to the middle of the opposite side, so the same word serves geometry.
senses.whyCN: 这条几何线通向对边的中点，因此同一个词也用于几何。

senses.title: A middle point in general
senses.definition: a point or value lying in the middle of a range
senses.definitionCN: 落在某个范围中间的点或值
senses.example: The median of the range falls halfway between the two extremes.
senses.exampleCN: 这一范围的中间值落在两个极端之间。
senses.why: The general sense is the plain reading of the Latin adjective, before any technical use.
senses.whyCN: 一般义是那个拉丁形容词最朴素的读法，早于任何技术用法。

senses.title: A strip dividing a road
senses.definition: the strip of ground that separates opposing lanes of traffic
senses.definitionCN: 把相反方向车道隔开的那条地带
senses.example: A low hedge runs along the median for two miles.
senses.exampleCN: 一条低矮的树篱沿着中央分隔带延伸两英里。
senses.why: The strip occupies the middle of the road, so the middle-value word was borrowed for it.
senses.whyCN: 这条地带占着道路的中间，于是表示「中间」的词被借来指它。

senses.title: A structure at the body's midline
senses.definition: an anatomical structure lying along the midline of the body
senses.definitionCN: 沿人体正中线分布的解剖结构
senses.example: The median nerve passes through the wrist.
senses.exampleCN: 正中神经经过腕部。
senses.why: Anatomy uses the adjective for anything placed on the midline, keeping the literal spatial sense.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学把这个形容词用于一切位于正中线上的结构，保留了字面的空间义。

senses.title: Middle in position or value
senses.definition: occupying or representing the middle of a range
senses.definitionCN: 占据或代表某个范围的中间
senses.example: The median age of the group is thirty-two.
senses.exampleCN: 这个群体的年龄中位数是三十二岁。
senses.why: As an adjective the word simply places something in the middle, whether in space or in a ranked list.
senses.whyCN: 作形容词时，这个词只是把某物放在中间，无论指空间还是指排序。

senses.title: The midline of a trapezoid
senses.definition: the segment joining the midpoints of the non-parallel sides of a trapezoid
senses.definitionCN: 连接梯形两条非平行边中点的线段
senses.example: Its length equals the average of the two parallel sides.
senses.exampleCN: 它的长度等于两条平行边的平均值。
senses.why: The segment sits halfway between the parallel sides, so geometry calls it a median as well.
senses.whyCN: 这条线段位于两条平行边之间的正中，几何学同样称它为中位线。

senses.title: The median voter in politics
senses.definition: the voter at the middle of the distribution of opinions
senses.definitionCN: 意见分布中处于中间位置的那位选民
senses.example: A candidate must win the median voter to take the seat.
senses.exampleCN: 候选人必须赢得中位选民才能拿下这个席位。
senses.why: Political science applies the statistical middle to opinions: whoever stands at the centre of the distribution decides the contest.
senses.whyCN: 政治学把统计上的中间用到意见上：站在分布中心的人决定胜负。

intro.en: Median comes from Latin medianus 'of the middle', an adjective from medius 'middle'; English took it directly from Latin in the sixteenth century, probably with French mediation.
intro.cn: median 出自拉丁形容词 medianus「中间的」，其词根为 medius「中间」；英语在十六世纪直接取自拉丁语，可能经法语中转。

items.en: Medius meant 'middle, in the middle'. It is generally traced to an old root for 'middle', a reconstructed form rather than a written record.
items.cn: medius 意为「中间的、在中间」。它一般被上溯到一个表示「中间」的古老词根，此形式属重构而非书面记录。

items.en: Medius plus the adjective ending -anus produced medianus 'of the middle, middlemost'.
items.cn: medius 加形容词词尾 -anus 构成 medianus「中间的、最当中的」。

items.en: The form passed through Late Latin and French usage before entering English, where it first described things lying in the middle.
items.cn: 这一形式经晚期拉丁语与法语用法，再进入英语，最初描述位于中间的事物。

items.en: The geometric sense of a line to the midpoint is old in Latin mathematical writing and passed into English with the word.
items.cn: 「通到中点的线」这一几何义在拉丁数学文献中已很古老，随词一同进入英语。

items.en: The statistical sense of the middle value is a nineteenth-century development, fixed as ordinary technical vocabulary in the twentieth.
items.cn: 「居中数值」的统计义是十九世纪的发展，到二十世纪固定为常用技术词汇。

items.en: The road strip and the anatomical uses are later transfers of the plain spatial sense; their exact first dates are approximate.
items.cn: 道路分隔带与解剖学用法都是空间义的较晚转移，确切首见年代只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin middle root, where prefix or ending is all that differs; group two holds words for a central value or position.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「中间」词根、只差前缀或词尾的词；第二组是表示中心值或中心位置的词。

entries.definition: The Latin neuter form used as a noun: something in the middle, hence a means or a material.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁中性形式作名词用：居中之物，引申为手段或媒材。

entries.definition: To stand in the middle between two parties; the verb keeps the spatial picture.
entries.definitionCN: 站在两方中间，动词保留了空间画面。

entries.definition: In- 'not' plus mediatus 'middle': with nothing in between, hence direct.
entries.definitionCN: in-「不」加 mediatus「中间」：中间没有东西，故指直接。

entries.definition: Inter- 'between' plus medius: lying between two stages or levels.
entries.definitionCN: inter-「在……之间」加 medius：位于两个阶段或层次之间。

entries.definition: A calculated value, which may differ from the middle item when the data are skewed.
entries.definitionCN: 由总和除以个数算出的值，数据偏斜时可能与居中那一项不同。

entries.definition: The point equally distant from both ends of a line or range.
entries.definitionCN: 与线段或范围两端等距的点。

entries.definition: The everyday word for the central part, with no technical sense.
entries.definitionCN: 表示中央部分的日常词，不含技术义。

entries.definition: The middle of a space or an activity, often a point of concentration.
entries.definitionCN: 空间或活动的中心，常指聚集之点。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定说法与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means 'middle', so every sense puts something at the centre of a row, a road, a body or a triangle.
normal.cn: 词根意为「中间」，因此每个义项都是把某物放在一列数、一条路、一个人体或一个三角形的中央。

normal.en: One family runs median, medial, medium, mediate and intermediate.
normal.cn: 同族词串成一条线：中位数、内侧的、媒介、调解、中间的。

normal.en: The negated relative is immediate: nothing in the middle means direct.
normal.cn: 加了否定前缀的亲属词是 immediate：中间没有东西，就是直接。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: median income, median age, the median strip, the median voter.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出用法：收入中位数、年龄中位数、中央分隔带、中位选民。

normal.en: In a triangle the three medians meet at one point, so the word always points to the halfway mark.
normal.cn: 在三角形里三条中线交于一点，可见这个词总指向「一半处」的标记。

abstract.en: Picture a row of pillars of different heights with the middle one marked by a ring of paint.
abstract.cn: 想象一排高低不同的柱子，正中间那根被画上一圈颜料。

abstract.en: Picture a road divided by a narrow green strip, with traffic flowing on either side.
abstract.cn: 想象一条被窄窄的绿带分开的道路，两侧车流各自前行。

abstract.en: Picture a line drawn from the tip of a triangle straight to the middle of the wall opposite.
abstract.cn: 想象从三角形顶点笔直画到对面墙正中的一条线。

examples.en: The median divides the ordered list into two equal halves.
examples.cn: 中位数把排好序的列表分成相等的两半。

examples.en: Median income in the region has barely moved.
examples.cn: 该地区的收入中位数几乎没有变化。

examples.en: The median strip was planted with low shrubs.
examples.cn: 中央分隔带上种了低矮的灌木。

dict_mnemonic.text: 词根意为「中间」，加形容词词尾表示「属于中间的」：把一列数按大小排好，站在正中的那一项就是中位数；一条路正中的地带就是中央分隔带。

root: 拉丁 medianus「中间的」＝ medius「中间」＋形容词词尾 -anus；medius 更早词根属重构形式。英语十六世纪直接取自拉丁语，可能经法语中转。同根词 medium、mediate、immediate、intermediate 只差前缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all place one thing at the centre: a value in a ranked list, a line to the midpoint, a strip in a road, a nerve on the body's midline, and a voter at the middle of opinion. The word never leaves the halfway mark.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把某物放在正中：排序列表里的一个值、通向中点的一条线、道路正中的一条带、身体正中线上的一条神经，以及意见分布正中的一位选民。这个词始终不离「一半处」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of columns ordered by height, with the middle one circled.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排按高度排好的柱子，正中间那根被圈出。

branches.en: MIDDLE VALUE: statistics and ordinary speech both name what stands halfway.
branches.cn: 中间值：统计学与日常说法都指站在一半处的那个。

branches.en: MIDPOINT: geometry draws to the middle of the opposite side.
branches.cn: 中点：几何把线画到对边的正中。

branches.en: THE ROAD: a strip occupies the middle of the carriageway.
branches.cn: 道路：一条地带占据车道的正中。

branches.en: POSITION: anatomy and ordinary adjectives place a structure on the midline.
branches.cn: 位置：解剖学与普通形容词都把结构放在正中线上。

branches.en: OPINION: politics applies the statistical middle to a distribution of views.
branches.cn: 意见：政治学把统计上的中间用到意见分布上。

intro.en: Median is a Latin adjective in English dress; the root medius also builds the nouns and verbs for means and mediation.
intro.cn: median 是一个穿上英语外衣的拉丁形容词；词根 medius 还构成表示手段与调解的名词和动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin medius yields medianus, medietas, medium and mediare; in- and inter- reverse or relocate the middle.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 medius 衍生 medianus、medietas、medium、mediare；前缀 in- 与 inter- 否定或移动「中间」。

items.example: The root places something at the centre.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根把某物放到中央。

items.example: The suffix turns the root into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把词根变成形容词。

items.example: The Latin adjective is the direct source of median.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁形容词是 median 的直接来源。

items.meaning: the middle value; middle in position
items.example: The median income rose.
items.exampleCN: 收入中位数上升了。

items.example: The medial nerve runs along the arm.
items.exampleCN: 内侧神经沿手臂分布。

items.structure: medius, neuter form used as a noun
items.example: Water is the medium for the reaction.
items.exampleCN: 水是这个反应的介质。

items.example: A neutral party mediated the dispute.
items.exampleCN: 一个中立方调解了这场争端。

items.example: An intermediate layer separates the two.
items.exampleCN: 一个中间层把两者隔开。

definition_zh: 极权主义的；（政权）试图控制社会与私人生活全部领域的
definition_en: of or relating to a system of government that claims control over every part of public and private life and allows no rival political power
core_image: 一张巨网罩住整座城市，从工厂到厨房，每一扇窗都连着同一根线
scene: 城市里每块布告栏都印着同一张面孔，广播从早到晚只有一种声音。 The totalitarian state demanded that every family report on its neighbours.
sceneCN: 句中这个词形容一种把公共与私人生活都纳入控制的政权（第 1 个义项：主张国家权力覆盖社会全部领域、不容对立政治力量存在的）；句意为极权国家要求每个家庭举报邻居。图中可辨识物件：布告栏、同一张面孔、广播喇叭、紧闭的家门、举报表格。

pos.zh: 极权主义的；全面控制社会与私人生活的
极权主义者；极权政权的支持者

derivatives.zh: 整体主义者 / 整体主义的
把事物当作不可分割整体的
使总体化；把各部分合成整体

senses.title: State control over every sphere
senses.titleCN: 国家权力覆盖社会全部领域
senses.definition: describing a regime that claims authority over industry, media, education, family life and private belief alike
senses.definitionCN: 形容一种政权声称对工业、媒体、教育、家庭生活与个人信念都拥有支配权
senses.example: The totalitarian state demanded that every family report on its neighbours.
senses.exampleCN: 这个极权国家要求每个家庭举报邻居。
senses.why: The word was coined in English in the nineteen-twenties on the Italian model totalitario, from total, because such a regime claims the whole of life and not merely the machinery of government.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在二十世纪二十年代按意大利语 totalitario 的样式在英语中造出，词干是「全部」，因为这类政权声称要管的是整个生活，而不只是政府机构。

senses.title: No tolerated opposition
senses.titleCN: 不容许任何对立政治力量
senses.definition: allowing only one party and treating organised criticism as a crime
senses.definitionCN: 只允许一个政党存在，把任何有组织的批评都当作犯罪
senses.example: Opposition parties were banned outright under the totalitarian system.
senses.exampleCN: 在极权制度下，反对党被彻底取缔。
senses.why: If the state owns the whole, a rival centre of loyalty is by definition a crack in that whole.
senses.whyCN: 如果国家声称拥有一切，那么另一个忠诚中心在定义上就是那个整体上的一道裂缝。

senses.title: One official ideology
senses.titleCN: 只承认一种官方意识形态
senses.definition: requiring public adherence to a single doctrine and presenting it as the settled truth about society
senses.definitionCN: 要求公众信奉唯一一套学说，并把它说成关于社会的定论
senses.example: Schoolbooks taught the totalitarian doctrine in every grade.
senses.exampleCN: 教科书在每个年级都讲授这套极权学说。
senses.why: A single party needs a single story about the past and the future, so doctrine becomes part of the state apparatus.
senses.whyCN: 一党统治需要唯一一套关于过去与未来的叙述，于是学说本身成了国家机器的一部分。

senses.title: Demanding total obedience from a person
senses.definition: describing a leader, party or rule that requires unqualified obedience from each individual
senses.definitionCN: 形容某个领袖、政党或规则要求每个人无条件服从
senses.example: The party's totalitarian demand reached even into the choice of a career.
senses.exampleCN: 这个政党的极权要求甚至伸进了职业选择。
senses.why: The adjective attaches to the agent as well as to the system: a ruler is called totalitarian when he asks for the whole person.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词既能形容制度，也能形容施动者：当一个统治者索要整个人时，他就被称为极权的。

senses.title: Control extended to non-state institutions
senses.titleCN: 把控制延伸到非国家机构
senses.definition: used of a workplace, school or family that regulates every detail of its members' lives
senses.definitionCN: 用于形容把成员生活每个细节都管起来的单位、学校或家庭
senses.example: Critics called the company's totalitarian rules a parody of government.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者说这家公司的极权规章是对政府的一次戏仿。
senses.why: The word travels: any body that claims the whole of a person's life can take the label once reserved for the state.
senses.whyCN: 这个词会转移：任何索要一个人全部生活的团体，都能用上这个原属国家的标签。

senses.title: Uniform style in art and building
senses.titleCN: 艺术与建筑上的整齐划一
senses.definition: describing an aesthetic that suppresses individual variation in favour of one approved style
senses.definitionCN: 形容压抑个体差异、只留一种被批准风格的美学
senses.example: The regime's totalitarian architecture left no room for ornament.
senses.exampleCN: 这个政权的极权建筑不留任何装饰的余地。
senses.why: Art follows politics here: a style that admits only one form is the visible face of one-party rule.
senses.whyCN: 在这里艺术跟着政治走：只容一种形式的风格，就是一党统治看得见的脸。

senses.title: A supporter of such a system
senses.titleCN: 支持极权制度的人（可数名词）
senses.definition: a person who advocates or serves a totalitarian regime
senses.definitionCN: 主张或服务于极权政权的人
senses.example: The memoir describes how a young totalitarian rose through the party.
senses.exampleCN: 这本回忆录写到一个年轻的极权主义者如何在党内攀升。
senses.why: The noun arrived later than the adjective and always names a person, never a doctrine.
senses.whyCN: 名词义晚于形容词出现，而且始终指人，不指学说。

senses.title: The historical label for twentieth-century regimes
senses.titleCN: 二十世纪特定政权的历史标签
senses.definition: the term historians use for Fascist Italy, Nazi Germany and the Soviet system, and debate as a comparative category
senses.definitionCN: 历史学家用于法西斯意大利、纳粹德国与苏联体制的说法，并作为比较范畴加以争论
senses.example: Historians still argue about how far the totalitarian label fits each case.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家至今仍在争论这个极权标签在多大程度上适用于各个个案。
senses.why: The word was born as a description of one regime and later became a category that scholars test against others.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初只是对某一个政权的描述，后来变成学者用来检验其他政权的范畴。

intro.en: Totalitarian was formed in English in 1926 as a description of Italian fascism, on the model of Italian totalitario and with an ending borrowed from authoritarian. The root totus is Latin, but its deeper origin is not settled.
intro.cn: totalitarian 于 1926 年在英语中造出，用来描述意大利法西斯主义，仿意大利语 totalitario 而成，词尾借自 authoritarian。词干 totus 是拉丁语，但其更深来源未有定论。

items.en: Totus meant 'all, whole, entire'. Its deeper origin is unknown, so any Indo-European form proposed for it is a reconstruction rather than a demonstrated source.
items.cn: totus 意为「全部、整个」。其更深来源不明，凡为其提出的印欧语形式都属重构，并非已证实的来源。

items.en: Totalis 'entire' was built on totus and passed through Old French as total; the same stem yields totality and totalize.
items.cn: totalis「整个的」由 totus 构成，经古法语进入英语作 total；同一词干还产生 totality 与 totalize。

items.en: In the nineteen-twenties Italian political writing used totalitario for a state that claimed the whole of society; the exact first user is disputed.
items.cn: 二十世纪二十年代意大利政治写作使用 totalitario 指声称拥有整个社会的国家；最早使用者为谁仍有争议。

items.en: English totalitarian is recorded in 1926 in reference to Italian fascism. It was framed on total with the ending of authoritarian rather than on a Latin base.
items.cn: 英语 totalitarian 于 1926 年见于记录，指意大利法西斯主义。它以 total 为干、取 authoritarian 的词尾构成，并非来自某个拉丁词形。

items.en: The noun for a member of such a party is recorded from 1938. After the war the term widened into a comparative category applied to several regimes.
items.cn: 指这类政党成员的 noun 义自 1938 年见于记录。战后这个词扩大为一个用于多个政权的比较范畴。

items.en: Source uncertain for the pre-Latin origin of totus and for the identity of the first Italian coiner; the date 1926 itself is firm.
items.cn: 来源不确定之处在于 totus 在拉丁语之前的来源，以及首位意大利造词者是谁；1926 这个年代本身是确定的。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same Latin stem total-, which are easy to mix up in form; group two holds political adjectives that overlap in meaning but differ in what they claim.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词干 total- 的词，形式上极易混淆；第二组是语义重叠但主张内容不同的政治形容词。

entries.definition: Complete in extent or number; it counts or measures a quantity and makes no political claim.
entries.definitionCN: 指范围或数量上的完整；它只是计数或计量，不作政治主张。

entries.definition: The whole of something taken together, as in the totality of the evidence; a noun of quantity, not of rule.
entries.definitionCN: 指某物合起来的整体，如证据的整体；是数量的名词，不是统治的名词。

entries.definition: To gather parts into one whole or to state something as a single total; it describes a way of counting, not of governing.
entries.definitionCN: 指把各部分合成整体，或把某物说成一个总数；说的是计数方式，不是统治方式。

entries.definition: A rare term for the doctrine that society should be treated as one indivisible unit; it names a belief rather than the apparatus of a state.
entries.definitionCN: 罕见说法，指社会应被视为不可分割整体的信念；它命名一种信念，而非国家机器。

entries.definition: Favouring imposed order and obedience; it can describe a strong government without claiming control of every private detail.
entries.definitionCN: 偏爱强加秩序与服从；可形容强势政府，但不必然声称控制每个私人细节。

entries.definition: Marked by the unchecked will of a single ruler; the emphasis is on who decides, not on how far the state reaches.
entries.definitionCN: 以单一统治者不受制约的意志为特征；重点在谁作决定，而非国家伸手多远。

entries.definition: Of a ruler who exercises power arbitrarily and harshly; it stresses cruelty and caprice rather than total organisation.
entries.definitionCN: 指统治者专断而严酷地行使权力；强调残暴与任性，而非全面组织社会。

entries.definition: Of a doctrine that the sovereign holds unlimited legal authority; it is a claim about law, while totalitarian is a claim about social life.
entries.definitionCN: 指君主拥有无限法律权威的学说；它主张的是法律权限，而 totalitarian 主张的是社会生活。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin pieces, real derived words and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁语构件、真实的派生词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: total plus the ending of authoritarian: the whole of life, enforced by authority.
normal.cn: total 加上 authoritarian 的词尾：生活的全部，由权威来执行。

normal.en: The family runs total, totality, totalize, totalitarian and totalitarianism.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 total、totality、totalize、totalitarian 与 totalitarianism。

normal.en: Latin totus 'whole' is the root, and its own earlier origin is unknown.
normal.cn: 词根是拉丁 totus「全部」，它更早的来源不明。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the political use: totalitarian state, totalitarian regime, totalitarian control.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出政治用法：极权国家、极权政权、极权控制。

normal.en: The ending matches authoritarian and egalitarian, both nineteenth-century political coinages.
normal.cn: 词尾与 authoritarian、egalitarian 一致，这两个词都是十九世纪的政治造词。

abstract.en: Picture a single key that opens every door on one street, so no door can be locked from inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙能开一条街上所有的门，于是没有一扇门能从里面反锁。

abstract.en: Picture a map with one colour only, so no border can be told from another border.
abstract.cn: 想象一张只有一种颜色的地图，于是任何边界都分不出彼此。

abstract.en: Picture a choir where every voice is tuned to the same note, leaving no second line to hear.
abstract.cn: 想象一个合唱团把每个声音都调到同一个音，于是听不到第二条声部。

examples.en: The totalitarian regime censored newspapers, schools and private letters alike.
examples.cn: 这个极权政权把报纸、学校与私人信件一并审查。

examples.en: Scholars debate whether the totalitarian label describes a type or only a period.
examples.cn: 学者在争论极权这个标签描述的是一个类型，还是仅仅一个时期。

examples.en: Her novel shows how a totalitarian demand can enter an ordinary family.
examples.cn: 她的小说展示极权的要求如何进入一个普通家庭。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「透头-他立」——把每个人的「头」都透过管起来，只许「立」一种声音 → 极权的

root: 拉丁 totus「全部、整个」+ 英语形容词词尾（借自 authoritarian）；totus 更深来源不明，凡提出的印欧形式均为重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses fan out from one claim: the whole of life belongs to the state, and that claim is then read as a party monopoly, a doctrine, a demand on persons, an extension into other institutions, a style, a person and a historical label.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从同一个主张展开：整个生活属于国家；这一主张再依次读作一党垄断、一套学说、对个人的索求、向其他机构的延伸、一种风格、一个人、一个历史标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one net over the whole city, every window tied to the same wire.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张巨网罩住整座城市，每一扇窗都连着同一根线。

branches.en: DOCTRINE AND LABEL: the claim about the whole of life begins as a description and later becomes a category historians test.
branches.cn: 主张与标签：关于整个生活的主张先是描述，后来成为历史学家检验的范畴。

branches.en: PARTY AND CREED: one party needs one story, so the monopoly of power and the monopoly of truth are the same institution seen twice.
branches.cn: 政党与信条：一党需要一套叙述，于是权力的垄断与真理的垄断是同一机构的两种看法。

branches.en: PERSON AND SYSTEM: a ruler can be called totalitarian for demanding the whole person, and the noun names whoever serves that demand.
branches.cn: 人与制度：统治者因索要整个人而被称为极权的，名词则指服务于这一索要的人。

branches.en: BEYOND THE STATE: the same demand appears in a firm or a family, which shows the claim is about control rather than about office.
branches.cn: 越过国家：同样的索求出现在公司或家庭里，说明这一主张关乎控制，而非关乎公职。

branches.en: VISIBLE FORM: a style admitting one shape only is the aesthetic mirror of one-party rule.
branches.cn: 可见形态：只容一种形状的风格，是一党统治在美学上的镜像。

intro.en: Totalitarian is an English coinage assembled from a Latin root and two productive endings, so its parts can be read separately from its politics.
intro.cn: totalitarian 是英语造词，由一个拉丁词根与两个能产词尾拼成，因此其构件可以脱离政治含义单独读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin totus gives totalis and, through French, total; the endings -arian and -ism came into English from Latin and Greek patterns and now build many modern labels.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 totus 产生 totalis，并经法语产生 total；词尾 -arian 与 -ism 由拉丁与希腊的模式进入英语，如今构成许多现代标签。

items.example: The root carries the idea of a whole with no part left outside.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着「整体，无一部分在外」的意思。

items.example: The medieval form supplied the everyday adjective total.
items.exampleCN: 这个中世纪词形提供了日常形容词 total。

items.structure: total (English adjective and noun, from Old French)
items.example: The total cost was never published.
items.exampleCN: 总成本从未公布。

items.example: The totality of the records was sealed.
items.exampleCN: 全部记录被封存。

items.structure: total + -arian (one who, or of a kind)
items.meaning: of a state claiming the whole of life
items.meaningCN: 主张掌控整个生活的；极权的
items.example: The totalitarian state claimed the whole of life.
items.exampleCN: 这个极权国家声称拥有整个生活。

items.meaning: the system or doctrine of such rule
items.example: Totalitarianism reduces citizens to subjects.
items.exampleCN: 极权制度把公民降为臣民。

items.meaning: belonging to, or one who follows
items.example: The ending also builds authoritarian and egalitarian.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾还构成 authoritarian 与 egalitarian。

items.example: The ending turns an adjective into the name of a system.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把形容词变成一种制度的名称。

items.example: The survey totalizes scattered local figures.
items.exampleCN: 这份调查把分散的地方数字汇成整体。

latinEntries.structure: totalitas, totalitatis (f., third declension, Medieval Latin)

definition_zh: 解剖学；身体结构；解剖；剖析
definition_en: the scientific study of the structure of bodies, or the structure of a body or system itself
core_image: 一具被细心分层的躯干示意图，肌肉、血管与骨骼逐层揭开
scene: 医学院的新生第一学期就要背骨头。 Anatomy students spend the first term learning every bone of the hand.
sceneCN: 这里 anatomy 指「解剖学」（第 1 个义项：研究生物体结构的学科）；句意：解剖学学生第一学期要学完手部每一块骨头。图中可辨识物件：分层人体图、手部骨骼标本、标注签。

pos.zh: 解剖学；身体结构；解剖（行为）；剖析（可数时指某生物或某系统的结构）

derivatives.zh: 原子（同出希腊 temnein「切」，但前缀相反，见 similar）

senses.title: The Science of Structure
senses.titleCN: 解剖学：研究身体结构的学科
senses.definition: the scientific study of the structure of living bodies
senses.definitionCN: 研究生物体结构的科学
senses.example: Anatomy students spend the first term learning every bone of the hand.
senses.exampleCN: 解剖学学生第一学期要学完手部每一块骨头。
senses.why: Greek ana- meant 'up, throughout' and temnein meant 'to cut'. Anatomē was a cutting-up, and the name of the act became the name of the science that performs it.
senses.whyCN: 希腊前缀 ana- 意为「向上、遍及」，temnein 意为「切」。anatomē 就是「切开」，这个动作的名称后来变成了从事该动作的学科名称。

senses.title: Body Structure Itself
senses.titleCN: 身体结构：部件如何安排
senses.definition: the actual structure of a body, its parts and their arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 身体实际的结构、各部分及其排列
senses.example: The dolphin's anatomy shows that its flipper is a modified arm.
senses.exampleCN: 海豚的身体结构表明，它的鳍肢是改造过的手臂。
senses.why: The same noun names the object as well as the study. When a biologist says 'the anatomy of the dolphin', the cutting has become a description of what was found.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词既指学科也指对象；当生物学家说 the anatomy of the dolphin 时，「切」已经变成了对所见之物的描述。

senses.title: The Act of Dissection
senses.titleCN: 解剖：切开并分离的动作
senses.definition: the act or practice of cutting a body apart to study it
senses.definitionCN: 为研究而把身体切开的动作或做法
senses.example: The anatomy of the specimen took the whole afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 对这份标本的解剖花了一整个下午。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: the physical cutting. Modern laboratories may use imaging instead, but the word still remembers the knife.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：实际的切割。现代实验室可能改用成像技术，但这个词仍记得那把刀。

senses.title: Detailed Analysis
senses.titleCN: 剖析：把一个整体拆开来看
senses.definition: a detailed examination of the parts of a thing or idea
senses.definitionCN: 对事物或观念的各个部分所作的细致检查
senses.example: The book is an anatomy of how rumours spread.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书是对谣言如何传播的一次剖析。
senses.why: The metaphor is exact: to understand a whole, take it apart part by part. Analysts therefore borrow the anatomist's word for structures that are not biological.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻非常贴切：要理解一个整体，就把它一部分一部分拆开。因此分析者借解剖学家的词，用于并非生物的结构。

senses.title: The Human Body
senses.definition: the human body, especially in informal or humorous use
senses.definitionCN: 人的身体，尤用于口语或戏谑
senses.example: He fell and bruised his entire anatomy.
senses.exampleCN: 他摔了一跤，全身都碰伤了。
senses.why: Because anatomy studies the body, the noun can stand for the body itself. The tone is usually light, as if the speaker were looking at the body from outside.
senses.whyCN: 因为解剖学研究身体，这个名词可以代指身体本身；语气通常轻松，仿佛说话者从外部打量这具身体。

senses.title: Plant and Animal Structure
senses.titleCN: 动植物结构：非人体的解剖
senses.definition: the structure of plants or animals studied as a field
senses.definitionCN: 作为研究领域的植物或动物结构
senses.example: Plant anatomy explains why stems bend toward light.
senses.exampleCN: 植物解剖学解释了茎为何向光弯曲。
senses.why: The science is not limited to people. Comparative anatomy compares species, and plant anatomy studies tissues; the same cutting-up logic applies.
senses.whyCN: 这门科学并不限于人。比较解剖学比较各物种，植物解剖学研究组织；「切开来看」的逻辑是一样的。

senses.title: Structure of an Institution
senses.titleCN: 机构的结构：组织如何构成
senses.definition: the internal structure and working parts of an organization or system
senses.definitionCN: 组织或系统的内部结构与运作部件
senses.example: The report examined the anatomy of the health service.
senses.exampleCN: 该报告考察了医疗服务体系的结构。
senses.why: Institutions have parts that can be mapped like organs. The word implies that the parts are interdependent, so a change in one shows up elsewhere.
senses.whyCN: 机构有可以像器官一样被描绘的部件；这个词暗示各部件相互依赖，因此改一处就会在别处显现。

senses.title: The Anatomy Course
senses.titleCN: 解剖学课程：作为科目的解剖
senses.definition: the subject or course taught under this name
senses.definitionCN: 以解剖学为名讲授的科目或课程
senses.example: She passed anatomy but failed physiology.
senses.exampleCN: 她解剖学通过了，生理学却没过。
senses.why: In medical schools the science becomes a subject with exams. Names of disciplines often work this way: biology is both a field and a class at nine o'clock.
senses.whyCN: 在医学院，这门科学变成有考试的科目。学科名称常如此运作：biology 既是研究领域，也是九点钟的那堂课。

intro.en: Anatomy comes from Greek anatomē 'a cutting up', from ana- 'up, throughout' and temnein 'to cut'. Latin borrowed it as anatomia, and English took it in the sixteenth century; the exact date is approximate.
intro.cn: anatomy 出自希腊 anatomē「切开」，由 ana-「向上、遍及」与 temnein「切」构成。拉丁语借作 anatomia，英语于十六世纪引入；确切年代为约数。

items.en: Temnein meant 'to cut'. From it came tomos 'a cut' and the adjective -tomos, which survives in English compounds such as appendectomy and lobotomy.
items.cn: temnein 意为「切」，由此产生 tomos「切口」与形容词 -tomos；后者在英语复合词中留存，如 appendectomy（阑尾切除术）、lobotomy（脑叶切断术）。

items.en: The same root produced atomos, 'uncuttable', from a- 'not' plus tomos. Democritus used it for the smallest indivisible piece of matter. Anatomy and atom are therefore opposites built from one verb: one cuts up, the other cannot be cut.
items.cn: 同一词根产生 atomos「不可切的」，由 a-「不」加 tomos 构成；德谟克利特用它指不可再分的最小物质。因此 anatomy 与 atom 是由同一个动词造出的反义对：一个切开，一个不可切。

items.en: Anatomē meant 'a cutting up, dissection'. Greek medicine used it for the procedure of opening a body to learn its parts, not for the parts themselves.
items.cn: anatomē 意为「切开、解剖」。希腊医学用它指打开身体以了解其部件的操作，而不是指部件本身。

items.en: Latin anatomia kept both the act and the science. Medieval and Renaissance anatomists added the sense 'the structure so revealed', which English inherited.
items.cn: 拉丁 anatomia 同时保留行为与学科两义；中世纪与文艺复兴时期的解剖学家又添上「由此揭示的结构」这一含义，英语继承了它。

items.en: From the seventeenth century English extended anatomy to the parts of anything, from a poem to a government. The metaphor survives because every whole can be taken apart.
items.cn: 自十七世纪起，英语把 anatomy 扩展到任何事物的部件，从一首诗到一个政府。这个比喻之所以存活，是因为任何整体都可以拆开。

note.en: The first group separates members of the Greek cutting family that look alike. The second holds near-synonyms for study, body and analysis.
note.cn: 第一组区分希腊「切」词族中形近的成员；第二组是表示研究、身体与分析的近义词。

entries.definition: The smallest unit of an element, named by Greek atomos 'uncuttable'. It is the exact opposite prefix to anatomy, which is about cutting up.
entries.definitionCN: 元素的最小单位，名称来自希腊 atomos「不可切的」；它的前缀恰与 anatomy「切开」相反。

entries.definition: Relating to anatomy or to body structure. It modifies nouns such as structure, position and model.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指与解剖学或身体结构有关的；修饰 structure、position、model 等名词。

entries.definition: A person who studies or practises anatomy. It names the human agent, not the field.
entries.definitionCN: 研究或从事解剖的人；命名的是人，而非领域。

entries.definition: The act of cutting something apart for study. It is the procedure, while anatomy can also be the science or the structure.
entries.definitionCN: 为研究而切开某物的行为；它是操作过程，而 anatomy 还可指学科或结构。

entries.definition: The study of how body parts work. Anatomy asks what the parts are; physiology asks what they do.
entries.definitionCN: 研究身体部件如何运作的学科；anatomy 问部件是什么，physiology 问它们做什么。

entries.definition: The study of form, especially in biology and linguistics. It is broader than anatomy and does not imply dissection.
entries.definitionCN: 研究形式的学科，尤用于生物学与语言学；比 anatomy 更宽，且不暗示解剖。

entries.definition: The way parts are put together. It is the neutral word; anatomy adds the biological or systematic flavour.
entries.definitionCN: 各部分的组合方式；是中性词，而 anatomy 增添了生物学或系统性的色彩。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ana- 'up, throughout' + temnein 'cut' + -y: the cutting-up that reveals structure.
normal.cn: ana-「向上、遍及」+ temnein「切」+ -y：揭示结构的切开。

normal.en: The family runs anatomical, anatomically, anatomist, anatomize, and the -tomy words such as appendectomy.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 anatomical、anatomically、anatomist、anatomize，以及 appendectomy 一类 -tomy 词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the use: human anatomy, comparative anatomy, plant anatomy, gross anatomy.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：人体解剖学、比较解剖学、植物解剖学、大体解剖学。

normal.en: atom is the same root with the opposite prefix: 'not cuttable' against 'cut up'.
normal.cn: atom 是同一词根加相反前缀：不可切，对比切开。

normal.en: anatomy asks what the parts are; physiology asks what they do.
normal.cn: anatomy 问部件是什么，physiology 问部件做什么。

abstract.en: Picture a watch opened on a table, every wheel laid out in order.
abstract.cn: 想象一只表在桌上被打开，每个齿轮都按顺序摆好。

abstract.en: Picture a map of a city printed as layers: roads, pipes, then power lines.
abstract.cn: 想象一张城市地图分层印出：先是道路，再是管道，然后是电线。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence taken apart word by word to see how it holds together.
abstract.cn: 想象一个句子被逐词拆开，以看清它如何组合。

examples.en: Human anatomy has changed little since the Renaissance.
examples.cn: 自文艺复兴以来，人体解剖学变化不大。

examples.en: The anatomy of a frog is often taught before that of a mammal.
examples.cn: 教学上常先讲青蛙的解剖结构，再讲哺乳动物。

examples.en: Her paper offers an anatomy of the failure rather than a remedy.
examples.cn: 她的论文对这次失败作了剖析，而没有给出补救办法。

dict_mnemonic.text: ana（向上、分开）+ tomy（切）→ 分开切开来研究 → 解剖学；身体结构

root: 希腊 ana-「向上、遍及」+ temnein「切」→ anatomē「切开、解剖」→ 拉丁 anatomia → 英语 anatomy；同根 atom 意为「不可切的」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act of cutting: the science, the structure revealed, the cutting itself, metaphorical analysis, the body in speech, plant and animal bodies, institutional structure and the school subject.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都沿着「切开」这一动作展开：学科、被揭示的结构、切割本身、比喻性的剖析、口语中的身体、动植物身体、机构结构与学校科目。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body opened layer by layer, each part labelled.
core.cn: 核心意象：一具被逐层打开、每个部件都带标签的身体。

branches.en: THE ACT AND THE SCIENCE: the physical cutting and the discipline that grew from it.
branches.cn: 动作与学科：实际的切割，以及由它生长出来的学科。

branches.en: WHAT THE CUT REVEALS: human, animal and plant bodies are described part by part.
branches.cn: 切开后所见：人、动物与植物的身体被逐部件描述。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: books, rumours and institutions can be taken apart the same way.
branches.cn: 比喻延伸：书籍、谣言与机构也能以同样方式拆解。

branches.en: THE BODY IN SPEECH: informal use lets the noun stand for the whole body.
branches.cn: 口语中的身体：非正式用法让该名词代指整个身体。

branches.en: THE SUBJECT: in medical schools the science becomes a course with examinations.
branches.cn: 科目：在医学院，这门科学变成有考试的课程。

intro.en: Anatomy is a Greek compound: a prefix of opening, the verb 'to cut', and a noun ending. English also uses the combining form -tomy for surgical cuttings.
intro.cn: anatomy 是希腊语复合词：表示打开的动词前缀、动词「切」，以及名词词尾。英语还用构词成分 -tomy 表示外科切开。

latinIntro.en: Latin anatomia came from Greek anatomē. The Latinized form supplies anatomy, anatomical, anatomist and anatomize; the Greek root tom- supplies appendectomy, tonsillectomy and lobotomy.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 anatomia 来自希腊 anatomē；拉丁化形式衍生 anatomy、anatomical、anatomist、anatomize；希腊词根 tom- 衍生 appendectomy、tonsillectomy、lobotomy。

items.meaning: a cutting up; the structure revealed
items.example: The anatomy of the insect was drawn in detail.
items.exampleCN: 这只昆虫的解剖结构被详细绘制。

items.example: The anatomical model comes apart in twelve pieces.
items.exampleCN: 这个解剖模型可拆成十二块。

items.example: The two joints are anatomically identical.
items.exampleCN: 这两个关节在结构上完全相同。

items.example: The anatomist named the muscle in 1840.
items.exampleCN: 这位解剖学家在 1840 年给该肌肉命名。

items.meaning: to dissect or analyse in detail
items.example: He anatomized the argument line by line.
items.exampleCN: 他逐行剖析了这场论证。

items.example: An atom of carbon has six protons.
items.exampleCN: 一个碳原子有六个质子。

items.structure: tomos (a cut, a slice) + English form
items.meaning: a large book, a 'slice' of writing
items.example: The library owns a rare tome on beetles.
items.exampleCN: 图书馆藏有一部罕见的甲虫专著。

items.meaning: a cutting short; a perfect summary
items.example: The small town is the epitome of quiet.
items.exampleCN: 这个小镇是宁静的缩影。

latinEntries.meaning: dissection; the science of the body

latinEntries.structure: atomus, -i (f. or m., Greek loan in Latin)

definition_zh: 使迷惑；使不知所措；使晕头转向；把……弄糊涂；使混乱
definition_en: to confuse someone completely, so they cannot think clearly or find their way
core_image: 走岔路口的旅人：路标全转了个圈，四顾茫然
scene: 列车晚点，站内的指示牌又七零八落。 The complicated map bewildered the first-time visitors.
sceneCN: 这里 bewilder 是「使迷惑、使不知所措」（第 1 个义项：令人 confused 得晕头转向）；句意是复杂的地图让初次来访的游客晕头转向。

pos.zh: 使迷惑；使晕头转向
使慌乱；使不知所措

collocations.zh: 令人眼花缭乱的一大堆

derivatives.zh: 过去分词转形容词，义为「困惑的；不知所措的」
现在分词转形容词，义为「令人困惑的；眼花缭乱的」
bewilder 加名词后缀 -ment，义为「困惑；迷乱」
基础词，义为「荒野的；狂乱的」，bewilder 由其派生

senses.title: To confuse completely
senses.definition: to make someone so confused that they cannot think or act clearly
senses.definitionCN: 使某人困惑到无法清晰思考或行动
senses.example: The complicated map bewildered the first-time visitors.
senses.exampleCN: 复杂的地图让初次来访的游客晕头转向。
senses.why: The old image is losing one's way in the wilderness, now in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 古义是在荒野中迷路，如今转为心智上的迷失。

senses.title: To leave someone at a loss
senses.definition: to make someone feel helpless because they do not know what to do
senses.definitionCN: 因不知该如何应对而令人手足无措
senses.example: She was bewildered by the sudden accusations.
senses.exampleCN: 突如其来的指责让她不知所措。
senses.why: A lost traveler stands still, unsure which step to take.
senses.whyCN: 迷途的旅人原地呆立，不知下一步迈向何处。

senses.title: To make something puzzling
senses.definition: to make a system, rule, or situation too tangled to follow
senses.definitionCN: 使制度、规则或情形盘根错节而难以理解
senses.example: A bewildering array of choices faced the buyer.
senses.exampleCN: 琳琅满目的选择令买家眼花缭乱。
senses.why: Many tangled paths make a forest bewildering.
senses.whyCN: 岔路繁多，森林便令人迷乱。

senses.title: To confuse the senses
senses.definition: to overload sight, sound, or smell so that the senses lose order
senses.definitionCN: 让视觉、听觉或嗅觉过载，感官失去条理
senses.example: The market's noise and colours bewildered his senses.
senses.exampleCN: 市场的喧嚣与色彩让他的感官应接不暇。
senses.why: The wilderness image applies to perception as well as thought.
senses.whyCN: 荒野迷路的意象同样适用于感官层面。

senses.title: To disorder or jumble
senses.definition: to throw something into confusion or disorder
senses.definitionCN: 使某物陷入混乱无序
senses.example: The contradictory reports bewildered the investigation.
senses.exampleCN: 互相矛盾的报告搅乱了调查。
senses.why: To bewilder an order is to make paths cross without signposts.
senses.whyCN: 打乱秩序，就是让路径交错而无路标可循。

senses.title: To perplex mentally
senses.definition: to puzzle someone's mind over a question or idea
senses.definitionCN: 以问题或想法难住某人的头脑
senses.example: The geometry proof bewildered the whole class.
senses.exampleCN: 这道几何证明难住了全班。
senses.why: A mind, like a traveler, can lose the logical path.
senses.whyCN: 头脑如旅人，也会在逻辑之路上迷路。

senses.title: To disorient in place
senses.definition: to make someone lose their sense of direction or place
senses.definitionCN: 使某人失去方向感或方位感
senses.example: The mirrored corridors bewildered the guests.
senses.exampleCN: 镜子迷宫般的走廊让客人们晕头转向。
senses.why: This keeps the original literal sense of wandering lost.
senses.whyCN: 此义保留了字面上「迷路」的本义。

senses.title: To stun with novelty
senses.definition: to overwhelm someone with things too new or rapid to absorb
senses.definitionCN: 以过于新奇或迅疾的事物将人淹没
senses.example: The pace of change bewildered the older workers.
senses.exampleCN: 变化的节奏令老员工目不暇接。
senses.why: When new paths appear faster than one can walk, one is lost again.
senses.whyCN: 新路出现得比脚步更快，人便再度迷失。

intro.en: Bewilder is be- plus an old verb wilder, to lead astray, from wilderness.
intro.cn: bewilder 由 be- 加古动词 wilder「使迷路」构成，wildler 源自 wilderness「荒野」。

items.en: wildēor meant wild beast; wild dēor, wild animal, the source of wilderness.
items.cn: 古英语 wildēor 意为「野兽」，wild dēor 即 wild animal，是 wilderness 的来源。

items.en: wildernesse meant a wild, pathless place where one wanders lost.
items.cn: 中古英语 wildernesse 指无路的荒野，人在其中迷途彷徨。

items.en: wilder meant to lead astray, to lure into the wilds; origin partly uncertain.
items.cn: 中古英语 wilder 意为「使迷路、引入荒野」；其来源部分不确定。

items.en: bewilder first appears meaning to lose one's way in pathless places.
items.cn: 17 世纪晚期 bewilder 首见，义为在无路之地迷失。

items.en: now chiefly figurative: to confuse the mind, the senses, or the plans.
items.cn: 如今多作比喻：使心智、感官或计划陷于迷乱。
