definition_zh: 恢复力；韧性；回弹能力
definition_en: the capacity to recover quickly from difficulties, or of a system to absorb disturbance and return to its previous state or function
core_image: 被压弯的芦苇在风停后弹回原位
scene: 洪水退去后，这片芦苇地在两个季节内恢复了原有高度与盖度，显示出很强的恢复力。 After the flood receded, this reed bed recovered its former height and cover within two seasons, showing strong resilience.
sceneCN: 这里 resilience 是「恢复力」（第 1 个义项：受扰后回到原状态的能力）；句意：洪水退去后，这片芦苇地在两个季节内恢复了原有高度与盖度，显示出很强的恢复力。

pos.zh: 恢复力；韧性；回弹能力（多作不可数）

forms.label: 复数（少见，指多种恢复力）

derivatives.zh: 弹回；撤回（法律与正式用语）

senses.title: Ecological capacity to absorb disturbance
senses.titleCN: 生态学上的吸收扰动能力
senses.definition: the capacity of an ecosystem to absorb disturbance and keep its structure and functions
senses.definitionCN: 生态系统吸收扰动并保持结构与功能的能力
senses.example: Coral reef resilience depends on herbivorous fish and clean water.
senses.exampleCN: 珊瑚礁的恢复力依赖植食性鱼类与清洁的水。
senses.why: From Latin resilire 'to leap back', resilience is the ability to be pushed and still spring back into the same shape.
senses.whyCN: 来自拉丁语 resilire「跳回」，resilience 就是被推之后仍弹回原形的能力。

senses.title: Engineering return time
senses.definition: the speed with which a system returns to equilibrium after a displacement
senses.definitionCN: 系统被推离后回到平衡的速度
senses.example: Engineering resilience measures how quickly the lake clears after a storm.
senses.exampleCN: 工程恢复力度量湖泊在风暴后多快恢复清澈。
senses.why: In engineering, resilience is a stopwatch: the faster the return, the more resilient the system. Ecology later distinguished this from the ability to absorb change at all.
senses.whyCN: 在工程学中，resilience 是秒表：回归越快，系统越有恢复力。生态学后来把它与“能否吸收变化”区分开。

senses.title: Psychological resilience
senses.definition: the capacity of a person to cope with stress, loss, or adversity and continue functioning
senses.definitionCN: 个人应对压力、丧失或逆境并继续运作的能力
senses.example: Children's resilience after displacement depended on stable caregivers.
senses.exampleCN: 流离失所后儿童的心理韧性取决于稳定的照护者。
senses.why: The physical image of springing back is applied to the mind: adversity bends a person, and resilience is the return, not the absence of bending.
senses.whyCN: 弹回的物理意象被用于心理：逆境把人压弯，resilience 是回归，而不是从未被压弯。

senses.title: Material resilience
senses.definition: the ability of a material to return to its original shape after being bent or compressed
senses.definitionCN: 材料被弯曲或压缩后恢复原形的能力
senses.example: The resilience of the reed fibres makes the mat spring back.
senses.exampleCN: 芦苇纤维的回弹性使垫子能弹回。
senses.why: This is the oldest literal layer: resiliens described something leaping back, and materials still demonstrate the original image most directly.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的字面层：resiliens 描述某物跳回，而材料至今最直接地展示这一原始意象。

senses.title: Community or social resilience
senses.definition: the capacity of a community to prepare for, respond to, and recover from shocks
senses.definitionCN: 社区准备、应对并从冲击中恢复的能力
senses.example: Neighbour networks increased the town's resilience to the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 邻里网络提高了小镇对洪水的韧性。
senses.why: The unit changes from an individual to a community; the 'springing back' now depends on social ties, infrastructure, and institutions.
senses.whyCN: 单位从个人变为社区；“弹回”现在依赖社会纽带、基础设施与制度。

senses.title: Organizational or business resilience
senses.definition: the capacity of an organization to withstand disruption and continue its core functions
senses.definitionCN: 组织承受中断并继续核心职能的能力
senses.example: Supply-chain resilience became a board-level concern after the pandemic.
senses.exampleCN: 疫情之后，供应链韧性成为董事会层面的议题。
senses.why: The collective unit changes again: an organization must keep its core functions when suppliers, staff, or systems fail.
senses.whyCN: 集体单位再次变化：当供应商、员工或系统失效时，组织必须维持核心职能。

senses.title: Resilience contrasted with resistance
senses.titleCN: 恢复力与抵抗力的对照
senses.definition: the property of recovering after change, as opposed to resisting change in the first place
senses.definitionCN: 变化后恢复的属性，与首先抵抗变化的属性相对
senses.example: A resistant forest barely changes; a resilient one changes and returns.
senses.exampleCN: 有抵抗力的森林几乎不变；有恢复力的森林会变化然后回归。
senses.why: The pair divides the labour of stability: resistance refuses the push, resilience accepts it and comes back.
senses.whyCN: 这一对概念分担了稳定性的工作：抵抗力拒绝推力，恢复力接受推力再回来。

senses.title: Resilience as a policy goal
senses.titleCN: 作为政策目标的恢复力
senses.definition: a desired capacity that governments, insurers, and planners try to measure and increase
senses.definitionCN: 政府、保险机构与规划者试图度量并提升的理想能力
senses.example: The city plan set a resilience target for heat waves.
senses.exampleCN: 城市规划为热浪设定了韧性目标。
senses.why: When a concept becomes a target, it is operationalized: indicators, audits, and budgets turn 'springing back' into something to be managed.
senses.whyCN: 当概念成为目标，它就被操作化：指标、审计与预算把“弹回”变成可管理的东西。

intro.en: Resilience comes from Latin resiliens, the present participle of resilire 'to leap back', from re- 'back' + salire 'to leap'. The same salire gives result and assault.
intro.cn: resilience 来自拉丁语 resiliens，即 resilire「跳回」的现在分词，由 re-「向后」+ salire「跳」构成。同一个 salire 还衍生 result 与 assault。

items.en: resilire 'to rebound, recoil, leap back' = re- 'back' + salire 'to leap, jump'. Its participle resiliens is the direct source of the English noun and adjective.
items.cn: resilire「弹回、反冲、跳回」= re-「向后」+ salire「跳」。其分词 resiliens 是英语名词与形容词的直接来源。

items.en: English resilience is recorded in the seventeenth century, first for the physical property of springing back.
items.cn: 英语 resilience 于 17 世纪被记录，最初指物体弹回的物理属性。

items.en: The word extended to character: a resilient person recovers from hardship as a bent rod recovers its shape.
items.cn: 该词扩展到性格：有韧性的人从困苦中恢复，正如弯曲的杆恢复形状。

items.en: Ecology adopted resilience for the capacity to absorb disturbance; C. S. Holling distinguished it from resistance and from engineering return time.
items.cn: 生态学采用 resilience 指吸收扰动的能力；Holling 把它与抵抗力和工程回归时间区分开。

items.en: Modern usage spans materials, psychology, ecology, disaster planning, and business; the noun is usually uncountable.
items.cn: 现代用法横跨材料、心理学、生态学、灾害规划与商业；该名词通常不可数。

note.en: The first group separates resilience terms, the second compares capacities under stress.
note.cn: 第一组区分恢复力术语，第二组比较压力下的能力。

entries.definition: having resilience; the adjective describes the bearer, the noun the capacity.
entries.definitionCN: 具有恢复力的；形容词描述承载者，名词描述能力。

entries.definition: an American variant of resilience, chiefly in psychology and policy writing.
entries.definitionCN: resilience 的美式变体，主要用于心理学与政策写作。

entries.definition: to spring back or withdraw, chiefly in legal usage.
entries.definitionCN: 弹回或撤回，主要用于法律语境。

entries.definition: an outcome, literally 'that which springs back'; it shares salire but not the 'recover' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 结果，字面为“弹回之物”；共享 salire，但无“恢复”义。

entries.definition: the capacity to withstand a push without being displaced.
entries.definitionCN: 承受推力而不被推离的能力。

entries.definition: the ability to keep functioning across a range of conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 在一系列条件下持续运作的能力。

entries.definition: the ability to absorb energy without breaking; it is about not failing, not about returning.
entries.definitionCN: 吸收能量而不破坏的能力；关乎不失效，而非回归。

entries.definition: the capacity to adjust to new conditions rather than return to old ones.
entries.definitionCN: 调整以适应新条件、而非回到旧状态的能力。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin leap, standard phrases, and real contrasts.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语“跳”的意象、标准搭配与真实对比。

normal.en: re- + salire: to leap back. Resilience is the leap back after being bent.
normal.cn: re- + salire：向后跳。resilience 是被压弯后的那一跳。

normal.en: Result and assault share salire: one springs back, the other leaps at.
normal.cn: result 与 assault 共享 salire：一个弹回，一个扑向。

normal.en: Resistance refuses the push; resilience takes it and returns.
normal.cn: 抵抗力拒绝推力；恢复力接受推力并回归。

normal.en: Psychological resilience is not 'never bending'; it is bending and coming back.
normal.cn: 心理韧性不是“从不弯曲”，而是弯曲后再回来。

normal.en: Engineering resilience is measured by return time; ecological resilience by the ability to absorb change.
normal.cn: 工程恢复力以回归时间度量；生态恢复力以吸收变化的能力度量。

abstract.en: Picture a reed in wind: it bends almost flat, then stands up when the gust passes. That stand-up is resilience.
abstract.cn: 想象风中的芦苇：它几乎被压平，阵风过后又立起来。这个“立起来”就是 resilience。

abstract.en: The word always implies a prior disturbance; without a push there is nothing to spring back from.
abstract.cn: 这个词总隐含先前的扰动；没有推力，就无所谓弹回。

abstract.en: A system can be resilient and still change: returning to function is not the same as returning to the exact old state.
abstract.cn: 系统可以有恢复力却仍发生变化：回到功能不等于回到完全旧状态。

examples.en: The reef's resilience declined as water temperatures rose.
examples.cn: 随着水温升高，该礁的恢复力下降。

examples.en: Community resilience depends on trust as much as on concrete barriers.
examples.cn: 社区韧性既依赖混凝土屏障，也依赖信任。

examples.en: Engineers measure resilience as the time a network needs to recover.
examples.cn: 工程师把恢复力度量为一个网络恢复所需的时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: “瑞贼连斯”——被压弯了还能连着弹回来 → resilience 恢复力、韧性

root: 拉丁语 resilire「跳回」，re-（向后）+ salire（跳）；同根词有 result、assault、salient。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of resilience: ecological absorption, engineering return time, psychological coping, material spring-back, community and organizational capacity, the contrast with resistance, and the same capacity used as a policy target.
sensesIntro.cn: resilience 的八个义项：生态吸收、工程回归时间、心理应对、材料回弹、社区与组织能力、与抵抗力的对照，以及作为政策目标的同一能力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bent reed springs upright when the wind stops.
core.cn: 核心意象：被压弯的芦苇在风停后弹直。

branches.en: ECOLOGY: the capacity to absorb disturbance and keep the same relationships.
branches.cn: 生态学：吸收扰动并保持原有关系格局的能力。

branches.en: CONTRAST: resilience is coming back, resistance is not moving at all.
branches.cn: 对照：恢复力是回到原状，抵抗力是根本不被推动。

branches.en: ENGINEERING: the stopwatch version, measured as return time.
branches.cn: 工程学：用秒表计时的版本，以回归时间度量。

branches.en: PERSON AND MATERIAL: minds and fibres both bend and come back.
branches.cn: 人与材料：心理与纤维都会弯曲再回弹。

branches.en: COLLECTIVE AND POLICY: communities, firms, and governments turn resilience into a target.
branches.cn: 集体与政策：社区、企业与政府把恢复力变成目标。

intro.en: Resilience is Latin re- + salire plus the noun suffix -ence. English also forms resilient, resile, and the variant resiliency; salire is a bound Latin stem.
intro.cn: resilience 是拉丁语 re- + salire 加名词后缀 -ence。英语还构成 resilient、resile 与变体 resiliency；salire 是黏着拉丁词干。

latinIntro.en: Latin salire 'to leap' yields resilient, resilience, resile, result, assault, and salient; the re- prefix marks a backward direction in the resilient branch.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 salire「跳」衍生 resilient、resilience、resile、result、assault、salient；re- 前缀在 resilient 一支标记向后方向。

items.example: The reed bed shows resilience.
items.exampleCN: 芦苇地表现出恢复力。

items.meaningCN: 弹回的；有韧性的（-ent 形容词）
items.example: Resilient crops survive drought.
items.exampleCN: 有韧性的作物能熬过干旱。

items.example: The town recovered resiliently.
items.exampleCN: 小镇有韧性地恢复了。

items.example: The report measured resiliency.
items.exampleCN: 报告测量了韧性。

items.example: The contract resiled to earlier terms.
items.exampleCN: 合同回退到先前条款。

items.meaning: that which springs back; an outcome
items.example: The result followed the cause.
items.exampleCN: 结果随原因而来。

items.example: The storm assaulted the coast.
items.exampleCN: 风暴猛扑海岸。

items.example: The salient ridge stands out.
items.exampleCN: 显著的山脊很突出。

definition_zh: 教师；（常含贬义）卖弄学问的教书匠；历史上指护送男孩上学的家奴
definition_en: a teacher, often one who is pedantic; historically a household slave who escorted a boy to school
core_image: 一个年长的仆人提着灯，走在前头，把男孩送到学堂门口，然后等在墙外
scene: 古罗马的家庭里，一名受过教育的奴仆每天清晨提着灯，把孩子送到学堂再回家。 In a Roman household, a pedagogue walked the boy to school each morning and waited outside.
sceneCN: 这里 pedagogue 指历史上负责护送并照看男孩的家奴（第 5 个义项：古代护送男孩上学的家仆）；句意为在古罗马家庭中，一名教仆每天早晨把孩子送到学校并在外面等候。

pos.zh: 教师；教书先生（较正式，也可带轻蔑）
（历史）古代护送男孩上学的家奴

derivatives.zh: 教育学；教学法（由希腊语 paidagogia「照看男孩」经拉丁与法语进入英语）
教学法的（由 pedagogy 的词干加表示「属于」的希腊后缀构成）
教学法的（由 pedagogic 加表示「属于」的英语后缀构成）
从教学法角度（由 pedagogical 加表示「方式」的后缀构成）
教学法研究（由 pedagogic 加表示「学问」的后缀构成）

senses.title: A schoolmaster
senses.definition: a teacher, especially an old-fashioned or formal name for a schoolmaster
senses.definitionCN: 教师，尤指旧式或正式的校长、教书先生称呼
senses.example: The village pedagogue taught every child in one room.
senses.exampleCN: 村里的教书先生在一间屋里教所有孩子。
senses.why: This is the oldest English sense after the word entered from Latin: the person in charge of teaching.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词从拉丁语进入英语后最古老的义：负责教学的人。

senses.title: A pedantic teacher
senses.definition: a teacher who insists on formal rules and displays learning rather than helping students learn
senses.definitionCN: 坚持形式规则、炫耀学问而不帮助学生学习的教师
senses.example: The new head was a pedagogue who corrected visitors' grammar.
senses.exampleCN: 新校长是个教书匠，连来访者的语法都要纠正。
senses.why: The word acquired a sneer: teaching that becomes showing off turns the title into an insult.
senses.whyCN: 这个词带上了讥讽：当教学变成炫耀，这个称号就变成侮辱。

senses.title: A college teacher
senses.definition: a formal or literary word for a teacher at a college or university
senses.definitionCN: 对学院或大学教师的正式或书面称呼
senses.example: The committee included a pedagogue from the medical school.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会包括一位来自医学院的教师。
senses.why: In elevated prose the word can still name the profession without any sneer.
senses.whyCN: 在正式书面语中，这个词仍可中性地命名这一职业。

senses.title: An educational thinker or writer
senses.definition: a person who writes about teaching and learning rather than only practising it
senses.definitionCN: 写作论述教学与学习、而不只是实践的人
senses.example: The old pedagogue's essays were read long after his school closed.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老教育家的文章在他学校关闭很久后仍被阅读。
senses.why: Writing about teaching extends the person-word from the classroom to the study.
senses.whyCN: 写作论述教学把这个指人的词从教室延伸到书房。

senses.title: The ancient slave escort
senses.definition: the household slave in ancient Greece who walked a boy to school, carried his things and supervised him
senses.definitionCN: 古希腊负责送男孩上学、拿东西并照看他的家奴
senses.example: In a Roman household, a pedagogue walked the boy to school each morning and waited outside.
senses.exampleCN: 在古罗马家庭中，一名教仆每天早晨把孩子送到学校并在外面等候。
senses.why: The original Greek word named this servant, so the modern teacher sense is a later promotion of the escort.
senses.whyCN: 最初的希腊词命名这名仆役，因此现代教师义是这一护送者身份后来的升格。

senses.title: A drillmaster
senses.definition: a person who drills others in a routine, often with little concern for understanding
senses.definitionCN: 让人反复操练一套程序、常不顾理解的人
senses.example: The choir's pedagogue drilled the same phrase for an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 合唱团的教练把同一乐句练了一个小时。
senses.why: When teaching is reduced to repetition, the word slides from instructor to drillmaster.
senses.whyCN: 当教学被缩减为重复，这个词就从教师滑向操练者。

senses.title: A symbol of educational authority
senses.definition: a figure who stands for the authority of the school over the learner
senses.definitionCN: 代表学校对学习者拥有权威的形象
senses.example: In the novel, the pedagogue is a figure of fear rather than help.
senses.exampleCN: 在这部小说里，教师是令人畏惧而非助人的形象。
senses.why: Literature uses the word as a type, so it can name an office rather than a particular person.
senses.whyCN: 文学把这个词当作类型使用，因此它可以命名一种职位，而非特定个人。

senses.title: Abstract: anyone who leads a learner
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：任何引导学习者的人
senses.definition: any person who takes charge of leading someone toward knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 任何负责把某人引向知识的人
senses.example: Every good editor is something of a pedagogue.
senses.exampleCN: 每个好编辑都有点像教师。
senses.why: At its widest the word returns to the Greek image of leading, without the school or the sneer.
senses.whyCN: 推到最宽处，这个词回到希腊语的「引导」意象，既无学校，也无讥讽。

intro.en: Pedagogue comes from Greek paidagogos, 'the slave who led a boy to school', built on pais 'child' and agein 'to lead', through Latin paedagogus. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: pedagogue 来自希腊语 paidagogos「送男孩上学的家奴」，由 pais「孩子」与 agein「引导」构成，经拉丁 paedagogus 进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Pais, stem paid-, meant 'child, boy'. The same stem is behind pediatrics and pedagogy.
items.cn: pais 的词干是 paid-，意为「孩子、男孩」。同一词干也构成 pediatrics 与 pedagogy。

items.en: Agein meant 'to lead, drive'. It supplies the guiding half of the compound.
items.cn: agein 意为「引导、驱赶」。它提供这个复合词中「引导」的一半。

items.en: Paidagogos was the household slave who escorted a boy to school, carried his books and watched him on the way.
items.cn: paidagogos 是护送男孩上学、拿书本并沿途照看的家奴。

items.en: Latin borrowed paedagogus, keeping the servant sense and also using it for a teacher or tutor.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 paedagogus，保留仆役义，也用它指教师或导师。

items.en: English pedagogue is recorded from the sixteenth century, first as a schoolmaster and later as a learned teacher.
items.cn: 英语 pedagogue 自十六世纪有记录，先指校长或教师，后指有学问的教书人。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the sneering sense of a pedantic teacher developed later and is generally dated to the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：指卖弄学问的教师这一讥讽义后来才出现，一般认为在十九世纪。

note.en: Group one separates the person from the field and its adjectives, and from two Greek look-alikes; group two holds the neutral names for a teacher.
note.cn: 第一组把人称词与领域词、形容词分开，并区分两个希腊语形近词；第二组是教师的中性名称。

entries.definition: The theory or practice of teaching, not the person who teaches.
entries.definitionCN: 教学的理论或实践，不是教书的人。

entries.definition: Relating to teaching methods; a pedagogue is the person, pedagogical is the manner.
entries.definitionCN: 与教学方法有关；pedagogue 是人，pedagogical 是方式。

entries.definition: From dēmos 'people' plus agogos 'leader': a leader who appeals to a crowd's emotions. It shares the leader half, not the child half.
entries.definitionCN: 由 dēmos「人民」加 agogos「引导者」构成：诉诸人群情绪的领袖。它共享「引导者」一半，不共享「孩子」一半。

entries.definition: A person who displays book learning; it may be connected through French and Italian to pedagogue, but the link is not certain.
entries.definitionCN: 炫耀书本学问的人；它可能经法语与意大利语与 pedagogue 有关，但这一联系并不确定。

entries.definition: The plain name for a person who teaches; pedagogue is more formal and can sound old-fashioned or scornful.
entries.definitionCN: 教人者的朴素名称；pedagogue 更正式，也可能显得旧式或轻蔑。

entries.definition: A formal name for a teaching professional; it does not carry the sneer that pedagogue can carry.
entries.definitionCN: 对教育专业人员的正式称呼；不带 pedagogue 可能带的讥讽。

entries.definition: A person who instructs in a skill or course; it is practical and neutral.
entries.definitionCN: 在技能或课程中指导的人；实用而中性。

entries.definition: An old-fashioned word for a male teacher or head of a school; it overlaps with the first sense of pedagogue.
entries.definitionCN: 对男教师或校长的旧式称呼；与 pedagogue 的第一个义项重叠。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real Greek words and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的希腊词与真实的同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Pais means child and agein means lead, so the pedagogue was the one who led the child.
normal.cn: pais 意为孩子，agein 意为引导，所以 pedagogue 就是引导孩子的人。

normal.en: The original pedagogue was a slave, not a professor: the word began with feet on the road.
normal.cn: 最初的 pedagogue 是家奴，不是教授：这个词开始于走在路上的脚。

normal.en: Fixed phrases carry the tone: a strict pedagogue, a pedantic pedagogue, a progressive pedagogue.
normal.cn: 固定说法带着语气：严厉的教师、卖弄学问的教书匠、主张进步的教师。

normal.en: Pedagogy is the field and pedagogical the adjective, but pedagogue is only the person.
normal.cn: pedagogy 是领域，pedagogical 是形容词，而 pedagogue 只指人。

normal.en: Demagogue shares the leader half, so it means a leader of people, not of children.
normal.cn: demagogue 共享「引导者」一半，所以它指引导人民的人，而非孩子。

abstract.en: Picture an old servant carrying a lamp ahead of a boy on a dark road.
abstract.cn: 想象一个老仆提着灯，走在男孩前面的暗路上。

abstract.en: Picture a teacher who corrects a visitor's grammar before saying hello.
abstract.cn: 想象一位教师先纠正来访者的语法，再打招呼。

abstract.en: Picture a schoolroom where one figure stands at the front and everyone else listens.
abstract.cn: 想象一间教室，一个人站在前面，其余人都在听。

examples.en: The old pedagogue knew every family in the valley by name.
examples.cn: 那位老教师能叫出河谷里每一户人家的名字。

examples.en: Critics called him a pedagogue rather than a thinker.
examples.cn: 批评者称他是教书匠，而非思想家。

examples.en: In the ancient household, the pedagogue carried the boy's books and walked behind him.
examples.cn: 在古代家庭里，教仆拿着男孩的书，走在他后面。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派达 够格」——提灯送孩子上学的老仆人 → 教师、教书匠

root: 希腊 paidagogos「送男孩上学的家奴」= pais「孩子」+ agein「引导」；经拉丁 paedagogus 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with the schoolmaster, then move to the pedantic teacher, the college teacher, the educational writer, the ancient slave escort, the drillmaster, the symbol of authority and finally anyone who leads a learner.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从教书先生出发，转到卖弄学问的教师、大学教师、教育著作家、古代教仆、操练者、权威象征，最后是任何引导学习者的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old servant with a lamp walks a boy to school and waits outside the wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个提着灯的老仆把男孩送到学堂，然后在墙外等候。

branches.en: THE TITLE: the schoolmaster and the college teacher, neutral names for the person.
branches.cn: 称号：中小学教师与大学教师，都是对人的中性称呼。

branches.en: THE SNEER AND THE DRILL: showing off learning, then reducing teaching to repetition.
branches.cn: 讥讽与操练：先是炫耀学问，再把教学缩减为重复。

branches.en: WRITER AND SYMBOL: the person who writes about teaching, and the figure who stands for school authority.
branches.cn: 作者与象征：写教学的人，以及代表学校权威的形象。

branches.en: THE ORIGINAL ESCORT: the slave who walked the boy and carried his books.
branches.cn: 最初的护送者：走在一旁、拿着书本的家奴。

branches.en: THE LEADER OF A LEARNER: the widest reading returns to the Greek image of guiding.
branches.cn: 学习者的引导者：最宽的读法回到希腊语的引导意象。

intro.en: Pedagogue is the Greek compound of a child and a leader, carried into English through Latin.
intro.cn: pedagogue 是希腊语中「孩子」与「引导者」的复合词，经拉丁语进入英语。

latinIntro.en: Greek pais and agein give paidagogos; Latin paedagogus gives English pedagogue, while the field word adds pedagogy and pedagogical.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 pais 与 agein 构成 paidagogos；拉丁 paedagogus 衍生英语 pedagogue，领域词再加 pedagogy 与 pedagogical。

items.exampleCN: 第一个成分命名学习者。

items.example: The second element names the leading.

items.exampleCN: 最初的复合词命名仆役。

items.example: English narrowed it to the teacher.
items.exampleCN: 英语把它收窄到教师。

items.example: The field word is a later formation.

definition_zh: 限于；局限于；被限定在……范围内（多指由规则、权限或条件人为设限）
definition_en: to be kept within a fixed limit of place, number, group, subject or use, usually by a rule
core_image: 古籍阅览室门口立着牌子，只有持介绍信的研究者才能进，其余读者在门外等候
scene: 图书馆把古籍阅览室单独隔开，门口的登记簿只写研究者的名字，其他读者在门外等候。 Access to the rare book room can be restricted to researchers who bring a written permit.
sceneCN: 这里指入室权限被规定只给一类人（第 4 个义项：使用权限限于特定人群）；句意为进入古籍阅览室可能被限定为须持书面许可的研究者。图中可辨识物件：隔开的阅览室、门口的牌子、登记簿、门外等候的读者。

pos.zh: （固定搭配）限于；局限于；被限定在……范围

collocations.phrase: be restricted to a maximum of

senses.title: Confined to a place
senses.definition: to be allowed or found only in a stated area
senses.definitionCN: 指只被允许存在于或被见于某个特定区域
senses.example: The study can be restricted to the northern half of the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究可以只限于山谷的北半部。
senses.why: The word began with binding tight, and a place limit is the simplest kind of binding.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本义是「勒紧」，地域限制就是最朴素的一种勒紧。

senses.title: Capped at a number
senses.definition: to be kept at or below a stated figure
senses.definitionCN: 指被保持在某一数字或其以下
senses.example: The guest list can be restricted to forty names for the small hall.
senses.exampleCN: 由于礼堂较小，来宾名单可以限于四十人。
senses.why: A number limit is a fence around quantity, and the same phrase serves it without changing shape.
senses.whyCN: 数量限制是给「多少」围一道栅栏，同一个短语不必变形就能承担。

senses.title: Limited by authority
senses.definition: to have one's powers or access held within set bounds
senses.definitionCN: 指权力或接触范围被限制在规定界限内
senses.example: The clerk's access can be restricted to the first two floors of the archive.
senses.exampleCN: 这位职员的权限可以限于档案楼的前两层。
senses.why: Authority is the usual fence-builder: someone decides where the line falls.
senses.whyCN: 权限是最常见的栅栏建造者：总有人决定线画在哪里。

senses.title: Open only to a group
senses.definition: to be available only to a stated class of people
senses.definitionCN: 指只对某一类人开放
senses.example: The workshop can be restricted to students who have finished the first course.
senses.exampleCN: 工作坊可以只限修完第一门课的学生参加。
senses.why: Groups are bounded by a condition, and the phrase turns membership into a gate.
senses.whyCN: 群体由条件划界，这个短语把「成员资格」变成一道门。

senses.title: Confined to a subject
senses.definition: to keep discussion or content within a stated subject
senses.definitionCN: 指把讨论或内容限定在某个题目之内
senses.example: The debate can be restricted to the question of cost for the first hour.
senses.exampleCN: 第一个小时的辩论可以只限于成本问题。
senses.why: Subjects can be fenced as easily as fields, which is why the phrase suits meetings.
senses.whyCN: 题目也像田地一样可以围起来，所以这个短语适用于会议。

senses.title: A species held to a range
senses.definition: to exist naturally only within a particular habitat or region
senses.definitionCN: 指在自然界只存在于特定栖息地或区域
senses.example: This bird can be restricted to a single mountain range in the south.
senses.exampleCN: 这种鸟可能只限于南方的某一条山脉。
senses.why: Biology uses the word for a natural fence, even when no one built it.
senses.whyCN: 生物学用它指天然的栅栏，即使并没有人去建。

senses.title: A reading held narrow
senses.definition: to be understood only in a narrow stated way
senses.definitionCN: 指只能按某一种狭窄的意思理解
senses.example: The clause can be restricted to cases where the damage was reported at once.
senses.exampleCN: 这条可以只限于损坏被立即报告的情形。
senses.why: Here the limit is on meaning, and the word shows that interpretation can be fenced too.
senses.whyCN: 这里的限制落在意思上，说明解释同样可以围起来。

senses.title: A rule that forbids expansion
senses.definition: to be forbidden by rule from growing beyond a fixed limit
senses.definitionCN: 指按规则被禁止超出既定界限
senses.example: Building height can be restricted to five floors along the old street.
senses.exampleCN: 老城街沿线的建筑高度可以限于五层。
senses.why: Law is the most explicit builder of limits, and the phrase carries that official force.
senses.whyCN: 法律是最明确的设限者，这个短语带着那种官方力量。

intro.en: Restricted comes from Latin restrictus, the past participle of restringere, to bind back, from re- and stringere, to bind or draw tight. English took the verb in the sixteenth century. The same stringere gives strict, stringent and constrict, while limited comes from a different word, limes, a boundary.
intro.cn: restricted 出自拉丁语 restrictus，即 restringere 的过去分词，意为「往回束紧」，由 re- 与 stringere「束紧」构成。英语十六世纪借入这个动词。同一个 stringere 还给出 strict、stringent、constrict，而 limited 出自另一个词 limes「边界」。

items.en: Stringere meant to bind, draw tight or touch lightly, and it is the root of several words of tightening.
items.cn: stringere 意为束紧、拉紧或轻触，是好几个表示「收紧」的词根。

items.en: Re- plus stringere gave restringere, to bind back, hence to confine.
items.cn: re- 与 stringere 合成 restringere「往回束紧」，由此引申为限制。

items.en: The past participle restrictus meant bound or confined, and English formed the adjective from it.
items.cn: 过去分词 restrictus 意为被束住的、被限制的，英语由此构成形容词。

items.en: The verb entered English as a word of binding and confinement before it spread to rules and rights.
items.cn: 这个动词进入英语时是「束住、关住」的意思，之后才扩及规则与权利。

items.en: Limited comes from limes, a boundary, and simply states a bound; restricted adds the idea that someone drew it.
items.cn: limited 出自 limes「边界」，只陈述有界限；restricted 则多一层「有人画了这条线」。

note.en: The first group shares the binding root; the second group names neighbouring ideas of boundaries and confinement.
note.cn: 第一组共享「束紧」词根；第二组是与「边界、关限」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The active verb meaning to keep within limits.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某物保持在限度内的主动动词。

entries.definition: A rule or condition that limits something.
entries.definitionCN: 指限制某物的规则或条件。

entries.definition: Serving to limit, often used of clauses and rules.
entries.definitionCN: 指起限制作用的，多用于从句与规则。

entries.definition: Severe or exact, from the same binding verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指严厉或精确，同出「束紧」动词。

entries.definition: To squeeze or narrow, a physical tightening.
entries.definitionCN: 指压缩或收窄，是物理性的收紧。

entries.definition: To be kept within a bound, without implying who set it.
entries.definitionCN: 指被保持在界限内，不暗示由谁设定。

entries.definition: To be shut within a space or range, often physically.
entries.definitionCN: 指被关在某一空间或范围内，多指物理。

entries.definition: To have an upper limit fixed, usually a number.
entries.definitionCN: 指上限被固定，多用于数字。

entries.definition: To be valid for a stated group and no other.
entries.definitionCN: 指只对某一特定群体有效。

entries.definition: To be tied or obliged, from the same binding idea.
entries.definitionCN: 指被绑定或负有义务，同出「束」的意思。

entries.definition: To be kept for a particular person or use.
entries.definitionCN: 指专为某人或某用途保留。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the picture of pulling a rope tight, the strict family, and the contrast with the plainer word limited.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用「把绳子往回拉紧」的画面、「严格」这一族词，以及和更平实的「有限」一词的对照来记。

normal.en: Stringere is to draw tight, so restricted is a rope pulled back around a space.
normal.cn: stringere 是「拉紧」，所以 restricted 就是一根把空间往回围住的绳。

normal.en: Strict, stringent and constrict come from the same rope, so the family feels tight.
normal.cn: strict、stringent、constrict 都出自同一根绳，所以这一族词都带「紧」感。

normal.en: Restricted usually means someone set the limit; limited just says a limit exists.
normal.cn: restricted 通常意味着有人设了限；limited 只说存在界限。

normal.en: To marks the only place, group or use that is still allowed.
normal.cn: to 后面标出仍然被允许的那一个地点、群体或用途。

normal.en: A rare book room with a locked door is the picture to keep.
normal.cn: 一间上锁的古籍阅览室，就是该记住的画面。

abstract.en: Every fence defines a field as much as it excludes a walker.
abstract.cn: 每道栅栏在排除行人的同时，也定义了一块田地。

abstract.en: Restriction is power made visible: someone decided where the line falls.
abstract.cn: 限制是可见的权力：有人决定了线画在哪里。

abstract.en: A narrow reading is a fence built around meaning, and it can be as tight as any wall.
abstract.cn: 狭窄的解释是围着意义建的栅栏，可以像墙一样紧。

examples.en: The survey can be restricted to households in the inner city.
examples.cn: 这项调查可以只限于内城的住户。

examples.en: Entry can be restricted to people on the official list.
examples.cn: 入场可以只限名单上的人。

examples.en: The discussion can be restricted to the first two proposals.
examples.cn: 讨论可以只限于前两份提案。

definition_zh: 区分；分化；差异化；（数学）微分；分层
definition_en: the act of telling things apart, the process by which things become unlike, or the mathematical operation of finding a derivative
core_image: 一条原本同质的线分成两支：细胞、产品、课程各自长出不同的形状
scene: 显微镜下，一个细胞分裂成两个形状不同的细胞。 Under the microscope one cell divides into two cells of different shapes, and the observer writes differentiation in the notebook.
sceneCN: 这里 differentiation 是「细胞分化」（第 3 个义项：生物学上细胞变为不同形态与功能）；句意：显微镜下，一个细胞分裂成两个形状不同的细胞，观察者在记录本上写下「分化」。图中可辨识物件：显微镜、培养皿、两支不同形状的细胞、记录本。

pos.zh: 区分；分化；差异化；微分

collocations.zh: A 与 B 之间的区分

senses.title: Telling two things apart
senses.definition: the act of recognizing or stating the difference between two or more things
senses.definitionCN: 识别或说明两个或更多事物之间差别的行为
senses.example: The test rewards fine differentiation between closely related species.
senses.exampleCN: 这项测试奖励对近缘物种的精细区分。
senses.why: The Latin verb differre meant 'to carry apart'. Differentiation is the mental act of carrying two things apart until the gap between them is visible.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词 differre 意为“分开搬运”。differentiation 就是把两样东西在头脑中搬开、直到它们之间的缝隙看得见的行为。

senses.title: The process of becoming unlike
senses.definition: the process by which something develops qualities that separate it from others of its kind
senses.definitionCN: 某物发展出使其区别于同类之特性的过程
senses.example: Regional dialects show gradual differentiation over centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 地区方言在数百年间逐渐分化。
senses.why: Here the word names a process rather than an act of judgment. Two things start alike and drift apart; the -ation suffix makes the drift itself the noun.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词命名的不是判断行为，而是一个过程。两样东西起初相似，慢慢漂开；-ation 后缀使这段漂移本身成为名词。

senses.title: Cells taking on special roles
senses.definition: in biology, the process by which a less specialized cell becomes a distinct cell type
senses.definitionCN: 生物学中未特化的细胞变成特定细胞类型的过程
senses.example: Stem cell differentiation produces muscle, nerve and bone cells.
senses.exampleCN: 干细胞分化产生肌肉、神经与骨细胞。
senses.why: A stem cell carries the same instructions as every other cell. Differentiation is what carries one copy of those instructions down a single path, so the cell stops being interchangeable.
senses.whyCN: 干细胞携带的指令与其他细胞相同。分化就是把其中一份指令搬上一条特定路径，使这个细胞不再可互换。

senses.title: Making a product stand out
senses.definition: in marketing, the design of a product or brand so that buyers perceive it as distinct from rivals
senses.definitionCN: 营销中把产品或品牌设计得让买家觉得它不同于竞争者
senses.example: The firm relies on differentiation rather than low prices.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司靠差异化而非低价取胜。
senses.why: The verb differre also means 'to defer, to set apart'. A marketer sets a product apart from the shelf around it, and the noun names that deliberate setting-apart.
senses.whyCN: 动词 differre 也有“推迟、置于一旁”的意思。营销者把产品从四周的货架上“置开”，这个名词就命名这种刻意的分离。

senses.title: Teaching different levels in one class
senses.definition: in education, the adaptation of tasks and materials to learners of different readiness levels
senses.definitionCN: 教育中为不同准备水平的学习者调整任务与材料
senses.example: Curriculum differentiation lets advanced students move ahead.
senses.exampleCN: 分层课程让进度快的学生继续向前。
senses.why: A single class is treated as a set of groups rather than one mass. The word transfers the biological image of branching paths into the classroom.
senses.whyCN: 一个班级被当作一组组人，而不是一团人。这个词把生物学的“分岔路径”意象搬进了课堂。

senses.title: The derivative in calculus
senses.definition: in mathematics, the operation of finding the rate at which a function changes
senses.definitionCN: 数学中求函数变化率的运算
senses.example: Differentiation of that curve gives its slope at every point.
senses.exampleCN: 对那条曲线求微分，就得到它在每一点的斜率。
senses.why: A difference is a gap between two values. Differentiation shrinks that gap toward zero and asks what ratio survives; the word keeps the original 'difference' at its centre.
senses.whyCN: difference 是两个值之间的间隙。微分把这个间隙缩到趋近于零，再看还剩下什么比值；这个词的中心始终是“差”。

senses.title: Magma splitting into rock types
senses.definition: in geology, the process by which a single magma body separates into chemically distinct melts or rocks
senses.definitionCN: 地质学中单一岩浆体分离成化学成分不同的熔体或岩石的过程
senses.example: Magmatic differentiation explains why one volcano erupts several rock types.
senses.exampleCN: 岩浆分异解释了一座火山为何喷出多种岩石。
senses.why: One parent melt is carried apart into several fractions as minerals crystallize out. The geological sense is the laboratory version of 'becoming unlike'.
senses.whyCN: 一个母岩浆随着矿物结晶被“搬成”几个部分。这个地质义就是“变得不同”在实验室里的版本。

senses.title: Society splitting into roles
senses.definition: in sociology, the division of a society into groups and roles with distinct functions
senses.definitionCN: 社会学中社会分成功能不同的群体与角色的过程
senses.example: Urban growth brought sharper social differentiation.
senses.exampleCN: 城市增长带来更明显的社会分化。
senses.why: Modern societies do not do the same work with the same people. Differentiation names the branching of tasks, and with it the branching of identities.
senses.whyCN: 现代社会不再由同一批人做同样的工作。differentiation 命名的是任务的不断分岔，以及随之而来的身份分岔。

senses.title: Parts specializing inside a system
senses.definition: in systems theory and organization, the specialization of parts that once performed a common function
senses.definitionCN: 系统论与组织理论中原本承担共同功能的各部分走向专门化
senses.example: Biological and organizational systems both gain efficiency through differentiation.
senses.exampleCN: 生物系统与组织系统都通过功能分化提高效率。
senses.why: The counterpart of integration: a system splits into specialized parts that must then be coordinated. The word here measures internal specialization, not difference from outsiders.
senses.whyCN: 它是 integration（整合）的对立面：系统分裂成专门化的部分，随后必须被协调。这里的词衡量的是内部分工，而不是与外部者的差异。

intro.en: Differentiation is a Latin verb plus a Latin noun suffix: differre 'to carry apart', its noun differentia 'a difference', the verb differentiate, and finally -ation. English took the verb from French in the 19th century and built the noun on top of it.
intro.cn: differentiation 是拉丁动词加拉丁名词后缀：differre“分开搬运”，其名词 differentia“差异”，动词 differentiate，最后加 -ation。英语在 19 世纪从法语借入动词，再在其上造出名词。

items.en: The root *bher- meant 'to carry'. It supplies Latin ferre and English bear, and it is the second half of differre, 'to carry apart'.
items.cn: 词根 *bher- 意为“携带”。它给出拉丁语 ferre 与英语 bear，也是 differre“分开搬运”的后半部分。

items.en: Dis- 'apart' plus ferre 'carry' gave differre, 'to carry apart, to differ, to defer'. Its noun differentia named a difference, and the adjective differens named 'different'.
items.cn: dis-“分开”加 ferre“搬运”构成 differre，意为“搬开、相异、推迟”。其名词 differentia 指差异，形容词 differens 指“不同的”。

items.en: The suffix -atio built process nouns from verbs, as in formatio and creatio. Attached to a Latin-derived verb, it yields an English -ation noun naming the process or its result.
items.cn: 后缀 -atio 从动词造出过程名词，如 formatio、creatio。加在拉丁来源的动词上，就得到英语的 -ation 名词，指过程或其结果。

items.en: Old French differencier carried the verb into Middle English as differencien. The noun differentiation appears later, modelled directly on Latin differentia plus -ation.
items.cn: 古法语 differencier 把动词带入中古英语作 differencien。名词 differentiation 出现得更晚，直接仿照拉丁 differentia 加 -ation 构成。

items.en: Calculus gave the word its technical sense: differentiation is the operation inverse to integration. The term spread from French and German textbooks into English in the early 19th century.
items.cn: 微积分赋予这个词技术义：differentiation 是 integration 的逆运算。该术语在 19 世纪初从法语与德语教材传入英语。

items.en: Cell differentiation and social differentiation extend the same image of branching to tissues and to societies. The word now covers both a judgement and a natural process.
items.cn: 细胞分化与社会分化把同一“分岔”意象扩展到组织与社会。这个词现在同时覆盖判断行为与自然过程。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the verb, the adjective and the noun that all sit on the same Latin base. The meaning group compares words about difference, separation and specialization.
note.cn: 形近组区分同一拉丁词基上的动词、形容词与名词；词义组比较表示差异、分离与专门化的词。

entries.definition: to tell apart, to make different, or to find a derivative. It is the verb that lies behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 区分、使不同或求导。它是名词背后的动词。

entries.definition: the state of being unlike, or the amount by which two numbers differ. It names the gap, not the process of making one.
entries.definitionCN: 不同的状态，或两数相差的量。它指缝隙本身，而不是制造缝隙的过程。

entries.definition: relating to a difference, or a small amount by which values change. In maths it is the infinitesimal increment.
entries.definitionCN: 与差异有关的，或数值变化的微小量。数学中指无穷小增量。

entries.definition: a difference explicitly recognized or a mark of quality. It stresses the line drawn, while differentiation stresses the process of drawing it.
entries.definitionCN: 被明确认识到的差别，或优异的标志。它强调画出的那条线，而 differentiation 强调画线的过程。

entries.definition: the act of concentrating on one field or function. It is the result of differentiation in biology and in organizations.
entries.definitionCN: 集中于某一领域或功能的行为。它是生物学与组织中分化的结果。

entries.definition: the process of separating and going in different directions. It describes the paths, while differentiation describes the emerging difference.
entries.definitionCN: 分开并朝不同方向发展的过程。它描述路径，而 differentiation 描述显现出的差异。

entries.definition: the ability to see fine differences, or unfair treatment. It is close to sense 01 but carries a social judgement.
entries.definitionCN: 看出细微差别的能力，或指不公平对待。它接近第 1 义项，但带有社会判断。

normalIntro.en: These hooks build the word from differre, 'carry apart', and let the branching image cover cells, products and courses.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩从 differre“分开搬运”搭起这个词，再用分岔意象覆盖细胞、产品与课程。

normal.en: See dis- + ferre: to carry apart. Differentiation is the carrying-apart made into a noun.
normal.cn: 看见 dis- 加 ferre：分开搬运。differentiation 就是“搬开”这个动作变成名词。

normal.en: Picture one stem splitting into two branches: biology calls that cell differentiation.
normal.cn: 想象一根主干分成两枝：生物学把这叫细胞分化。

normal.en: In marketing, the same split happens on a shelf: your product takes its own branch.
normal.cn: 在营销中，同一种分岔发生在货架上：你的产品长出自己的一枝。

normal.en: Connect the maths sense to difference: a derivative measures how fast one value differs from the next.
normal.cn: 把数学义连到 difference：导数衡量一个值相对下一个值变化多快。

normal.en: Remember the pair: differentiation splits, integration joins.
normal.cn: 记住这一对：differentiation 拆开，integration 合拢。

abstract.en: Keep one shape in mind: a single trunk becoming a tree of distinct branches. Every sense is that shape.
abstract.cn: 只记一个形状：一根主干长成一棵分叉的树。每个义项都是这个形状。

abstract.en: Treat the word as a verb of distance: things are carried apart until each has its own name.
abstract.cn: 把这个词当作“距离的动词”：东西被搬开，直到每样都有自己的名字。

abstract.en: Notice that the noun never fully loses 'difference': even calculus is still measuring a gap.
abstract.cn: 注意这个名词从未丢掉“difference”：连微积分也仍在测量一个间隙。

examples.en: Careful differentiation between the two hypotheses is essential.
examples.cn: 对这两个假说作出仔细区分至关重要。

examples.en: Cell differentiation turns a single fertilized egg into a whole organism.
examples.cn: 细胞分化把一个受精卵变成完整的生物体。

examples.en: Differentiation of the function gives the velocity at any moment.
examples.cn: 对该函数求微分就得到任意时刻的速度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“地分人先谢”：大家分地、分开、分家，先分才有 differentiation 的区分与分化。

root: 拉丁语 differre“分开搬运”（dis- 分开 + ferre 携带），名词 differentia“差异”；再经法语 differencier 进入英语作 differentiate，加拉丁名词后缀 -ation 构成 differentiation。数学的“微分”义在 19 世纪从微积分术语中固定下来。

sensesIntro.en: One Latin verb, differre, means 'to carry apart'. Everything in this entry is a version of that carrying: a mind separates two species, a stem cell takes one path, a brand is set apart on a shelf, a magma splits into fractions, a calculus operation shrinks a gap toward zero. The nine senses differ only in what is being separated and who does the separating.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个拉丁动词 differre 意为“分开搬运”。本词条的一切都是这个“搬开”的版本：头脑分辨两个物种，干细胞走上一条路径，品牌在货架上被置开，岩浆分成几部分，微积分运算把间隙缩向零。九个义项的差别只在于分开的是什么、以及由谁来分。

core.en: Carrying apart: making what was one into things that are not interchangeable.
core.cn: 分开搬运：把原本是一体的东西变成不可互换的多件事物。

branches.en: Judgement and process: telling apart, and becoming unlike.
branches.cn: 判断与过程：分辨，以及逐渐变得不同。

branches.en: MATTER: cells taking roles, magma splitting into rock types.
branches.cn: 物质：细胞承担角色，岩浆分成不同岩类。

branches.en: MARKET AND SCHOOL: products set apart, lessons layered.
branches.cn: 市场与学校：产品被置开，课程被分层。

branches.en: CALCULUS: a gap shrunk toward zero.
branches.cn: 微积分：间隙被缩向零。

branches.en: SYSTEMS: societies and organizations dividing into functions.
branches.cn: 系统：社会与组织分成不同功能。

intro.en: Differentiation stacks three elements: dif- (a form of dis-), ferre 'carry', and -ation. The items below show the same base with other suffixes, and show where dis- keeps its 'apart' force.
intro.cn: differentiation 叠了三个成分：dif-（dis- 的一种形式）、ferre“携带”、-ation。下列条目展示同一词基配其他后缀，并展示 dis- 保留“分开”力量的情形。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give the verb and its two nouns. They explain why a word about difference also yields a word about deferring: carrying apart and putting off are the same gesture in time.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目给出动词及其两个名词。它们解释了为什么一个关于差异的词同时产生“推迟”义：在时间上把事搬开与推迟，是同一个动作。

items.meaning: the process of distinguishing or specializing
items.example: Differentiation of the two cases took hours.
items.exampleCN: 区分这两个病例花了几个小时。

items.meaning: to distinguish, to make distinct, to find a derivative
items.example: Readers must differentiate fact from opinion.
items.exampleCN: 读者必须把事实与观点区分开。

items.structure: Latin differens, present participle of differre
items.example: The two samples are chemically different.
items.exampleCN: 这两个样本在化学上不同。

items.meaning: the state of being unlike; the amount between two values
items.example: The difference is only a few degrees.
items.exampleCN: 差别只有几度。

items.meaning: relating to a difference; a small increment
items.meaningCN: 与差异有关的；微小增量
items.example: The differential between the two rates is small.
items.exampleCN: 两个比率的差值很小。

items.example: The accounts differ on one detail.
items.exampleCN: 这些叙述在一个细节上不同。

items.meaning: to put off to a later time
items.example: They deferred the decision until spring.
items.exampleCN: 他们把决定推迟到春天。

items.meaning: to carry back; to point to
items.example: The footnote refers to an earlier study.
items.exampleCN: 脚注指向一项更早的研究。

items.example: The data were transferred to a new drive.
items.exampleCN: 数据被转移到新硬盘。

items.example: The river made the valley fertile.
items.exampleCN: 这条河使河谷变得肥沃。

latinEntries.meaning: to carry apart; to differ; to defer

definition_zh: 顾问；辅导员；心理咨询师；（美国）律师；外交参赞
definition_en: a person who gives guidance, especially in law, education or mental health
core_image: 安静的办公室里，桌对面的人把纸巾盒往前推了推，墙上贴着课程表和一排值班姓名
scene: 开学第一周，一名新生因为选课和想家坐在指导老师对面，话没说完就红了眼眶。 The counselor helped the freshman choose courses and adjust to campus life.
sceneCN: 这里 counselor 指学校里负责学业与生活指导的老师（第 4 个义项：学校辅导员）；句意：这位辅导员帮新生选课，并适应校园生活。图中可辨识物件：纸巾盒、课程表、值班表、两把椅子。

pos.zh: 顾问；提供指导的人
（美国）律师
心理咨询师；辅导员
（外交）参赞

senses.title: A person who gives guidance
senses.definition: someone whose role is to advise another person
senses.definitionCN: 职责是向他人提出建议的人
senses.example: A counselor listened to the whole story before saying anything.
senses.exampleCN: 这位顾问听完整个来龙去脉才开口。
senses.why: The agent ending marks the person who does the advising, so the noun is the human counterpart of counsel as advice.
senses.whyCN: 施事后缀标记做这件事的人，所以这个名词是「建议」的人形对应物。

senses.title: A lawyer in American usage
senses.definition: in American English, a lawyer who advises clients and may appear in court
senses.definitionCN: 在美式英语中，指为客户提供咨询、也可出庭的律师
senses.example: The counselor filed the motion on behalf of the estate.
senses.exampleCN: 这位律师代表遗产一方提交了动议。
senses.why: Legal advice is the oldest branch of the trade, and American usage keeps the title for practising lawyers, especially in formal writing.
senses.whyCN: 法律咨询是这门行业最古老的一支，美式用法把这个称谓留给执业律师，尤其在正式文书中。

senses.title: A therapist or mental health counselor
senses.titleCN: 心理咨询师；心理治疗师
senses.definition: a trained professional who helps people with emotional or psychological difficulties
senses.definitionCN: 受过训练、帮助人们处理情绪或心理困难的专业人员
senses.example: She saw a counselor twice a month after the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 事故之后，她每月见两次心理咨询师。
senses.why: The twentieth century widened the word from legal advice to therapeutic guidance, because both are forms of structured talk.
senses.whyCN: 二十世纪把这个词从法律建议扩展到心理辅导，因为两者都是有结构的谈话。

senses.title: A school or college adviser
senses.titleCN: 学校辅导员；学业指导员
senses.definition: a staff member who guides students on courses, applications and personal problems
senses.definitionCN: 指导学生选课、申请与个人问题的教职员工
senses.example: The counselor helped the freshman choose courses and adjust to campus life.
senses.exampleCN: 这位辅导员帮新生选课，并适应校园生活。
senses.why: Schools needed someone between teacher and administrator, and the title transferred from law to education with the idea of guidance intact.
senses.whyCN: 学校需要一个介于教师与管理者之间的人，这个称谓便从法律转到教育，而「指导」这个观念原样保留。

senses.title: A camp counselor
senses.definition: a supervisor who looks after young campers and leads activities
senses.definitionCN: 照看年轻营员、带领活动的带队人员
senses.example: Each cabin of eight children shared one counselor.
senses.exampleCN: 每间住八个孩子的营房配一名辅导员。
senses.why: Supervision of the young is a form of guidance, so seasonal camps borrowed the same title for a temporary role.
senses.whyCN: 照看年轻人本身就是一种指导，所以季节性营地也用同一个称谓来指临时岗位。

senses.title: A diplomatic counselor
senses.definition: a senior officer at an embassy who handles a specialised area
senses.definitionCN: 使馆中负责某一专门领域的资深官员
senses.example: The cultural counselor arranged the exchange of students.
senses.exampleCN: 文化参赞安排了学生的互访。
senses.why: Diplomatic ranks adopted the word for an official who advises an ambassador within one field, keeping the advisory core.
senses.whyCN: 外交衔级采用这个词，指在某一领域向大使提供建议的官员，保留了「顾问」的内核。

senses.title: Counselor at law
senses.definition: a formal historical title for a licensed lawyer
senses.definitionCN: 历史上对持照律师的正式称谓
senses.example: The sign outside his office read counselor at law.
senses.exampleCN: 他办公室外的招牌上写着「执业律师」。
senses.why: The compound fixed the rank in a title, and the phrase survives on old brass plates long after ordinary speech dropped it.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合结构把身份固定成一个头衔，普通口语早已不用，它却还能在旧铜牌上见到。

senses.title: A specialist adviser in an organisation
senses.definition: an adviser attached to a body to cover one technical area, such as finance or genetics
senses.definitionCN: 受聘于某一机构、负责一个技术领域的顾问，如财务或遗传
senses.example: A genetic counselor explained the test results to the couple.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传咨询师向这对夫妇解释了检测结果。
senses.why: As knowledge specialised, organisations appointed advisers with a field label in front of the title, a pattern the word still follows.
senses.whyCN: 随着知识专门化，机构开始任命前面带领域标签的顾问，这个词至今仍循着这个模式。

intro.en: Counselor is counsel plus the agent ending -or, which comes from Latin -or. The base noun goes back to Latin consilium 'advice', and the American spelling with one l contrasts with British counsellor.
intro.cn: counselor 是 counsel 加施事后缀 -or，后者来自拉丁 -or。基础名词上溯拉丁 consilium「建议」，美式单 l 的拼法与英式 counsellor 相对。

items.en: Consilium meant advice, a plan or a body of advisers. It is the noun of consulere 'to consult', and not a form of the official title consul.
items.cn: consilium 指建议、计划或一群顾问。它是动词 consulere「咨询」的名词，而不是官职 consul 的形式。

items.en: The suffix -or marked the person who performs an action, as in doctor and victor. It gave English the shape of counselor, the one who gives the counsel.
items.cn: 后缀 -or 标记执行动作的人，如 doctor、victor。它给了英语 counselor 这个形态，即提供建议的人。

items.en: English first used counsel for the advice and for the adviser, before the agent ending was added to make the person explicit.
items.cn: 英语最初用 counsel 既指建议也指顾问，之后才加上施事后缀，把人明确标出。

items.en: Counselor was formed inside English rather than borrowed whole, which is why the British and American spellings differ: counsellor and counselor.
items.cn: counselor 是在英语内部构成的，而不是整体借入，所以英美拼写不同：counsellor 与 counselor。

items.en: Guidance work in schools and therapeutic work in clinics adopted the title during the twentieth century, widening it far beyond law.
items.cn: 二十世纪，学校的指导工作与诊所的治疗工作采用了这个称谓，使它远远超出法律领域。

items.en: Modern English uses the word for legal advisers, school advisers, therapists and camp staff, with the context deciding which role is meant.
items.cn: 现代英语用它指法律顾问、学校指导员、心理治疗师与营地带队人员，由语境决定所指的角色。

note.en: Group one separates the base word, the spelling variant and two look-alikes with other origins; group two sets the person against other helping roles.
note.cn: 第一组把基础词、拼写变体，与两个来源不同的形近词分开；第二组把这个人同其他助人角色作对照。

entries.definition: The advice itself or a legal team; counselor is always the person who gives the guidance.
entries.definitionCN: 指建议本身或一支律师团队；counselor 则始终指提供指导的人。

entries.definition: The same word spelled with double l in British English; the meaning does not change.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个词在英式英语中的双 l 拼法，含义不变。

entries.definition: A member of a council or local assembly, built on council 'meeting'; it is not an adviser.
entries.definitionCN: 指议会或地方议会的成员，构词基础是 council「集会」；它不是顾问。

entries.definition: A diplomatic or Roman official; the word shares sounds with counsel but has a separate origin and no advisory sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指外交或罗马官员；读音与 counsel 相近，来源不同，也无顾问之义。

entries.definition: The activity of giving guidance; the counselor is the person who performs it.
entries.definitionCN: 指提供指导的活动；counselor 是从事这项活动的人。

entries.definition: A broad word for anyone who gives recommendations; counselor often implies training or a formal role.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指提出建议的人；counselor 常暗示受过训练或有正式职位。

entries.definition: A trained practitioner who treats mental or physical conditions; a counselor may advise without clinical treatment.
entries.definitionCN: 治疗身心问题的受训执业者；counselor 可能只提供咨询而不做临床治疗。

entries.definition: The everyday word for a legal practitioner; counselor is the American formal title for the same role.
entries.definitionCN: 法律执业者的日常说法；counselor 是同一角色的美国正式称谓。

entries.definition: A formal American term for a legal representative, also used in official titles.
entries.definitionCN: 美国指法律代理人的正式说法，也用于官方头衔。

entries.definition: An experienced person who guides another over time; a counselor usually works within a defined role or session.
entries.definitionCN: 以经验长期引导他人的人；counselor 通常在一个明确的角色或会谈框架内工作。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real agent ending, the real legal sense and the real British spelling.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的施事后缀、真实的法律义与真实的英式拼写。

normal.en: Counsel plus the agent ending -or gives the person whose job is the advising.
normal.cn: counsel 加施事后缀 -or，得到以「提建议」为职责的那个人。

normal.en: The British spelling doubles the l: counsellor, while the American keeps one.
normal.cn: 英式拼写双写 l，写作 counsellor；美式只写一个 l。

normal.en: Councilor is a council member, not an adviser: the base word is council, a meeting.
normal.cn: councilor 是议会成员，不是顾问：它的基础词是 council，即集会。

normal.en: Fixed phrases name the setting: school counselor, marriage counselor, camp counselor.
normal.cn: 固定说法点明场景：学校辅导员、婚姻咨询师、夏令营辅导员。

normal.en: In American formal writing the word still means a lawyer, as in counselor at law.
normal.cn: 在美国正式文书中，这个词仍指律师，如「执业律师」这一旧称。

abstract.en: Picture a tissue box pushed across a desk, a timetable on the wall behind.
abstract.cn: 想象一盒纸巾被推过桌面，身后墙上贴着课程表。

abstract.en: Picture a title that fits a courtroom, a classroom and a clinic without changing its shape.
abstract.cn: 想象一个不用改变外形就能嵌进法庭、教室与诊室的称谓。

abstract.en: Picture a person whose only tool is structured talk, given at a fixed hour each week.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人唯一的工具是有结构的谈话，每周在固定时间进行。

examples.en: The counselor asked one more question and then stayed quiet.
examples.cn: 辅导员又问了一个问题，然后安静下来。

examples.en: A camp counselor must know every child by name.
examples.cn: 夏令营辅导员必须叫得出每个孩子的名字。

examples.en: The embassy counselor handled the visa dispute.
examples.cn: 使馆参赞处理了那桩签证纠纷。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「靠啥了」——心里没底就找顾问问一问「靠啥了」→ 辅导员、顾问

root: 英语 counsel（建议、法律顾问，源自拉丁 consilium）加施事后缀 -or（源自拉丁 -or），指提供指导的人；英式拼作 counsellor。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the general adviser, through the American lawyer, the therapist, the school adviser, the camp supervisor, the diplomatic rank, the old title at law, and the specialist adviser inside an organisation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从泛称顾问开始，经美国律师、心理治疗师、学校辅导员、夏令营带队人、外交参赞、旧时的执业律师头衔，最后到机构内的专科顾问。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a desk with a tissue box and a timetable, one person listening.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张放着纸巾盒与课程表的桌子，一个人在那里倾听。

branches.en: THE ROLE: the agent ending turns advice into a person whose job it is.
branches.cn: 角色：施事后缀把「建议」变成以此为职的人。

branches.en: THE LAW: the oldest field of advice supplies the American legal title.
branches.cn: 法律：最古老的咨询领域提供了美国的律师称谓。

branches.en: THE CLINIC: structured talk about feelings becomes a therapeutic profession.
branches.cn: 诊室：围绕情绪的有结构谈话，成为一门治疗职业。

branches.en: THE YOUNG: schools and camps appoint adults to guide students and campers.
branches.cn: 年轻人：学校与营地都安排成年人去指导学员与营员。

branches.en: THE FORMAL TITLES: embassies, old legal brass plates and specialised desks all keep the advisory core in a title.
branches.cn: 正式头衔：使馆、旧日的律师铜牌与专科岗位，都以头衔形式保留「顾问」的内核。

intro.en: Counselor is an English-built agent noun on a borrowed base, so its ending is the part that says 'the person'.
intro.cn: counselor 是在英语内部构成的施事名词，基础词是借来的，词尾才是表示「那个人」的部分。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is consilium 'advice' from consulere 'to consult'; the Latin agent suffix -or supplies the ending, and the spelling -our marks the British form.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁基础是 consilium「建议」，出自 consulere「咨询」；拉丁施事后缀 -or 提供词尾，而 -our 拼法标出英式形式。

items.example: The verb names the asking.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词命名「求教」。

items.example: The noun named the advice.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名建议。

items.meaningCN: 执行动作的人（施事后缀）
items.example: Doctor and victor share the ending.
items.exampleCN: doctor 与 victor 共享这个词尾。

items.structure: consilium used as an English noun
items.meaningCN: 建议；法律顾问（借入后一形兼两义）
items.example: Counsel sat beside the client.
items.exampleCN: 顾问坐在当事人旁边。

items.meaningCN: 提供指导的人（在英语内部由基础词加施事后缀构成）
items.example: The counselor listened.
items.exampleCN: 辅导员在倾听。

items.meaningCN: 提供指导的活动（动名词后缀把动作转成持续的工作）
items.example: Counseling takes time.
items.exampleCN: 辅导需要时间。

items.meaning: spelling variant with no change of meaning
items.meaningCN: 英式拼法变体，含义不变（同一词尾的书写差异）
items.example: British writes counsellor.
items.exampleCN: 英式写作 counsellor。

items.meaningCN: 执业律师（固定头衔把顾问义限定到法律职业）
items.example: The plate read counselor at law.
items.exampleCN: 铜牌上写着「执业律师」。

definition_zh: 名词：大麦（一种禾谷作物及其麦粒）；珍珠麦；用于酿造的麦芽原料
definition_en: a hardy cereal grass and its grain, used for food, for malting and for brewing beer and whisky
core_image: 一片金黄的麦田，风过时整片麦浪起伏
scene: 六月的田里一片金黄，风过时整片麦浪起伏。 The field of barley rippled in the wind.
sceneCN: 这里 barley 是「大麦」（第 1 个义项：一种禾谷作物）；句意是大麦田在风中起伏。

pos.zh: 名词：大麦；大麦粒

forms.label: 不可数名词（无屈折变化）

derivatives.zh: 名词：大麦粒；旧时长度单位
名词：麦芽，大麦发芽烘干而成

senses.title: The cereal crop
senses.definition: a hardy cereal grass, Hordeum vulgare, grown for its grain
senses.definitionCN: 一种耐寒的禾谷作物，学名 Hordeum vulgare，为取麦粒而种
senses.example: The field of barley rippled in the wind.
senses.exampleCN: 大麦田在风中起伏。
senses.why: Old English bærlic meant of barley; the adjective was re-cut as a noun in Middle English.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 bærlic 意为「大麦的」；中古英语把这个形容词重新当作名词使用。

senses.title: Malt for brewing
senses.definition: the grain soaked and dried to make malt for beer and whisky
senses.definitionCN: 浸水发芽再烘干制成麦芽，用于啤酒与威士忌
senses.example: Malted barley gives the beer its body.
senses.exampleCN: 麦芽赋予啤酒酒体。
senses.why: Barley germinates easily, so brewers chose it over other grains.
senses.whyCN: 大麦易发芽，酿酒人因此选它而非其他谷物。

senses.title: Pearl barley as food
senses.definition: the grain polished and used in soups and stews
senses.definitionCN: 磨去外层的麦粒，用于汤与炖菜
senses.example: Add pearl barley to the soup an hour before serving.
senses.exampleCN: 上桌前一小时把珍珠麦加进汤里。
senses.why: Polishing removes the husk, leaving a round white grain called pearl barley.
senses.whyCN: 抛光去掉外壳，留下圆白的麦粒，称作珍珠麦。

senses.title: Barley drinks
senses.definition: in barley water and barley wine, drinks made from the grain
senses.definitionCN: 用于 barley water 与 barley wine 等大麦饮品
senses.example: She cooled the barley water and added lemon.
senses.exampleCN: 她把大麦水放凉，再加柠檬。
senses.why: The grain names the drink, as wheat names wheat beer.
senses.whyCN: 谷物为饮品命名，正如小麦命名小麦啤酒。

intro.en: Barley is an Old English adjective that forgot it was an adjective.
intro.cn: barley 本是一个古英语形容词，后来忘了自己的词性。

items.en: The root bhares- meant barley and gave Latin far and Old English bere.
items.cn: 词根 bhares- 意为大麦，衍生出拉丁语 far 与古英语 bere。

items.en: The Germanic form bariz- carried the grain name north.
items.cn: 日耳曼语形式 bariz- 把这个谷物名带到北方。

items.en: Bere meant barley; barn is bere plus ern, a barley house.
items.cn: bere 意为大麦；barn 由 bere 加 ern「房屋」构成，本义「大麦屋」。

items.en: Bærlic added -lic to bere, meaning of barley.
items.cn: bærlic 在 bere 上加 -lic，意为「大麦的」。

items.en: The adjective was reanalysed as a noun, giving barley.
items.cn: 这个形容词被重新分析为名词，成为 barley。

items.en: Barley remains the brewing grain, malted into beer and whisky.
items.cn: barley 仍是酿造用谷物，制成麦芽后用于啤酒与威士忌。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -ley or bar- shape; the near-meaning group lists other cereal grains.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -ley 或 bar- 形状；近义组列出其他禾谷作物。

entries.definitionCN: 几乎不；仅仅

entries.definition: big and strong in build
entries.definitionCN: 魁梧的

entries.definition: a freshwater fish with whiskers
entries.definitionCN: 鲃（淡水鱼）

entries.definition: a cereal grown for porridge
entries.definitionCN: 燕麦

entries.definition: a hardy grain for dark bread
entries.definitionCN: 黑麦

entries.definition: the grain ground into flour
entries.definitionCN: 小麦

entries.definition: a small-seeded cereal
entries.definitionCN: 粟；小米

normalIntro.en: Barley is bere plus -lic, and its cousin barn literally means a barley house.
normalIntro.cn: barley 是 bere 加 -lic，而它的亲戚 barn 字面就是「大麦屋」。

normal.en: Bere is the Old English grain word hidden inside barley and barn.
normal.cn: bere 是藏在 barley 与 barn 里的古英语谷物词。

normal.en: -lic became Modern English -ly, so bærlic meant barley-like.
normal.cn: -lic 演变为现代英语 -ly，所以 bærlic 意为「大麦般的」。

normal.en: Barley is usually uncountable: a field of barley, not barleys.
normal.cn: barley 通常不可数：说 a field of barley，不说 barleys。

normal.en: Pearl barley is the polished grain used in soup.
normal.cn: pearl barley 是磨光后用于煮汤的麦粒。

normal.en: Do not confuse barley with barely, which means almost not.
normal.cn: 别把 barley 与 barely 混淆，后者意为「几乎不」。

abstract.cn: 想象收割前一片金黄的麦田在风中弯腰。

abstract.en: See grain sprouting on a warm malting floor.
abstract.cn: 想象麦粒在温暖的制麦芽地板上发芽。

abstract.en: See a round white grain dropping into a soup pot.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗圆白的麦粒落进汤锅。

sensesIntro.en: A crop, a malt, a soup grain and a drink all come from barley.
sensesIntro.cn: 一种作物、一份麦芽、一粒汤料和一杯饮品，都来自 barley。

definition_zh: 在进行中；酝酿中；徒步的
definition_en: in progress or being planned; on foot, walking
core_image: 脚步已迈出：事情正在路上，肉眼可见地展开
scene: 办公室里流言四起，人人神色紧张。 Rumours of a merger were afoot long before the official announcement.
sceneCN: 这里 afoot 是「正在酝酿、进行中」（第 1 个义项：计划或活动已经在展开）；句意是合并的传言早在官方宣布之前就已四处流传。

pos.zh: 进行中的；酝酿中的（表语用法为主）
徒步地；在活动状态中

derivatives.zh: 基础名词，义为「脚；英尺」；afoot 即 foot 的介词化组合
foot 复合名词，义为「小径；人行道」
foot 复合名词，义为「脚步声；客流」
同构词式 a- + fire，义为「燃烧着；激动不已」

senses.title: In progress or being planned
senses.definition: currently happening or being prepared, often secretly or without public confirmation
senses.definitionCN: 正在发生或正在筹划，常带有秘密进行、尚未公开的色彩
senses.example: Rumours of a merger were afoot long before the official announcement.
senses.exampleCN: 合并的传言早在官方宣布之前就已四处流传。
senses.why: The image is of feet already in motion: an undertaking has set out and cannot be seen fully yet, hence plans under way.
senses.whyCN: 意象是「脚步已经迈开」：一项行动已经上路、但全貌尚未可见，于是引申为「计划在酝酿推进中」。

senses.title: On foot; walking
senses.definition: travelling or moving on foot rather than by vehicle or horse
senses.definitionCN: 不乘车马、以双脚行进
senses.example: The pilgrims completed the last stage of their journey afoot.
senses.exampleCN: 朝圣者们徒步完成了旅程的最后一段。
senses.why: This is the literal layer: a- plus foot simply describes someone standing or moving on their feet.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面层：a-（处于状态）+ foot（脚），直接描写「双脚着地、以脚行进」的原始画面。

senses.title: In active circulation or existence
senses.definition: present and circulating among people, as rumours, diseases, or ideas
senses.definitionCN: 指流言、疾病、观念等正在人群中流传、存在
senses.example: Several strains of flu were afoot that winter.
senses.exampleCN: 那年冬天有好几种流感病毒在流行。
senses.why: What is under way is also out and about among people, so the sense extends from plans to anything circulating actively.
senses.whyCN: 「在推进」的东西同时也在人群间流转，于是词义从「计划」扩展到一切正在活跃流传的事物。

intro.en: A native English formation: the prefix a- (on, in) plus foot, first literal, then figurative.
intro.cn: 英语本土构词：前缀 a-（处于……状态）+ foot（脚），先有字面义，后生比喻义。

items.en: The reconstructed root *ped- (foot) underlies foot and its Germanic cousins.
items.cn: 重构词根 *ped-（脚）是 foot 及其日耳曼同族词的远源。

items.en: on fote meant on foot; the phrase lived as two words.
items.cn: 古英语作 on fote，意为「以脚行进」，当时仍是短语形式。

items.en: The phrase fused into afoot, keeping the walking sense and adding the sense of in progress.
items.cn: 中古英语中短语融合为 afoot，保留「徒步」义，并新增「进行中」一义。

items.en: Shakespeare uses something is afoot in the figurative sense of stirrings under way.
items.cn: 莎士比亚笔下已用 something is afoot 表示「有动静、有事酝酿」。

items.en: The figurative sense now dominates; the walking sense survives mostly in literary or set phrases.
items.cn: 现代英语中比喻义占主导；「徒步」义主要残存于书面语和固定搭配。

note.en: Afoot signals ongoing movement, often with a hint of secrecy; underway and in motion are its plain neighbours.
note.cn: afoot 强调正在推进，常带一丝隐秘色彩；underway 与 in motion 是它的平义近邻。

entries.definition: burning; filled with excitement
entries.definitionCN: 燃烧着的；激动的——同款 a- 前缀构词，意象平行

entries.definition: on or into a ship, aircraft, or train
entries.definitionCN: 在船（车、机）上——同为 a- + 名词的组合

entries.definition: free to go or travel anywhere
entries.definitionCN: 自由自在、无牵挂的——同根 foot

entries.definition: coldly distant in manner
entries.definitionCN: 冷漠疏远的——拼写与 afoot 相似，词源不同（航海词 luff）

entries.definition: having started and in progress
entries.definitionCN: 进行中——平义近邻，无隐秘色彩

entries.definition: developing, especially trouble about to happen
entries.definitionCN: 酝酿中的（多指麻烦）——与 afoot 的隐秘义相合

entries.definition: awaiting decision or settlement
entries.definitionCN: 待决的；悬而未决的——强调等待而非推进

entries.definition: in movement; out of bed and active
entries.definitionCN: 活动起来的；骚动的——同为 a- 系状态词

entries.definition: temporarily inactive
entries.definitionCN: 休眠的；中止的——afoot 的反义状态

normalIntro.en: Read the word literally as a + foot: feet already moving, so the matter is under way.
normalIntro.cn: 把词读作 a + foot：脚已在动，事情自然「在路上」。

normal.en: something is afoot: the classic phrase for secret goings-on
normal.cn: something is afoot 是「有情况、有猫腻」的经典说法

normal.en: plans are afoot: they have set out but are not announced
normal.cn: plans are afoot：计划已启动但尚未公开

normal.en: afoot versus aloof: feet moving versus standing apart
normal.cn: afoot（脚步在动）对照 aloof（冷眼旁观），拼写一步之差

normal.en: afire, aboard, afoot: the a- family marks an active state
normal.cn: afire、aboard、afoot 同属 a- 家族，都表示「处于某状态」

normal.en: walk afoot: the old literal sense of travelling on foot
normal.cn: walk afoot 保留「徒步」的古义，帮助锚定词形

abstract.en: Boots stepping out of frame while only shadows show what is coming
abstract.cn: 一双靴子正迈出画面，只见影子不知来者

abstract.en: A pot lid rattling softly before the soup boils over
abstract.cn: 锅盖在汤滚溢之前轻轻地颤动作响

abstract.en: A train already moving as its destination sign flickers on
abstract.cn: 列车已然启动，目的地的灯牌才刚刚亮起

examples.en: Detective stories thrive on the feeling that something sinister is afoot.
examples.cn: 侦探小说的魅力正在于那种「有阴谋在暗中酝酿」的感觉。

examples.en: Negotiations have been afoot for months without any public result.
examples.cn: 谈判已暗中进行了数月，尚无公开结果。

examples.en: They travelled the final miles afoot when the bus broke down.
examples.cn: 公共汽车抛锚后，最后几英里他们只能徒步前行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿福特」——阿福特着脚满屋踱步，事情正办着呢。谐音仅助记，并非词源。

root: 英语本土构词：前缀 a-（古英语 on，处于……状态）+ foot（脚，源自印欧词根 *ped-）；「双脚着地」的字面画面引申出「徒步」义，又由「脚步已动」引申出「在进行中、酝酿中」的比喻义。

sensesIntro.en: From the literal picture of walking feet grows the figurative sense of plans already moving.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「双脚行走」的字面画面，长出「计划已然启动、暗中进行」的比喻义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: feet already in motion
core.cn: 核心意象：已经迈开的脚步

branches.en: travelling on one's own feet
branches.cn: 以双脚行进的字面义

branches.en: movement as the shared image
branches.cn: 「行进」是两义共享的画面

branches.en: plans quietly being prepared
branches.cn: 计划悄悄推进、尚未公开

branches.en: rumours or disease spreading about
branches.cn: 流言或疾病正在流传

branches.en: anything actively in motion among people
branches.cn: 一切在人群中活跃运转的事物

intro.en: The word is a native compound of the prefix a- and the root foot, not a Latin borrowing.

definition_zh: 杂交；杂交育种；异系交配
definition_en: the practice of breeding individuals from different breeds, varieties or species
core_image: 两个不同血统的畜群被分栏管理，再按计划配对
scene: 牧场把两种不同血统的牛分开管理，再按计划配种。技术员解释： Crossbreeding brings new traits into the herd without losing milk yield.
sceneCN: 这里指「杂交育种」（第 1 个义项：让不同品种或品系的个体交配繁育）；句意为杂交育种把新性状带入牛群，同时不损失产奶量。

pos.zh: 杂交；杂交育种；异系交配（不可数）

senses.title: Breeding across different kinds
senses.definition: the practice of mating individuals from different breeds, varieties or species
senses.definitionCN: 让不同品种、品系或物种的个体交配繁育的做法
senses.example: Crossbreeding brings new traits into the herd without losing milk yield.
senses.exampleCN: 杂交育种把新性状带入牛群，同时不损失产奶量。
senses.why: Cross- marks the joining of two lineages, and breeding names the controlled production of offspring.
senses.whyCN: cross- 标记两个世系的接合，breeding 命名对后代的有控生产。

senses.title: The process of cross-breeding
senses.definition: the repeated process of producing offspring from different lines
senses.definitionCN: 由不同品系反复产生后代的过程
senses.example: Crossbreeding continued for four generations before selection began.
senses.exampleCN: 杂交繁育持续了四代，之后才开始选择。
senses.why: The -ing form names the ongoing activity rather than a single mating.
senses.whyCN: -ing 形式命名持续的活动，而不是一次交配。

senses.title: Crossbreeding in livestock
senses.definition: the use of different cattle, sheep or pig breeds to combine production traits
senses.definitionCN: 利用不同牛、羊或猪品种来组合生产性状
senses.example: Crossbreeding improved growth rate in the beef herd.
senses.exampleCN: 杂交提高了肉牛群的生长速度。
senses.why: Farmers cross breeds to combine milk, meat or hardiness that no single breed supplies well.
senses.whyCN: 农民让品种杂交，以组合任何单一品种都无法充分提供的产奶、产肉或耐性。

senses.title: Crossbreeding in plants
senses.definition: the crossing of plant varieties or lines to create new combinations
senses.definitionCN: 让植物品种或品系杂交以产生新组合
senses.example: Crossbreeding two wheat lines produced a sturdier stem.
senses.exampleCN: 两个小麦品系杂交产生了更粗壮的茎。
senses.why: Plants allow controlled pollination, so the same practice becomes a field technique.
senses.whyCN: 植物可以人工控制授粉，因此同一做法成为田间技术。

senses.title: Crossbreeding in animals
senses.definition: the mating of animals from different breeds or populations
senses.definitionCN: 不同品种或种群的动物交配
senses.example: Crossbreeding the two deer populations raised genetic diversity.
senses.exampleCN: 两个鹿种群的杂交提高了遗传多样性。
senses.why: In animals the practice may be planned for production or allowed to restore diversity in small populations.
senses.whyCN: 在动物中，这种做法可以是为生产而计划，也可以是为恢复小群体的多样性而允许发生。

senses.title: Crossbreeding with a wild relative
senses.definition: crossing a domesticated line with a wild relative to transfer useful traits
senses.definitionCN: 让家养品系与野生近缘种杂交以转移有用性状
senses.example: Crossbreeding with a wild grass added salt tolerance.
senses.exampleCN: 与一种野生草杂交增添了耐盐性。
senses.why: Wild relatives hold traits that domestication lost, and crossing brings them back into the crop.
senses.whyCN: 野生近缘种保留着驯化过程中丢失的性状，杂交把它们带回作物。

senses.title: The production of crossbred offspring
senses.definition: the result of crossing, viewed as the appearance of mixed offspring
senses.definitionCN: 杂交的结果，即混合后代的出现
senses.example: Crossbreeding produced calves that gained weight faster.
senses.exampleCN: 杂交产生了增重更快的犊牛。
senses.why: The noun can focus on the outcome, where the mixed offspring are the point of the practice.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词可以聚焦结果，此时混合后代才是做法的重点。

senses.title: A metaphor for mixing sources
senses.titleCN: 比喻：不同来源的混合（少见）
senses.definition: a figurative blending of different traditions or sources
senses.definitionCN: 不同传统或来源的比喻性融合
senses.example: The festival is a crossbreeding of rural and urban customs.
senses.exampleCN: 这个节庆是乡村与城市习俗的混合。
senses.why: Outside farming the word is rare, but the picture of two lineages producing a new line can describe cultural mixing.
senses.whyCN: 在农业之外这个词很少用，但两个世系产生新世系的图像可以描述文化混合。

intro.en: Crossbreeding joins cross, from Latin crux 'cross', to breeding, from Old English bredan 'to warm, cherish, produce offspring'. The compound is modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: crossbreeding 把来自拉丁 crux「十字、交叉」的 cross 与来自古英语 bredan「保暖、抚育、生育」的 breeding 结合。这个复合词属近代。年代均为约数。

items.en: Crux meant 'cross, stake'. English cross came through Old Irish and Old Norse forms, and the verb cross developed the sense 'to pass or mix across'.
items.cn: crux 意为「十字架、木桩」。英语 cross 经古爱尔兰语与古诺斯语形式传入，动词 cross 又发展出「横跨、交叉混合」的意思。

items.en: Bredan meant 'to warm, keep warm, cherish', and by extension 'to produce young'. It is related to brood and broth and belongs to native Germanic stock.
items.cn: bredan 意为「保暖、抚育」，引申为「生育幼仔」。它与 brood、broth 相关，属本族日耳曼词。

items.en: Breeding developed in Middle English as the noun for producing and raising offspring, and later for the controlled improvement of stock.
items.cn: breeding 在中古英语中发展为表示生育与养育后代的名词，后来又指对畜禽的有控改良。

items.en: Crossbreeding became a standard term in the nineteenth century, when pedigree breeding and scientific agriculture separated crossing from inbreeding.
items.cn: crossbreeding 在 19 世纪成为标准术语，当时谱系育种与科学农业把杂交与近交区分开来。

items.en: Modern use pairs it with inbreeding and outcrossing, and extends it to conservation and plant breeding.
items.cn: 现代用法把它与近交、远交并列，并扩展到保护生物学与植物育种。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the exact first use of crossbreeding as a single term is not recorded, and the early sense development of the verb cross is complex.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：crossbreeding 作为单一术语的最早使用没有记录；动词 cross 的早期语义发展也很复杂。

note.en: Group one holds forms built on the same cross or breed stock; group two holds breeding terms that are close in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 cross 或 breed 词干的形式；第二组是意义接近的繁育术语。

entries.definition: To perform the cross, or the offspring itself; crossbreeding is the practice or process.
entries.definitionCN: 指实施杂交，或指杂交后代本身；crossbreeding 指做法或过程。

entries.definition: Describing an animal produced by crossing; it is a form of the verb, not the name of the practice.
entries.definitionCN: 描述由杂交产生的动物；是动词形式，不是做法名称。

entries.definition: The plain verb or noun for crossing; crossbreeding is the specialized breeding compound.
entries.definitionCN: 指杂交的普通动词或名词；crossbreeding 是专门的繁育复合词。

entries.definition: Breeding close relatives; it is the counterpart that crossbreeding is meant to avoid.
entries.definitionCN: 指近亲繁育；是 crossbreeding 想要避免的对立做法。

entries.definition: The general technical process of making hybrids; crossbreeding is more common in farm stock.
entries.definitionCN: 指制造杂交后代的一般技术过程；crossbreeding 多用于畜禽。

entries.definition: Crossing with an unrelated individual from outside the line; it is a narrower strategy.
entries.definitionCN: 指与品系外无关个体杂交；是一种更窄的策略。

entries.definition: Breeding between different populations or species where they meet; it often happens without planning.
entries.definitionCN: 指不同群体或物种在相遇处的繁育；常无计划地发生。

entries.definition: One act of crossing two individuals; crossbreeding names a sustained practice.
entries.definitionCN: 指让两个个体杂交的一次行为；crossbreeding 命名持续的做法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: cross 'across' + breeding 'producing young': producing young across two lines.
normal.cn: cross「横跨」+ breeding「生育后代」：跨两个世系生育后代。

normal.en: The family runs cross, crossbreed, crossbred, crossbreeding, outcrossing.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 cross、crossbreed、crossbred、crossbreeding、outcrossing。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: crossbreeding program, controlled crossbreeding, crossbreeding and inbreeding.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：杂交育种计划、受控杂交、杂交与近交。

normal.en: Crossbreeding is the opposite of inbreeding: outside lines versus close relatives.
normal.cn: 杂交与近交相对：一个是外来世系，一个是近亲。

normal.en: Farmers use it to combine traits that no single breed supplies.
normal.cn: 农民用它来组合任何单一品种都无法提供的性状。

abstract.en: Picture two herds in separate pens, then a gate opened between them.
abstract.cn: 想象两个畜群各在栏内，然后两栏之间的门被打开。

abstract.en: Picture two family trees grafted at one branch.
abstract.cn: 想象两棵家谱树在一个枝条上嫁接。

abstract.en: Picture two recipes from different regions cooked in one kitchen.
abstract.cn: 想象两个地区的菜谱在同一间厨房里烹制。

examples.en: Crossbreeding two local breeds raised both milk and heat tolerance.
examples.cn: 两个本地品种的杂交同时提高了产奶量与耐热性。

examples.en: The crossbreeding program lasted three generations.
examples.cn: 这个杂交育种计划持续了三代。

examples.en: Crossbreeding can rescue a small population from low diversity.
examples.cn: 杂交可以把一个小群体从低多样性中挽救出来。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one practice: two separate lines are brought together, and the practice is then named for livestock, crops, wild relatives, its offspring and occasionally culture.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一种做法展开：两个分开的世系被带到一起，这种做法再依次用于畜禽、作物、野生近缘种、其后代，偶尔也用于文化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two herds in separate pens with a gate opened between them.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个畜群各在栏内，两栏之间的门被打开。

branches.en: PRACTICE AND PROCESS: the general practice, and the ongoing activity over generations.
branches.cn: 做法与过程：一般做法，以及跨世代的持续活动。

branches.en: FARM STOCK: cattle, crops and animals each apply the same practice.
branches.cn: 农场畜禽：牛、作物与动物都应用同一做法。

branches.en: WILD RELATIVES: crossing brings lost traits back from wild lines.
branches.cn: 野生近缘种：杂交把丢失的性状从野生世系带回。

branches.en: OFFSPRING: the mixed young are the visible result.
branches.cn: 后代：混合的幼仔是可见的结果。

branches.en: METAPHOR: cultural traditions can be crossed like lines.
branches.cn: 比喻：文化传统也可以像世系一样被杂交。

intro.en: Crossbreeding is a compound of two free English words: cross, ultimately from Latin crux, and breeding, from native Old English bredan.
intro.cn: crossbreeding 是两个英语自由词的复合：cross 最终来自拉丁 crux，breeding 来自本族古英语 bredan。

latinIntro.en: Only the first element is Latin: crux 'cross' supplies cross. Breeding and its suffix -ing are native English, not Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 只有第一个成分是拉丁语：crux「十字」提供 cross。breeding 及其后缀 -ing 是英语本族成分，不是拉丁语。
