definition_zh: 解剖学的；身体结构的；结构上的
definition_en: relating to anatomy or to the structure of a body
core_image: 一张人体挂图上每块肌肉都被编号，线条标出它们之间的位置关系
scene: 这里指「解剖学的」。 The anatomical model comes apart in twelve layers, from skin to bone.
sceneCN: 这里 anatomical 指「解剖用的」（第 4 个义项：用于展示或研究身体结构的标本与模型）；句意：这个解剖模型可以拆成十二层，从皮肤到骨骼。图中可辨识物件：分层人体模型、编号标签、骨骼支架。

pos.zh: 解剖学的；身体结构的；结构上的（由 anatomy 加 -ical 构成，常修饰 model、structure、position 等）

collocations.zh: 解剖学姿势（标准站立位）

derivatives.zh: 在解剖结构上；从结构上看

senses.title: Of the Science
senses.titleCN: 解剖学的：属于这门学科
senses.definition: belonging to the science of anatomy
senses.definitionCN: 属于解剖学这门学科的
senses.example: The anatomical literature on the wrist is enormous.
senses.exampleCN: 关于腕部的解剖学文献浩如烟海。
senses.why: The adjective attaches the noun to the discipline. In this sense it sits beside histological, physiological and embryological as labels of research fields.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把名词挂到学科上；在这一义项里，它与 histological、physiological、embryological 并列，都是研究领域的标签。

senses.title: Of Body Structure
senses.titleCN: 身体结构的：讲部件怎么长
senses.definition: relating to the actual structure of a body
senses.definitionCN: 与身体实际结构有关的
senses.example: The anatomical difference between the two species is small.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个物种在身体结构上的差异很小。
senses.why: Here the reference is to parts and their arrangement, not to books about them. A difference is anatomical when it lies in structure rather than in behaviour or chemistry.
senses.whyCN: 这里指的是部件及其排列，而不是关于它们的书籍。当差异存在于结构而非行为或化学时，就说它是 anatomical 的差异。

senses.title: Structural, by Metaphor
senses.titleCN: 结构上的：用于非生物对象
senses.definition: relating to the internal structure of a non-biological thing
senses.definitionCN: 与非生物事物的内部结构有关
senses.example: The anatomical weaknesses of the treaty were obvious.
senses.exampleCN: 该条约在结构上的弱点显而易见。
senses.why: The metaphor treats an institution as a body with joints. It is looser than the biological sense and often signals that a failure lies in design, not in execution.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把机构当作有骨架的身体；它比生物学义更宽松，常暗示问题出在设计而非执行。

senses.title: For Display or Study
senses.definition: made to show or study body structure
senses.definitionCN: 为展示或研究身体结构而制作的
senses.example: The anatomical model comes apart in twelve layers, from skin to bone.
senses.exampleCN: 这个解剖模型可以拆成十二层，从皮肤到骨骼。
senses.why: Objects as well as ideas can be anatomical: a model, a chart, a plate. The word then labels the purpose of the object, not a branch of knowledge.
senses.whyCN: 物体也能是 anatomical 的：模型、挂图、图版。此时这个词标出的是该物件的用途，而不是知识分支。

senses.title: Standard Reference Position
senses.titleCN: 解剖学姿势的：标准化方位
senses.definition: relating to the standard position used to describe body parts
senses.definitionCN: 与描述身体部件时所用的标准姿势有关
senses.example: In the anatomical position the palms face forward.
senses.exampleCN: 在解剖学姿势中，手掌朝前。
senses.why: Description needs a fixed frame, or 'left' and 'right' mean nothing. The adjective marks that frame, which is a convention rather than a fact of the body.
senses.whyCN: 描述需要一个固定参照，否则「左」「右」毫无意义；这个形容词标出的正是那一参照，它是约定而非身体的事实。

senses.title: Recognizable in Structure
senses.titleCN: 解剖上可辨识的：结构上找得到
senses.definition: identifiable by its structure when examined
senses.definitionCN: 检查时能凭结构辨认出来的
senses.example: The tumour was anatomically distinct from the surrounding tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 该肿瘤在结构上与周围组织明显不同。
senses.why: Surgeons and radiologists ask whether a thing can be told apart by its parts. Anatomically distinct means the difference is visible in structure, before any chemical test.
senses.whyCN: 外科医生与放射科医生要问：某物能否凭其部件被区分开来。anatomically distinct 意为差异在结构上就可见，无需等到化学检验。

senses.title: Of the Anatomy Course
senses.definition: belonging to the teaching of anatomy
senses.definitionCN: 属于解剖学教学的
senses.example: The anatomical drawings were hung in the dissection room.
senses.exampleCN: 解剖图挂在解剖室里。
senses.why: Teaching produces its own vocabulary and objects. In this sense the adjective points to the classroom and its materials rather than to research.
senses.whyCN: 教学会产出自己的词汇与物件；在这一义项里，这个形容词指向课堂及其教材，而不是科研。

senses.title: Analytic, Part by Part
senses.titleCN: 结构分析的：逐部件拆解
senses.definition: treating a subject by separating its parts
senses.definitionCN: 把对象按部件分开处理
senses.example: The critic offered an anatomical reading of the novel.
senses.exampleCN: 这位批评家对小说作了结构解剖式的解读。
senses.why: This is the adjective of the metaphorical noun: an analysis that names each part and its function. It is more formal than 'structural' and more vivid than 'detailed'.
senses.whyCN: 这是比喻义名词的形容词形式：一种逐一点明每个部件及其作用的分析。它比 structural 更正式，比 detailed 更生动。

intro.en: Anatomical is anatomy plus -ical. Anatomy comes from Greek anatomē 'a cutting up', from ana- 'up, throughout' and temnein 'to cut'. The English adjective is dated only approximately.
intro.cn: anatomical 是 anatomy 加 -ical。anatomy 出自希腊 anatomē「切开」，由 ana-「向上、遍及」与 temnein「切」构成。英语形容词的年代仅为约数。

items.en: Temnein 'to cut' gave the noun tomos 'a cut piece' and the suffix -tomos. English keeps that suffix in surgical names such as appendectomy and lobotomy.
items.cn: temnein「切」给出名词 tomos「切下的一片」与后缀 -tomos；英语在外科名称中保留该后缀，如 appendectomy、lobotomy。

items.en: Anatomē meant the act of cutting up a body. Greek medicine used the word for dissection, and the study of parts grew around that practice.
items.cn: anatomē 指把身体切开的动作；希腊医学用这个词表示解剖，而关于部件的研究正是围绕这一实践发展起来的。

items.en: Latin anatomia carried both the procedure and the knowledge gained. Medieval Latin writers also used it for a written summary of body parts.
items.cn: 拉丁 anatomia 兼指操作过程与所获知识；中世纪拉丁作者也用它指关于身体部件的书面概述。

items.en: English anatomy appears in the sixteenth century, and the adjective anatomical followed in the same period or shortly after. The exact first citation of the adjective is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 anatomy 于十六世纪出现，形容词 anatomical 在同一时期或稍后跟上。该形容词的确切首见书证不确定。

items.en: Medicine fixed phrases such as anatomical position, anatomical variation and gross anatomical features. Each borrows the adjective to mark a standard frame or a level of observation.
items.cn: 医学固定了 anatomical position（解剖学姿势）、anatomical variation（解剖变异）、gross anatomical features（大体解剖特征）等说法；每个都借这个形容词标出标准参照或观察层次。

note.en: The first group separates the adjective from its noun and from its adverb. The second holds near-synonyms that describe structure at different levels.
note.cn: 第一组区分该形容词与其名词、副词；第二组是描述不同层次结构的近义词。

entries.definition: The field, the structure or the act of dissection. It is what the adjective describes, so the two never occupy the same slot in a sentence.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指学科、结构或解剖行为；它是该形容词所描述的对象，因此两者在句中不会占据同一位置。

entries.definition: Means 'in terms of body structure'. It modifies verbs and adjectives, as in anatomically correct or anatomically distinct.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，意为「在身体结构方面」；修饰动词与形容词，如 anatomically correct、anatomically distinct。

entries.definition: A person who studies anatomy. It never replaces the adjective before a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指研究解剖学的人；它不能替代名词前的形容词。

entries.definition: Relating to structure of any kind, biological or not. It is the broader and safer word where no body is involved.
entries.definitionCN: 与任何结构有关，无论是否生物；在不涉及身体时，它更宽泛也更稳妥。

entries.definition: Relating to form and shape, especially in biology and linguistics. It stresses outward form rather than internal arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 与形式和外形有关，尤用于生物学与语言学；强调外部形态，而非内部排列。

entries.definition: Relating to the microscopic study of tissues. It is a level below gross anatomy, so it is not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 与组织的显微研究有关；它比大体解剖低一个层次，因此并非同义词。

entries.definition: Relating to how the body works. It contrasts with anatomical, which concerns what the parts are and where they sit.
entries.definitionCN: 与身体如何运作有关；它与 anatomical 相对，后者关心部件是什么、位于何处。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: anatomy + -ical: belonging to the cutting-up science or to the structure it reveals.
normal.cn: anatomy + -ical：属于「切开之学」，或属于它揭示的结构。

normal.en: The family runs anatomy, anatomical, anatomically, anatomist, anatomize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 anatomy、anatomical、anatomically、anatomist、anatomize。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the use: anatomical structure, anatomical position, anatomical model, anatomical variation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：解剖结构、解剖学姿势、解剖模型、解剖变异。

normal.en: anatomical is about parts; physiological is about functions.
normal.cn: anatomical 讲部件，physiological 讲功能。

normal.en: atom carries the same root with a negative prefix: not cuttable, against cut up.
normal.cn: atom 是同一词根加否定前缀：不可切，与切开相对。

abstract.en: Picture a numbered diagram where every line points to one small part.
abstract.cn: 想象一张编号示意图，每条引线都指向一个小部件。

abstract.en: Picture a machine manual that begins by naming every screw before explaining what it does.
abstract.cn: 想象一本机器手册，先给每颗螺丝命名，再解释它的作用。

abstract.en: Picture two animals that look alike until you compare their skeletons.
abstract.cn: 想象两只动物外表相似，直到比较骨架才发现不同。

examples.en: The two species differ in anatomical detail but not in behaviour.
examples.cn: 这两个物种在解剖细节上不同，行为上却没有差别。

examples.en: The surgeon studied the anatomical charts before the operation.
examples.cn: 手术前外科医生仔细看了解剖图。

examples.en: An anatomically modern skeleton was found in the cave.
examples.cn: 洞穴中发现了一具结构上属于现代人的骨架。

dict_mnemonic.text: anatomy（解剖）+ ical（……的）→ 解剖学的、身体结构的

root: 希腊 ana-「向上、遍及」+ temnein「切」→ anatomē「切开」→ 拉丁 anatomia → 英语 anatomy → anatomical。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses attach the adjective to different things: a science, a body's parts, a non-biological structure, a teaching model, a standard position, a visible difference, a course and a method of analysis.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把这个形容词挂到不同对象上：一门学科、身体的部件、非生物结构、教学模型、标准姿势、可见差异、课程与分析方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a labelled chart where every line points to one part of a body.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张带标签的图，每条引线都指向身体的一个部件。

branches.en: THE DISCIPLINE AND ITS TEACHING: the adjective marks research literature and classroom materials alike.
branches.cn: 学科及其教学：这个形容词既可标出研究文献，也可标出课堂教材。

branches.en: STRUCTURE MADE VISIBLE: parts and their arrangement, including differences that can be seen before any test.
branches.cn: 可见的结构：部件及其排列，包括无需检验就能看出的差异。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: institutions and texts can be treated as bodies to be taken apart.
branches.cn: 比喻：机构与文本都可被当作身体来拆解。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: a model or chart is anatomical because of the use it serves.
branches.cn: 物件：模型或挂图之所以是 anatomical 的，是因为它服务的用途。

branches.en: THE CONVENTION: a standard position makes left and right describable at all.
branches.cn: 约定：标准姿势才使「左」「右」变得可以描述。

intro.en: Anatomical is a Greek compound with an English adjective ending: a prefix of opening, the verb 'to cut', the noun -y, and the adjective suffix -ical.
intro.cn: anatomical 是希腊复合词加英语形容词词尾：表示打开的前缀、动词「切」、名词词尾 -y，以及形容词后缀 -ical。

latinIntro.en: Latin anatomia supplies anatomy, anatomical, anatomically, anatomist and anatomize. The Greek root tom- also yields atom, tome, epitome and the surgical -ectomy names.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 anatomia 衍生 anatomy、anatomical、anatomically、anatomist、anatomize；希腊词根 tom- 还给出 atom、tome、epitome 以及外科的 -ectomy 类名称。

items.meaning: of body structure or of anatomy
items.example: The anatomical atlas has forty plates.
items.exampleCN: 这本解剖图谱有四十幅图版。

items.example: Anatomy was taught with drawings before it was taught with bodies.
items.exampleCN: 解剖学先以图画教授，后来才用实体。

items.example: The two hands are anatomically symmetrical.
items.exampleCN: 两只手在结构上是对称的。

items.example: The anatomist corrected the older drawing.
items.exampleCN: 这位解剖学家修正了那幅旧图。

items.example: She anatomized the contract clause by clause.
items.exampleCN: 她把合同逐条剖析了一遍。

items.example: The word atom once meant 'uncuttable'.
items.exampleCN: atom 一词原意是「不可切的」。

items.example: A single tome filled the shelf.
items.exampleCN: 一卷书就占满了书架。

items.meaning: a cutting short; a perfect example
items.example: The village is the epitome of calm.
items.exampleCN: 这个村庄是宁静的典型。

definition_zh: 联盟；联合政府；合并；军事联盟；商业联盟；临时性结合
definition_en: a temporary alliance of parties, groups or states formed to act together for a shared purpose
core_image: 几张桌子拼成一张长桌，各家的名牌并排摆着，散会时又各自搬回原处
scene: 选后第二天，几间办公室的门牌还挂着各自的名称，桌上却已摊开同一份组阁名单。 The two smaller groups formed a coalition after the election.
sceneCN: 选后第二天，几间办公室的门牌还挂着各自的名称，桌上却已摊开同一份组阁名单；句中的这个词指「若干团体为共同目的结成的联盟」（第 1 个义项：政党之间为组成政府或共同行动而订立的合作安排）。图中可辨识物件：拼起的长桌、各家名牌、组阁名单、铅笔、门口的名牌。

pos.zh: 联盟；联合政府；合并体（可数）
（作定语）联盟的；联合的

senses.title: An alliance of parties
senses.definition: an arrangement in which two or more parties agree to act together, often to command a majority
senses.definitionCN: 两个或多个政党约定共同行动、常为取得多数席位的安排
senses.example: The two parties signed a coalition after weeks of talks.
senses.exampleCN: 两党经过数周谈判后签署了联盟协议。
senses.why: Separate groups grow together for one purpose: each keeps its own name while acting as one body.
senses.whyCN: 各自独立的团体为同一个目的长到一起：各自保留名号，却作为一个整体行动。

senses.title: A coalition government
senses.definition: a government formed by more than one party sharing ministries and responsibility
senses.definitionCN: 由不止一个政党共同组成、分享各部职位与责任的政府
senses.example: The coalition government lasted only eighteen months.
senses.exampleCN: 这个联合政府只维持了十八个月。
senses.why: When no party wins a majority, the alliance itself must take on the shape of a government.
senses.whyCN: 当没有一个政党赢得多数时，联盟本身就必须长成政府的形状。

senses.title: An alliance of states or bodies
senses.titleCN: 国家或组织之间的联盟
senses.definition: a group of states, unions or organizations that agree to cooperate on a common aim
senses.definitionCN: 就共同目标约定合作的一群国家、团体或组织
senses.example: A coalition of coastal cities lobbied for cleaner shipping fuel.
senses.exampleCN: 一群沿海城市游说推行更清洁的船用燃料。
senses.why: The same logic works above the level of parties: separate members join for a shared aim.
senses.whyCN: 同一套逻辑在政党之上也成立：各自独立的成员为共同目标联合。

senses.title: The act of merging
senses.definition: the process by which separate parts grow or come together into one mass
senses.definitionCN: 各自分离的部分长合或聚成一个整体的过程
senses.example: The coalition of the two firms took effect in April.
senses.exampleCN: 两家公司的合并于四月生效。
senses.why: The word first names a physical growing together; the political alliance is that process applied to groups.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指物理上的长合；政治联盟就是把这一过程用在团体上。

senses.title: A military coalition
senses.definition: a group of armed forces from several countries fighting or training together
senses.definitionCN: 由若干国家的武装力量共同作战或共同训练形成的集团
senses.example: The military coalition flew joint patrols over the region.
senses.exampleCN: 军事联盟在该地区上空进行联合巡逻。
senses.why: Armies from separate states join under one command, keeping their own flags but sharing a plan.
senses.whyCN: 不同国家的军队归入同一指挥之下，各自保留旗帜，却共用一份计划。

senses.title: An advocacy or business alliance
senses.definition: a loose alliance of companies or campaigners formed to press one common demand
senses.definitionCN: 由公司或倡议者组成的松散联盟，为提出同一项诉求而行动
senses.example: A coalition of retailers asked for a delay in the new rules.
senses.exampleCN: 一群零售商组成的联盟要求推迟新规。
senses.why: Any group too small to be heard alone can grow together with others and speak once.
senses.whyCN: 任何独自发声太小的团体，都可以与别人长到一起，只发一次声。

senses.title: A temporary combination
senses.definition: a union made for a limited task or period, expected to dissolve afterwards
senses.definitionCN: 为有限的任务或时段结成、预期事后会解散的联合
senses.example: Their coalition was temporary and ended with the single vote.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的联盟是临时的，随着那一次投票结束而终止。
senses.why: Growing together does not mean fusing for ever: the parts can separate once the shared aim is met.
senses.whyCN: 长到一起不等于永久融合：共同目标一旦达成，各部分仍可分开。

senses.title: Coalition politics as a practice
senses.definition: the everyday work of negotiating, sharing posts and holding an alliance together
senses.definitionCN: 谈判、分配职位并把联盟维系下去的日常工作
senses.example: Coalition politics rewards patience more than rhetoric.
senses.exampleCN: 联盟政治奖赏耐心，而不是辞令。
senses.why: Once an alliance exists, it becomes a practice: meetings, quotas and compromises rather than a single signature.
senses.whyCN: 联盟一旦存在，就变成一种实践：会议、配额与妥协，而不是一次签字。

intro.en: Coalition comes from Latin coalescere 'to grow together', built from co- 'together' and alescere 'to grow'. The political sense is a later English extension. The word's first appearance in English is not securely dated.
intro.cn: 这个词出自拉丁语中意为「长到一起」的动词，由意为「共同」的前缀与意为「生长」的词根构成。政治义是英语里后来的延伸。它在英语中首见的时间不能确证。

items.en: Alescere was an inceptive verb meaning 'to begin to grow'. It is related to alere 'to nourish' and to adultus 'grown up'.
items.cn: 这个拉丁动词是表示「开始生长」的起始动词，与意为「滋养」的动词及意为「已长成的」分词同族。

items.en: Co- 'together' plus alescere gave coalescere 'to grow together, to unite into one body'. The image is biological, not political.
items.cn: 意为「共同」的前缀加「生长」构成表示「长到一起、并成一个整体」的动词。这个画面是生物性的，不是政治的。

items.en: The past participle coalitus meant 'grown together'. From its stem the noun coalitio was formed.
items.cn: 过去分词意为「已经长到一起的」。名词形式正是从这个词干构成的。

items.en: French took the Latin noun as coalition and used it for a union of parties or groups. English borrowed the French form rather than the Latin one.
items.cn: 法语借入这个拉丁名词，用来指政党或团体的联合。英语借的是法语形式，而不是拉丁形式。

items.en: In English the word settled into political life during the eighteenth century, when ministries began to be built from several factions. The exact first use remains uncertain.
items.cn: 在英语里，这个词于十八世纪进入政治生活，当时内阁开始由若干派系拼组。确切的首见时间仍不确定。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word spread to military, business and campaign alliances, always keeping the idea of separate parts acting as one.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，这个词扩展到军事、商业与倡议联盟，始终保留「各自独立的部分作为一个整体行动」的意思。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin root of growing together; the second group gathers words for alliances of different strength and duration.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「长到一起」的词根；第二组汇集了强度与持续时间各不相同的联盟说法。

entries.definition: To grow together into one body. It names the process; the noun names the resulting alliance.
entries.definitionCN: 指长合成为一个整体。它指过程，名词则指长合之后形成的联盟。

entries.definition: The process of merging, often physical or chemical. It does not by itself mean a political deal.
entries.definitionCN: 指合并的过程，常是物理或化学过程。它本身不指政治交易。

entries.definition: In the process of growing together. It describes the state, not the finished group.
entries.definitionCN: 指正处于长合过程中的。它描述状态，而不是已经成形的团体。

entries.definition: Of or belonging to a coalition. It is the adjective built on the noun, not a separate alliance.
entries.definitionCN: 指属于联盟的。它是从名词构成的形容词，不是另一种联盟。

entries.definition: A union of groups or states, often sealed by a treaty and meant to last. A coalition is usually narrower and more temporary.
entries.definitionCN: 指团体或国家的联合，常以条约缔结、意在持久。联盟通常更窄，也更临时。

entries.definition: An association of states, clubs or people for a common cause. It often has a name and a membership list.
entries.definitionCN: 指为国家、俱乐部或人因共同事业结成的协会，常有名称与成员名单。

entries.definition: A group of states or members that votes as one. It stresses weight in a vote rather than a written deal.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为一个单位投票的一群国家或成员。它强调投票分量，而不是书面协议。

entries.definition: A joining of parts into one body, often permanent and sometimes losing separate identities.
entries.definitionCN: 指把各部分并成一个整体，常为永久，有时会失去各自的独立身份。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin picture of growing together, the derived family, and the fixed phrases of government and war.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语「长到一起」的画面、派生词族，以及政府与战争语境中的固定搭配。

normal.en: The prefix means 'together', the root means 'grow': the whole word is a growing together.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「共同」，词根意为「生长」：整个词就是「长到一起」。

normal.en: Separate parties keep their own names while growing into one government.
normal.cn: 各自独立的政党保留自己的名号，却长成一个政府。

normal.en: The family runs coalesce, coalescence, coalescent and coalitional.
normal.cn: 同族词包括合并、合并过程、合并中的与联盟的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: form a coalition, a coalition government, a military coalition.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：组成联盟、联合政府、军事联盟。

normal.en: Its weakness is built in: a coalition can break up as easily as it was formed.
normal.cn: 它的弱点写在构造里：联盟解散可以和组成一样容易。

abstract.en: Picture several pots of paint poured into one can: the colours touch but do not mix at once.
abstract.cn: 想象几罐颜料倒进同一个桶：颜色挨在一起，却没有立刻混匀。

abstract.en: A coalition is a shared table, not a shared identity; each name card stays on the table.
abstract.cn: 联盟是一张共用的桌子，而不是共用的身份；每张名牌始终摆在桌上。

abstract.en: It ends when the common purpose ends, which is why it is strong today and fragile tomorrow.
abstract.cn: 共同目标结束，它也就结束；所以它今天坚固，明天脆弱。

examples.en: Without a majority, the largest party had to build a coalition within a week.
examples.cn: 由于没有多数，最大党必须在一周内搭起一个联盟。

examples.en: The coalition broke apart over a single clause in the budget.
examples.cn: 这个联盟因为预算里的一条条款而瓦解。

examples.en: A coalition of universities shared the cost of the telescope.
examples.cn: 一个大学联盟分担了这台望远镜的费用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扣阿利申」——把几股人「扣」在一起，讲「阿」字顺，只有「利」害一致才「申」明组阁，正好是一个联盟

root: 拉丁 coalescere「长到一起」= co-（共同）+ alescere「生长」，过去分词 coalitus，名词 coalitio；同根词包括表示「合并」的动词、表示「合并过程」的名词与表示「正在合并」的形容词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all come from one biological picture: separate parts grow together, then keep separate names while acting as a single body for as long as the purpose lasts.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都出自同一个生物画面：各自分离的部分长到一起，随后保留各自的名号，只要目的还在，就作为一个整体行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: separate parts grow together, share a purpose, and can still come apart.
core.cn: 核心意象：各自独立的部分长到一起，共用一个目的，也仍可能重新分开。

branches.en: DEAL AND GOVERNMENT: first the parties agree, then that agreement puts on the shape of a cabinet.
branches.cn: 协议与政府：先是政党达成协议，随后这份协议长成内阁的形状。

branches.en: STATES AND ARMIES: the same union works among cities and among armed forces under one command.
branches.cn: 国家与军队：同一套联合也用于城市之间，以及归入同一指挥的武装力量之间。

branches.en: MERGE AND DISSOLVE: the act of growing together and the limited term that lets the parts separate again.
branches.cn: 合并与解散：长合的动作，以及允许各部分重新分开的有限期限。

branches.en: SMALL VOICES JOINED: shops or campaigners too quiet alone grow together and speak once.
branches.cn: 微弱的声音合起来：独自太轻的商家或倡议者长到一起，只发一次声。

branches.en: DAILY PRACTICE: keeping the alliance alive takes meetings, quotas and compromise, not one signature.
branches.cn: 日常实践：维系联盟靠会议、配额与妥协，而不是一次签字。

intro.en: Coalition is built from a Latin prefix, a Latin root and a Latin noun suffix, and the same pieces build a compact family.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个拉丁前缀、一个拉丁词根和一个拉丁名词后缀构成，同样的构件还构成一个紧凑的词族。

latinIntro.en: Co- 'together' supplies the prefix; alescere 'to grow' supplies the root; -itio, -itionem turns the participle into a noun of action.
latinIntro.cn: 意为「共同」的前缀提供第一段；意为「生长」的词根提供第二段；名词后缀把分词变成表示动作的名词。

items.structure: co- (Latin prefix, 'together, with'; variant con- before some consonants)
items.meaningCN: 共同；一起，语义偏移为「联合」
items.example: The prefix marks joint action in many verbs.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀在许多动词里标出共同行动。

items.example: The root is visible in adult and adolescent.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根在「成年」与「青春期的」里仍可看出。

items.meaningCN: 长合在一起，语义偏移为「合并、联合」
items.example: The two streams coalesce below the bridge.
items.exampleCN: 两条溪流在桥下汇合。

items.structure: coalesce + -ence (noun suffix of state or process)
items.meaningCN: 长合的过程，语义偏移为「融合、合并」
items.example: Coalescence of the droplets formed a single drop.
items.exampleCN: 小滴融合成了一个单滴。

items.meaningCN: 正在长合的，语义偏移为「合并中的」
items.example: The coalescent groups soon spoke with one voice.
items.exampleCN: 这些正在合并的团体很快用同一个声音说话。

items.structure: co- + alit- (from Latin coalitus 'grown together') + -ion (Latin noun suffix)
items.meaningCN: 长到一起的团体，语义偏移为「联盟、联合政府」
items.example: The coalition held its first meeting on Friday.
items.exampleCN: 该联盟在周五举行了第一次会议。

items.meaning: of or belonging to a coalition
items.meaningCN: 属于联盟的，语义偏移为「联盟的、联合的」
items.example: Coalitional discipline held for six months.
items.exampleCN: 联盟纪律维持了六个月。

items.meaning: in the act of growing together
items.meaningCN: 正在进行长合的，语义偏移为「合并中的」
items.example: The coalescing factions chose one chairman.
items.exampleCN: 正在合并的各派选出了一位主席。

definition_zh: 爱冒险的；大胆的；充满危险的
definition_en: eager to try new and risky things, or full of risk and excitement
core_image: 背包里塞着绳索，眼睛却盯着没有足迹的方向
scene: 山谷入口的木牌上写着禁止通行，一个年轻人却已经在解背包的扣子。 An adventurous hiker ignored the sign and took the old goat path.
sceneCN: 这里 adventurous 是「爱冒险的」（第 1 个义项：乐于尝试新鲜而带风险之事的）；句意为一名爱冒险的徒步者无视告示，走上了那条旧羊道。图中可辨识的物件：木牌、背包、绳索。

pos.zh: 爱冒险的；大胆的；充满危险的

derivatives.zh: 本形容词的名词基础，义为「冒险；奇遇」
由 adventurous 加 -ly 构成，义为「冒险地；大胆地」
由 adventurer 的词干加 -ism 构成，义为「冒险主义」，多含贬义

senses.title: Eager for new and risky experience
senses.definition: describing a person who actively seeks novelty and risk
senses.definitionCN: 形容主动寻求新奇与风险的人
senses.example: She was adventurous enough to move abroad with no job lined up.
senses.exampleCN: 她够爱冒险，没找好工作就搬到了国外。
senses.why: The -ous ending turns adventure into a trait, so the adjective describes a person's appetite rather than an event.
senses.whyCN: -ous 词尾把 adventure 变成一种特质，所以这个形容词描述的是人的胃口，而不是事件。

senses.title: Full of risk and excitement
senses.definition: describing a journey or undertaking that contains real danger
senses.definitionCN: 形容包含真实危险的旅程或行动
senses.example: The descent through the gorge was an adventurous route.
senses.exampleCN: 穿过峡谷下行的路线充满冒险。
senses.why: The same adjective can look outward at the journey, where the risk belongs to the road rather than to the person.
senses.whyCN: 同一个形容词也可以朝外看旅程，此时风险属于道路，而不属于人。

senses.title: Unconventional in method
senses.definition: describing an approach that departs from the safe or standard way
senses.definitionCN: 形容偏离稳妥或标准做法的办法
senses.example: The director took an adventurous approach to a familiar play.
senses.exampleCN: 导演对一出熟悉的戏采取了大刀阔斧的处理。
senses.why: Departing from the standard route is the mental version of leaving the marked path.
senses.whyCN: 偏离标准路线，是「离开标记好的小路」在思维层面的版本。

senses.title: Bold in taste
senses.definition: describing choices in food, fashion or design that risk being disliked
senses.definitionCN: 形容在饮食、时装或设计上敢于冒被厌恶之险的选择
senses.example: The menu is adventurous, with fermented fruit and raw fish.
senses.exampleCN: 这份菜单很大胆，有发酵水果和生鱼。
senses.why: Taste is a small arena of risk, where trying the strange dish is the everyday form of adventure.
senses.whyCN: 口味是一个小型的风险场，尝试怪菜就是冒险的日常形式。

senses.title: Risky in financial terms
senses.definition: describing an investment or portfolio that accepts high risk for high return
senses.definitionCN: 形容为求高回报而接受高风险的投资或组合
senses.example: Analysts warned that the fund was too adventurous for retirees.
senses.exampleCN: 分析师警告说，这只基金对退休者来说过于激进。
senses.why: Finance reuses the travel metaphor: a portfolio can take an unmarked route too.
senses.whyCN: 金融沿用旅行的比喻：一份投资组合也可以走没有标记的路。

senses.title: Marvellous in the manner of romance
senses.definition: in literary description, full of marvels and unlikely turns
senses.definitionCN: 在文学描写中，充满奇观与不大可能的转折
senses.example: The memoir reads like an adventurous romance.
senses.exampleCN: 这本回忆录读起来像一部传奇冒险故事。
senses.why: Romance is the genre where adventure was first a literary shape, and the adjective still carries that glow.
senses.whyCN: 传奇是 adventure 最初获得文学形状的体裁，这个形容词仍带着那层光。

senses.title: Physically bold, of a child
senses.definition: describing a child who climbs, explores and tests limits
senses.definitionCN: 形容爱攀爬、爱探索、不断试探界限的孩子
senses.example: An adventurous toddler will find every unlocked door.
senses.exampleCN: 一个胆大的幼儿会找到每一扇没锁的门。
senses.why: The trait appears early, before any journey, as a body testing the edges of a room.
senses.whyCN: 这种特质很早就出现，还在任何远行之前，表现为一具身体在试探房间的边缘。

senses.title: Recklessly bold, with disapproval
senses.definition: used with disapproval of boldness that ignores sensible limits
senses.definitionCN: 带不赞同地形容无视合理界限的胆大
senses.example: Critics called the plan adventurous rather than innovative.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者称这个计划是鲁莽，而不是创新。
senses.why: A trait praised in one context is blamed in another, so the adjective can slide from courage to recklessness.
senses.whyCN: 同一种特质在此处受赞、在彼处受责，所以这个形容词能从勇气滑向鲁莽。

intro.en: Adventurous is adventure plus -ous; the noun goes back through Old French aventure to Latin adventura, things about to happen.
intro.cn: adventurous 是 adventure 加 -ous；名词经古法语 aventure 上溯到拉丁语 adventura「即将发生之事」。

items.en: Venire meant to come, the root shared by venue, avenue and event.
items.cn: venire 意为「来」，venue、avenue 与 event 共享这个词根。

items.en: The future participle adventura named what is about to happen, a word of open endings.
items.cn: 将来分词 adventura 命名「将要发生的事」，是一个结局未定的词。

items.en: Aventure meant chance or a risky enterprise, and it carried both into English.
items.cn: aventure 意为「机缘」或「风险功业」，并把两者一并带进英语。

items.en: French formed the adjective aventureux, meaning given to risk, and English followed with its own -ous form.
items.cn: 法语构成形容词 aventureux，意为「爱冒险的」，英语随后用自己的 -ous 形式跟上。

items.en: The English adjective settles in the sixteenth century, first describing travellers and tales.
items.cn: 英语形容词在十六世纪稳定下来，最早用于描述旅行者与故事。

items.en: Modern use extends the adjective to cuisine, finance and child behaviour, keeping the same risk at its centre.
items.cn: 现代用法把这个形容词扩展到饮食、金融与儿童行为，中心始终是同一份风险。

note.en: The look-alike group is the adventure family; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of boldness, which differ in whether the risk is physical, social or merely stylistic.
note.cn: 形近组是 adventure 词族；近义组收表示胆大的形容词，差别在于风险是身体上的、社交上的，还是仅仅风格上的。

entries.definition: The noun this adjective describes.
entries.definitionCN: 这个形容词所描述的名词。

entries.definition: The person, often with a hint that the risk is taken for gain.
entries.definitionCN: 冒险的人，常暗示其冒险带有图利目的。

entries.definition: A rarer synonym built with -some instead of -ous.
entries.definitionCN: 用 -some 而非 -ous 构成的较少见同义词。

entries.definition: Willing to take great risks, stressing courage in the moment rather than a lasting trait.
entries.definitionCN: 愿意承担大风险，强调当下的勇气而非持久的特质。

entries.definition: Confident and unafraid, a broader word that need not involve physical danger.
entries.definitionCN: 自信而不惧，范围更广，不一定涉及身体危险。

entries.definition: Inclined to take chances, a formal and slightly old-fashioned synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 倾向于碰运气，正式而略显过时的同义词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the aventure stem, the -ous ending and the collocations the adjective actually forms.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用 aventure 词干、-ous 词尾，以及这个形容词实际构成的搭配。

normal.en: Adventure plus -ous makes a trait: a person who carries adventure inside.
normal.cn: adventure 加 -ous 造出一种特质：把冒险装在身体里的人。

normal.en: The same adjective describes the traveller and the road, the appetite and the danger.
normal.cn: 同一个形容词既描述旅行者，也描述道路；既描述胃口，也描述危险。

normal.en: Be adventurous with food is the everyday invitation to try something strange.
normal.cn: be adventurous with food 是邀请人尝试怪东西的日常说法。

normal.en: The comparatives are more and most adventurous, never adventurouer.
normal.cn: 比较级与最高级是 more 与 most adventurous，绝不用 adventurouer。

normal.en: Adventurism is the noun for the disapproved version, risk taken for its own sake.
normal.cn: adventurism 是带贬义的名词，指为冒险而冒险。

abstract.en: Picture a boot print just outside the rope that marks the safe path.
abstract.cn: 想象安全小路的绳索之外，正好有一个靴印。

abstract.en: The word lives on a sliding scale: curiosity at one end, recklessness at the other.
abstract.cn: 这个词活在一条滑动刻度上：一端是好奇，另一端是鲁莽。

abstract.en: Small risks rehearse big ones, which is why a child and a fund manager can share the word.
abstract.cn: 小风险是巨大风险的排练，所以一个孩子和一位基金经理能共用这个词。

examples.en: The more adventurous students chose the mountain route.
examples.cn: 更爱冒险的学生选择了山路。

examples.en: An adventurous menu can frighten a tired traveller.
examples.cn: 一份大胆的菜单会吓到疲惫的旅人。

examples.en: She was adventurous with colour, and her paintings showed it.
examples.cn: 她用色大胆，她的画作看得出这一点。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德文彻勒斯」——彻勒斯敢往没路的地方走：爱冒险的

root: adventure（冒险，源自拉丁 adventura「即将发生之事」）+ 形容词词尾 -ous → adventurous，义为爱冒险的、充满危险的。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of adventurous all measure appetite for risk: a person, a journey, a method, a taste, a portfolio, a romance, a child and a criticised boldness.
sensesIntro.cn: adventurous 的八个义项都在衡量对风险的胃口：一个人、一段旅程、一种方法、一种口味、一份投资、一部传奇、一个孩子，以及一种受批评的胆大。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pack of rope carried toward ground with no footprints.
core.cn: 核心意象：背着绳索，走向没有足迹的地面。

branches.en: THE PERSON LINE: the appetite for risk shows first in a body, then in a character.
branches.cn: 人物线：对风险的胃口先在身体上显露，然后在性格上显露。

branches.en: THE JOURNEY LINE: the road and the romance both carry the danger outside the traveller.
branches.cn: 旅程线：道路与传奇都把危险放在旅行者之外。

branches.en: THE METHOD LINE: leaving the marked path becomes leaving the standard method.
branches.cn: 方法线：离开标记好的小路，变成离开标准的做法。

branches.en: THE TASTE LINE: food and money are small arenas where the same risk is tried.
branches.cn: 口味线：饮食与金钱是同一份风险被尝试的小型场地。

branches.en: THE LIMIT LINE: the same boldness is praised or blamed depending on who pays for it.
branches.cn: 界限线：同一份胆大是受赞还是受责，取决于谁为它买单。

intro.en: Adventurous is aventure plus -ous; the noun behind it is a Latin future participle, and English adds -ly and -ism to the same stem.
intro.cn: adventurous 是 aventure 加 -ous；其后的名词是拉丁将来分词，英语又在同一词干上加 -ly 与 -ism。

latinIntro.en: Venire, advenire and adventura are attested in Latin; the French adjective aventureux is attested too, so only the earliest link is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: venire、advenire 与 adventura 在拉丁语中有文献；法语形容词 aventureux 也有文献，只有最早的连接属于构拟。

items.example: It brought the noun into English.
items.exampleCN: 它把这个名词带进英语。

items.example: It closes adventure.
items.exampleCN: 它收束 adventure。

items.example: It forms adventurous.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 adventurous。

items.example: It forms adventurously.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 adventurously。

items.example: It forms adventurism.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 adventurism。

items.example: It forms the rare adventuresome.
items.exampleCN: 它构成少见的 adventuresome。

definition_zh: 毕业；毕业典礼；刻度划分
definition_en: the act or ceremony of completing a course of study, or the marking of a scale into regular degrees
core_image: 一顶学位帽放在折叠的证书旁，礼堂椅子排成整齐的方阵
scene: 礼堂里念到名字的人依次上台，接过证书后把帽穗拨到另一边。 Her graduation was the first in the family.
sceneCN: 礼堂里被念到名字的人依次上台，接过证书后把帽穗拨到另一边；句中的 graduation 指「完成学业的毕业典礼」（第 2 个义项：授予学位的仪式）。图中可辨识物件：学位帽、证书、礼堂座椅、帽穗。

pos.zh: 毕业；毕业典礼；刻度划分

senses.title: Completing a course of study
senses.definition: the act of finishing a course or a degree and being formally recognised
senses.definitionCN: 完成课程或学位并获得正式承认的行为
senses.example: Graduation from the programme takes two years.
senses.exampleCN: 从这个项目毕业需要两年。
senses.why: the Latin verb meant 'to take a degree', built on gradus 'step', so finishing study is pictured as reaching the top step of a stair.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「取得学位」，由 gradus「台阶」构成，因此完成学业被想象成走到楼梯的最高一级。

senses.title: The ceremony itself
senses.definition: the formal event at which degrees or diplomas are conferred
senses.definitionCN: 正式授予学位或证书的仪式
senses.example: Her graduation was the first in the family.
senses.exampleCN: 她的毕业典礼是家里第一次。
senses.why: the event sense grew from the act: once many people finish at once, the finishing needs a hall, a stage and a name read aloud.
senses.whyCN: 仪式义由行为义生长而来：一旦许多人同时完成，这份完成就需要礼堂、舞台与被念出的名字。

senses.title: Marks on a measuring scale
senses.definition: the set of marks that divide a scale into measured intervals
senses.definitionCN: 把量具分成等距区间的那些刻线
senses.example: The thermometer's graduation is etched in fine lines.
senses.exampleCN: 这支温度计的刻度以细线蚀刻。
senses.why: the physical sense is the oldest literal one: a scale is divided into steps, and each step is a degree.
senses.whyCN: 这个物理义是最早的字面义：量具被分成台阶，每一级就是一个度。

senses.title: A graduation rate
senses.definition: the proportion of students who finish a programme within a stated time
senses.definitionCN: 在规定时间内完成项目的学生比例
senses.example: The district reports a graduation rate above ninety percent.
senses.exampleCN: 该学区报告的毕业率超过九成。
senses.why: statistics turned an event into a ratio, so the word now measures a system rather than a person.
senses.whyCN: 统计学把事件变成比率，于是这个词衡量的是系统而非个人。

senses.title: Graduation requirements
senses.definition: the courses, credits and conditions a student must satisfy to finish
senses.definitionCN: 学生完成学业必须满足的课程、学分与条件
senses.example: The new graduation requirements include a research project.
senses.exampleCN: 新的毕业要求包含一个研究项目。
senses.why: requirements define the steps: if graduation is a stair, then each requirement is one tread that must be stood on.
senses.whyCN: 要求把台阶定义清楚：若毕业是楼梯，那么每一项要求都是必须踩上的一级。

senses.title: The graduating class
senses.definition: the group of students finishing in a given year, taken as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 在某一年完成学业、被视作整体的那群学生
senses.example: The graduating class planted a tree by the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 本届毕业生在门旁种了一棵树。
senses.why: the word attaches to a group as well as an act, because the people who finish together acquire a shared name.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既可指行为也可指群体，因为一同完成的人获得了一个共同的名字。

senses.title: A gradual transition, in old use
senses.definition: a passing from one state to another by small steps
senses.definitionCN: 以细小步伐从一种状态转入另一种状态
senses.example: Old texts describe the graduation of dusk into dark.
senses.exampleCN: 旧文献描写黄昏逐渐转入黑暗。
senses.why: the step image produced an older abstract sense: anything that changes by degrees undergoes a graduation.
senses.whyCN: 台阶意象产生了一个更旧的抽象义：凡按度变化者都经历一次「graduation」。

senses.title: Calibrating an instrument
senses.definition: the act of marking an instrument into regular degrees for measurement
senses.definitionCN: 把仪器划成规则度数以便测量的动作
senses.example: The technician finished the graduation of the new gauge.
senses.exampleCN: 技师完成了新量规的刻度标定。
senses.why: the technical sense keeps the verb alive: to graduate a vessel is to give it steps that can be read.
senses.whyCN: 技术义让动词用法保持活力：给容器「分度」，就是给它可读的台阶。

intro.en: Graduation comes from Latin graduatio, built on graduari 'to take a degree', from gradus 'step, degree'. The word entered English in the fifteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: graduation 来自拉丁 graduatio，由 graduari「取得学位」构成，后者出自 gradus「台阶、度数」。这个词于十五世纪进入英语。年代为约数。

items.en: Gradus meant 'step, stride, degree'. A stair and a scale share the word because both are measured in steps.
items.cn: gradus 意为「台阶、步伐、度数」。楼梯与量具共享这个词，因为两者都以台阶计量。

items.en: Gradi meant 'to walk, to step'. The verb behind gradus pictures movement foot by foot.
items.cn: gradi 意为「行走、迈步」，是 gradus 背后的动词，意象是一步一步地移动。

items.en: Graduari meant 'to take a degree, to be advanced step by step', used of students who had climbed the required steps.
items.cn: graduari 意为「取得学位、逐级晋升」，用于那些已爬完所需台阶的学生。

items.en: Graduatio named the act of conferring a degree, and the English noun kept that sense when it was borrowed.
items.cn: graduatio 指授予学位的行为，英语借入时保留了这一意义。

items.en: By the eighteenth century the noun also named the ceremony, and the older measuring sense continued in instruments, where a scale is divided into graduations.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，这个名词也指仪式；更早的测量义则在仪器中延续，量具被分成一道道刻度。

items.en: The deeper origin of gradus and gradi is uncertain; the usual link to a root meaning 'to step, go' is reconstructed. The spread from the degree sense to the scale sense is attested but not dated precisely.
items.cn: gradus 与 gradi 的更早来源不确定；通常所说的、与表示「迈步、行走」的词根的联系属重构形式。「学位」义向「刻度」义的扩展有书证，但确切年代不明。

note.en: Group one holds the step-root family and the words that look closest; group two holds the events and documents that mark the same end of study.
note.cn: 第一组是「台阶」词根的词族与最形近的词；第二组是标记同一学业终点的仪式与文件。

entries.definition: The person who has finished, or the verb of finishing; graduation is the act or the ceremony.
entries.definitionCN: 指已完成的人或完成的动作；graduation 是行为或仪式。

entries.definition: Moving by small degrees; it shares the step image but has nothing to do with finishing school.
entries.definitionCN: 指按小度数变化；共享台阶意象，却与完成学业无关。

entries.definition: In small steps, the adverb of gradual rather than of graduation.
entries.definitionCN: 指以小步伐地，是 gradual 的副词而非 graduation 的。

entries.definition: A series of stages or shades; closer to the scale sense than to the ceremony.
entries.definitionCN: 指一连串阶段或层次；比仪式义更接近刻度义。

entries.definition: The American name for the ceremony, literally a beginning, stressing the start rather than the finish.
entries.definitionCN: 美式对毕业典礼的称呼，字面是「开始」，强调开端而非结束。

entries.definition: A formal assembly, often for conferring degrees; it names the gathering, not the completion.
entries.definitionCN: 指正式集会，常用于授学位；命名的是聚会而非完成。

entries.definition: The act of certifying a qualification; graduation is the finishing, certification the documentation.
entries.definitionCN: 指认证资格的行为；graduation 是完成，certification 是出具文件。

entries.definition: British usage for finishing secondary school, without the ceremony or degree sense.
entries.definitionCN: 英式说法，指读完中学，不含仪式或学位义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations here are the real step image, the real Latin verb for taking a degree, and the real modern statistics.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想取自真实的台阶意象、真实的「取得学位」拉丁动词，以及真实的现代统计用法。

normal.en: gradus 'step': a degree is a step on a stair.
normal.cn: gradus「台阶」：一个学位就是楼梯上的一级。

normal.en: graduari 'to take a degree': the student has climbed the required steps.
normal.cn: graduari「取得学位」：学生已爬完所需台阶。

normal.en: The family runs graduate, gradual, gradually, gradation.
normal.cn: 词族包括 graduate、gradual、gradually、gradation。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the event: graduation ceremony, graduation day, graduation gown.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出事件：毕业典礼、毕业日、毕业袍。

normal.en: The scale sense survives on instruments: a thermometer has graduations.
normal.cn: 刻度义留在仪器上：温度计有一道道刻度。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase whose top step is a stage with a name being read aloud.
abstract.cn: 想象一座楼梯，最高一级是舞台，上面正念出一个名字。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler and a diploma lying side by side, both divided into degrees.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺与一张文凭并排放着，两者都被分成度数。

abstract.en: Picture a class planting a tree that will be taller than them next time.
abstract.cn: 想象一个班级种下一棵树，下次相见时它会比他们更高。

examples.en: Graduation requirements changed after the curriculum review.
examples.cn: 课程复审后，毕业要求发生了变化。

examples.en: The graduation rate rose for the third year running.
examples.cn: 毕业率连续第三年上升。

examples.en: He missed his sister's graduation because of the storm.
examples.cn: 因为暴风雨，他错过了姐姐的毕业典礼。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「grad（台阶）」——一级一级走完，走到最高那级 → 毕业、毕业典礼

root: 拉丁 gradus「台阶、度数」（源自 gradi「迈步」）→ graduari「取得学位」→ graduatio → 英语 graduation；gradus 与 gradi 的更早来源不确定，与「迈步」词根的联系属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses climb one stair: study is finished step by step, the finishing becomes a ceremony, the steps become marks on a scale, then a rate, a set of requirements, a class, an older gradual change and a technical calibration.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项爬同一座楼梯：学业被逐级完成，完成变成仪式，台阶随后变成量具上的刻度、毕业率、一组要求、一个班级、一种旧的渐变，以及技术上的标定。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a staircase whose top step is a stage, and whose treads are also etched on a measuring instrument.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座楼梯，最高一级是舞台，而它的各级踏步同时也蚀刻在一件量具上。

branches.en: THE CLIMB: finishing is reaching the top, and requirements are the treads that must be stood on.
branches.cn: 攀爬：完成即登顶，要求则是必须踩上的踏步。

branches.en: THE GATHERING: a ceremony and a class give the private climb a public shape.
branches.cn: 聚集：仪式与班级给私人的攀爬一个公开的形状。

branches.en: THE SCALE: a stair and a gauge are both divided into degrees, one for climbing and one for reading.
branches.cn: 刻度：楼梯与量具都被分成度数，一个供攀爬，一个供读数。

branches.en: THE RATIO: statistics turns a personal arrival into a system's percentage.
branches.cn: 比率：统计学把个人的到达变成系统的百分比。

branches.en: OLD GRADATION: anything that changes by small steps undergoes a graduation.
branches.cn: 旧的渐变义：凡按小步变化者都经历一次「graduation」。

intro.en: The word is a Latin root plus two suffixes, and the same pieces build the whole graduate family and the scale words beside it.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁词根加两个后缀构成，同一批部件造出整个 graduate 词族及其旁边的刻度词。

latinIntro.en: Gradus and gradi supply the step; graduari and graduatio supply the degree-taking; the English noun keeps both the ceremony and the scale.
latinIntro.cn: gradus 与 gradi 提供「台阶」；graduari 与 graduatio 提供「取得学位」；英语名词同时保留仪式与刻度两义。

items.example: Gradus is the shared root.
items.exampleCN: gradus 是共享词根。

items.example: Gradi is the verb behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: gradi 是名词背后的动词。

items.example: Graduari names the climb's end.
items.exampleCN: graduari 指攀爬的终点。

items.example: Graduatio became English graduation.
items.exampleCN: graduatio 变成英语 graduation。

items.example: The noun entered English in the fifteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词于十五世纪进入英语。

items.meaning: one who has taken a degree
items.example: The person and the verb share one form.
items.exampleCN: 人与动词共用一词形。

items.example: Gradual keeps the step image.
items.exampleCN: gradual 保留台阶意象。

items.example: Gradually is the adverb of gradual.
items.exampleCN: gradually 是 gradual 的副词。

items.example: Gradation is close to the scale sense.
items.exampleCN: gradation 接近刻度义。

definition_zh: 教师；（大学）讲师；教练，指导员；指导手册（旧义）
definition_en: a person who teaches a subject or trains people in a skill, especially in a practical or college setting
core_image: 副驾驶座上坐着一个人，脚边也有一副刹车，随时准备替学员踩下
scene: 驾校的副驾驶座上，一名教员脚边也有一副刹车，随时准备替学员踩下。 The instructor beside her kept a second brake within reach during the first lesson.
sceneCN: 这里 instructor 指「教授某项技能并在旁边纠正的教练或教员」（第 1 个义项：大学或训练机构中的教师）；句意为第一堂课上，坐在她旁边的教练脚边备着第二副刹车。可辨识物件：副驾驶座、副刹、方向盘、后视镜。

pos.zh: 教师；（大学）讲师；教练，指导员；指导手册（旧义）

senses.title: A college teacher
senses.definition: a teacher at a college or university, often below the rank of professor
senses.definitionCN: 学院或大学里的教师，职级通常低于教授
senses.example: The instructor taught two sections of introductory economics.
senses.exampleCN: 这位讲师教两个班的经济学入门。
senses.why: The agent noun simply names the person who performs the act of instructing.
senses.whyCN: 这个施事名词只是命名执行「教导」这一动作的人。

senses.title: A driving instructor
senses.definition: a person who teaches someone to drive and supervises practice on the road
senses.definitionCN: 教人驾驶并在路上监督练习的人
senses.example: The instructor beside her kept a second brake within reach.
senses.exampleCN: 坐在她旁边的教练脚边备着第二副刹车。
senses.why: A skill learned in a moving vehicle needs someone able to take control instantly.
senses.whyCN: 在行驶的车里学技能，必须有人在旁能立刻接管。

senses.title: A fitness instructor
senses.definition: a person who leads exercise sessions and corrects posture and technique
senses.definitionCN: 带领训练课并纠正姿势与技术的人
senses.example: The instructor adjusted the bar before the next set.
senses.exampleCN: 教练在下一组之前调整了杠铃。
senses.why: Bodies learn by correction, so the word follows the person who supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 身体靠纠正来学习，这个词因此跟着提供纠正的人走。

senses.title: A flight instructor
senses.definition: a licensed pilot who trains student pilots in the air and on the ground
senses.definitionCN: 在空中与地面训练学员飞行员的持照飞行员
senses.example: Her flight instructor signed off the solo before winter.
senses.exampleCN: 她的飞行教员在入冬前批准了单飞。
senses.why: The highest-stakes training keeps the same title, because the act of instructing does not change with altitude.
senses.whyCN: 风险最高的训练仍用同一称谓，因为教导这一行为不因高度而改变。

senses.title: A sports or outdoor instructor
senses.titleCN: 运动或户外项目的教练
senses.definition: a person who teaches skiing, swimming, climbing or a similar physical skill
senses.definitionCN: 教授滑雪、游泳、攀岩等身体技能的人
senses.example: The ski instructor took the beginners down the easiest slope.
senses.exampleCN: 滑雪教练带初学者走最容易的那条坡。
senses.why: Each sport keeps the general word rather than inventing a new title, since teaching method is shared.
senses.whyCN: 各项运动都沿用这个通称而不另造头衔，因为教学方法相通。

senses.title: A military instructor
senses.definition: a soldier whose duty is to drill recruits in weapons, tactics or discipline
senses.definitionCN: 负责训练新兵武器、战术或纪律的军人
senses.example: The drill instructor counted cadence on the parade ground.
senses.exampleCN: 操练教官在阅兵场上喊着步伐节拍。
senses.why: Armies were among the first institutions to make instruction a specialized role.
senses.whyCN: 军队是最早把「教导」变成专职角色的机构之一。

senses.title: A book that instructs
senses.definition: an older use of the word for a manual or guide that teaches its reader
senses.definitionCN: 较古的用法，指教导读者的手册或指南
senses.example: The eighteenth-century instructor sold better than the novel.
senses.exampleCN: 那本十八世纪的指南书比小说卖得好。
senses.why: Before teaching was a profession, the word could name the printed thing that did the teaching.
senses.whyCN: 在教学成为职业之前，这个词可以指承担教导的那本印刷物。

senses.title: The Latin sense of a preparer
senses.definition: the original sense of one who arranges or equips something for others
senses.definitionCN: 原义：为他人安排或配备某物的人
senses.example: In Latin the word described the person who fitted out a house or a campaign.
senses.exampleCN: 在拉丁语里，这个词指为房屋或战事做配备的人。
senses.why: The modern teacher and the old organizer share the idea of getting someone ready.
senses.whyCN: 现代教师与旧的筹备者共享「让某人准备好」这一要点。

intro.en: Instructor is the agent noun of the Latin verb instruere 'to equip, arrange, teach'; the personal ending -or marks the one who acts. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: instructor 是拉丁动词「装备、安排、教导」的施事名词，表示人的词尾标记行动者。年代均为约数。

items.en: Instruere combined 'into' with 'build' to mean 'build in, equip, prepare', and it already covered both equipment and teaching.
items.cn: 这个拉丁动词把「进入」与「建造」合起来，表示「搭入、装备、准备」，本就兼指装备与教导。

items.en: The suffix -or marked the person who carries out the action, as in doctor or victor, so instructor was the one who equipped or prepared.
items.cn: 后缀标记执行动作的人，如「医生」或「胜利者」，因此这个词指做配备或准备的人。

items.en: English adopted instructor for a teacher, first in religious and then in general education.
items.cn: 英语借入这个词指教师，先用于宗教教导，再扩展到一般教育。

items.en: In the twentieth century the title spread to driving, flying, skiing and fitness, where instruction is sold as a service.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，这一称谓扩展到驾驶、飞行、滑雪与健身，这些领域的教学成为一项服务。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest English use as a job title is not securely dated, and the rank of college instructor varies by country.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：作为职称的最早英语用法年代不确，且大学讲师职级在不同国家并不一致。

note.en: Group one holds agent nouns that look or sound close to instructor; group two holds the teaching titles it is measured against.
note.cn: 第一组是形或音与 instructor 接近的施事名词；第二组是拿来与它比较的教学职称。

entries.definition: From a Latin verb meaning 'to prick or urge on', so an instigator starts trouble rather than teaching anyone.
entries.definitionCN: 来自表示「刺、怂恿」的拉丁动词，因此它指挑起事端的人，而非教导者。

entries.definition: Built on the same equipping verb but with a noun suffix, so it names the tool that equips the work.
entries.definitionCN: 同出那个表示「配备」的动词，但带名词后缀，指为工作配备的工具。

entries.definition: The rare passive counterpart, the person being taught; instructor is the one doing the teaching.
entries.definitionCN: 罕用的被动对应词，指被教的人；instructor 是施教的一方。

entries.definition: One who builds; it shares the building root but has nothing to do with lessons.
entries.definitionCN: 建造者；共享「建造」词根，但与教学无关。

entries.definition: The general word for someone who teaches in a school; instructor is narrower and often practical or college-level.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指在学校教书的人；instructor 范围更窄，常指实务训练或大学层次。

entries.definition: Someone who drills a practical skill, especially in sport or industry; it stresses repetition more than explanation.
entries.definitionCN: 训练实务技能的人，尤用于体育或行业；它更强调重复而非讲解。

entries.definition: A college teaching post that usually involves formal lectures; instructor may involve smaller classes.
entries.definitionCN: 大学教职，通常以正式讲座授课；instructor 可能带小班课。

entries.definition: Someone who improves another person's performance, often one to one; the word is warmer than instructor.
entries.definitionCN: 提升他人表现的人，常为一对一；语气比 instructor 更亲和。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the agent suffix, the skill settings where the word is used, and the family it belongs to.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：施事后缀、这个词被使用的技能场景，以及它所属的词族。

normal.en: The ending means 'the one who does it', so instructor is simply the person who instructs.
normal.cn: 这个词尾意为「做此事的人」，所以 instructor 就是执行教导的人。

normal.en: The title travels with any skill that needs correction at close range: driving, flying, skiing, lifting.
normal.cn: 凡是需要近身纠正的技能，都带着这个称谓：驾驶、飞行、滑雪、举重。

normal.en: A college instructor usually teaches smaller sections than a professor and may not hold a permanent post.
normal.cn: 大学讲师通常比教授带更小的班，且可能没有终身职位。

normal.en: Its verb is instruct and its abstract noun is instruction; three forms, one act.
normal.cn: 它的动词表示「教导」，抽象名词表示「教学」；三个形式，同一个动作。

normal.en: If the word appears on a car or an aircraft, expect a second set of controls.
normal.cn: 若这个词出现在汽车或飞机上，就该想到还有第二套操纵装置。

abstract.en: Picture two pairs of hands on one steering wheel.
abstract.cn: 想象两双手同时放在一个方向盘上。

abstract.en: Picture a voice counting while another body learns the rhythm.
abstract.cn: 想象一个声音在数拍子，另一个身体在学节奏。

abstract.en: Picture a ladder held steady at the bottom while someone climbs.
abstract.cn: 想象有人往上爬时，梯子在底下被人扶稳。

examples.en: The instructor cancelled the lesson because of the storm.
examples.cn: 教练因暴风雨取消了课程。

examples.en: New instructors shadow a senior colleague for a term.
examples.cn: 新讲师要跟一位资深同事听课一个学期。

examples.en: The flight instructor logged forty hours with her student.
examples.cn: 飞行教员与学员一起记录了四十小时飞行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「引着搭的人」——把人引进门、搭起技能框架的人 → 教师、教练

root: 拉丁语「装备、安排、教导」这一动词的施事名词，词尾表示「做此事的人」；英语 instructor 指教师、讲师与教练。词根印欧来源属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all name one person: the one who stands beside a learner and builds the skill in. The setting changes from college to car, gym, aircraft, slope, parade ground and even an old printed guide.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都指同一种人：站在学习者旁边、把技能搭进去的那个人。场景从大学换到汽车、健身房、飞机、雪坡、操练场，甚至一本古老的印刷指南。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a steady hand beside a learner, ready to correct or take over.
core.cn: 核心意象：学习者身旁一只稳定的手，随时准备纠正或接管。

branches.en: THE BUILDER: the college teacher and the Latin preparer both get another person ready.
branches.cn: 搭建者：大学讲师与拉丁语里的筹备者，都在让别人准备好。

branches.en: THE SECOND BRAKE: a driving lesson needs someone able to stop the car at once.
branches.cn: 第二副刹车：驾驶课需要有人能立刻把车停下。

branches.en: THE CORRECTING BODY: gym and slope both teach through repeated physical correction.
branches.cn: 纠正身体：健身房与雪坡都靠反复的身体纠正来教。

branches.en: HIGH-STAKES DRILL: aircraft and parade ground keep the title because the risk is real.
branches.cn: 高风险操练：飞机与操练场保留这个称谓，因为风险确实存在。

branches.en: THE PAPER TEACHER: an old guidebook could carry the name when no person was present.
branches.cn: 纸上的教师：在没有真人在场时，旧指南书也能承担这个名字。

intro.en: Instructor is built from a verb plus the Latin personal suffix, and the same pieces recur in a cluster of English words.
intro.cn: instructor 由一个动词加拉丁语表示人的后缀构成，同样的部件在若干英语词中反复出现。

latinIntro.en: The verb means 'to equip or teach'; the suffix marks the doer. Adding other suffixes to the same stem yields instruction and instructional.
latinIntro.cn: 动词意为「装备或教导」；后缀标记行动者。同一词干加其他后缀，就得到「教学」与「教学的」。

items.example: The verb supplies both the act and the agent.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词同时提供动作与行动者。

items.example: The suffix turns the act into a person.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动作变成一个人。

items.example: The instructor corrected the grip.
items.exampleCN: 教练纠正了握法。

items.structure: instruct (English verb, back-formed from the noun)
items.example: She instructs a class of thirty.
items.exampleCN: 她教一个三十人的班。

items.example: The instructions were printed on one sheet.
items.exampleCN: 说明印在一张纸上。

items.example: Instructional materials were redesigned.
items.exampleCN: 教学材料被重新设计。

items.example: The mistake was instructive.
items.exampleCN: 这个错误很有教益。

items.example: The older form is now rarely used.
items.exampleCN: 这一旧形式今已罕用。

latinEntries.meaning: to equip; to arrange; to teach
